articles.title: This Soldier Kept a Diary in the Trenches of World War I. A Child Found It at the Dump Decades Later, Pierced by a Bullet and Stained With Blood

paras.en: The day the boy found the diary, he’d been scrounging for treasures at the local dump in Stourbridge, England. He and his friends had entered through a small opening at the bottom of a wire fence. Then they spotted something among the bottles and cans: a nearly four-inch-long volume with a green cover, its pages turning in the wind.
paras.zh: 男孩发现日记的那天，他正在英格兰斯托布里奇当地的垃圾场寻找宝藏。他和他的朋友们从铁丝网底部的一个小开口进入。然后他们在瓶子和罐子里发现了一些东西：一本近四英寸长的书，封面是绿色的，书页在风中翻动。

paras.en: The year was 1965, but the diary entries dated to 1918. Their author was a man named Corporal Claude Nuttall, who had served as an infantryman (or “Digger”) in the Australian Army during World War I. He met his wife, Violet Palfreyman, while recovering from an injury in an English hospital. Weeks after the wedding, he returned to the front.
paras.zh: 时间是 1965 年，但日记条目的日期却是 1918 年。日记的作者是一位名叫克劳德·纳托尔 (Claude Nuttall) 下士的男子，他曾在第一次世界大战期间在澳大利亚军队担任步兵（或“挖掘者”）。他在英国一家医院养伤时认识了他的妻子维奥莱特·帕尔弗里曼 (Violet Palfreyman)。婚礼几周后，他又回到了前线。

paras.en: Did Nuttall ever make it home? The boy wondered about the soldier’s fate, and the diary offered several ominous clues. The corner appeared to have been pierced by a bullet, and its pages were stained with blood. Nuttall’s last entry was dated August 10, 1918. The pages that followed were blank.
paras.zh: 纳托尔回家了吗？男孩想知道这名士兵的命运，而日记提供了一些不祥的线索。书页的一角似乎被子弹打穿了，书页上沾满了血迹。纳托尔的最后一篇文章日期为 1918 年 8 月 10 日。接下来的页面是空白的。

paras.en: “Heavy bombardment by our guns. Push still in progress,” he wrote. “Packed up ready to move forward again. Prisoners still coming back. Wrote to Violet.”
paras.zh: “我们的炮火猛烈轰炸。推进仍在进行中，”他写道。 “收拾好行李，准备再次前进。囚犯们还在回来。写信给维奥莱特。”

paras.en: The diary eventually made its way to Colin Reid, a former curator at the Dudley Museum and Art Gallery in England’s West Midlands, who spent decades researching the soldier’s story. The culmination of his efforts is the book The Digger’s Diary, which comes out this fall.
paras.zh: 这本日记最终落到了英格兰西米德兰兹达德利博物馆和艺术画廊的前馆长科林·里德手中，他花了几十年的时间研究这位士兵的故事。他的努力的顶峰是《挖掘者日记》一书，该书将于今年秋天出版。

paras.en: “At the start, I wanted to solve the mystery of Claude’s fate,” Reid tells Smithsonian magazine. “An emotional compulsion, I suppose. The fact that his diary was unfinished, bloodstained and had been punctured by a bullet compelled me to find out if he had survived and returned back to Violet.”
paras.zh: “一开始，我想解开克劳德命运之谜，”里德告诉史密森尼杂志。 “我想是一种情感上的冲动。他的日记尚未完成，血迹斑斑，还被子弹打穿，这一事实迫使我去查明他是否还活着并回到了维奥莱特身边。”

paras.en: The story of the diary’s discovery begins with the Stourbridge dump. The boy who found the volume was 12-year-old Alan Southall, who held onto it for three decades. In 1996, he showed up at the Dudley Museum asking for Reid, who was then working on a World War I exhibition. Southall pulled out the diary, which he’d carefully tucked inside a plastic bag, and asked whether the curator wanted to put it on display.
paras.zh: 这本日记的发现故事始于斯托布里奇垃圾场。发现这本书的男孩是 12 岁的艾伦·索索尔 (Alan Southall)，他持有这本书三十年了。 1996 年，他出现在达德利博物馆，询问当时正在筹备一次世界大战展览的里德。索撒尔拿出他小心翼翼地塞在塑料袋里的日记，询问策展人是否愿意将其展出。

paras.en: But Southall had other questions, too. In The Digger’s Diary, the curator recalls what his visitor told him: “For 30 years, I’ve wanted to know Corporal Nuttall’s fate. But I have never done anything about it, because I don’t think things ended well for him.”
paras.zh: 但索撒尔还有其他问题。在《挖掘者日记》中，馆长回忆起访客告诉他的话：“三十年来，我一直想知道纳托尔下士的命运。但我从未采取任何行动，因为我认为他的结局并不好。”

paras.en: The diary went on view in the museum’s exhibition, titled “The Great War.” But when the show closed, Reid kept thinking about the little book with the green cover. About a decade later, he decided to write a book of his own. The curator tracked down Southall, who let him borrow the diary.
paras.zh: 这本日记在博物馆的题为“伟大的战争”的展览中展出。但演出结束后，里德一直在想着那本绿色封面的小书。大约十年后，他决定写一本自己的书。馆长找到了索撒尔，索撒尔让他借了日记。

paras.en: Reid got to work, searching for any information he could find about the Australian soldier. “The more I learned, the more I wanted to learn,” he tells BBC News’ Aida Fofana and Sarah Julian. “Right from the very first moment that I held the diary, I had that real sense of connection with it. I was really hooked.”
paras.zh: 里德开始工作，寻找他能找到的有关这名澳大利亚士兵的任何信息。 “我学得越多，我就越想学，”他告诉 BBC 新闻的艾达·福法纳和莎拉·朱利安。 “从我拿起日记的那一刻起，我就与它产生了真正的联系。我真的被迷住了。”

paras.en: - On August 4, 1914, Australia entered World War I—the deadliest conflict in the country’s history.
paras.zh: - 1914 年 8 月 4 日，澳大利亚卷入第一次世界大战——这是该国历史上最致命的冲突。

paras.en: - According to the Australian War Memorial, the country’s population was fewer than five million at the time, and the death toll was more than 60,000.
paras.zh: - 根据澳大利亚战争纪念馆的数据，当时该国人口不足五百万，死亡人数超过六万。

paras.en: Born in 1895, Nuttall enlisted in the Australian Army’s 23rd Battalion in 1915, just after his 20th birthday. He traveled to the Western Front, where he fought the Germans. In his diary, he’d written that he’d been awarded a medal from George V; Reid had always wanted to know more about the courageous act that merited this reward. He found the answer in Nuttall’s military records: On his 21st birthday, in July 1916, the soldier had helped rescue injured soldiers from no man’s land, the perilous stretch of earth between opposing trenches.
paras.zh: 纳托尔出生于 1895 年，1915 年刚过 20 岁生日，就加入了澳大利亚陆军第 23 营。他前往西线，在那里与德国人作战。他在日记中写道，乔治五世授予他一枚勋章；里德一直想更多地了解值得这项奖励的勇敢行为。他在纳托尔的军事记录中找到了答案：1916 年 7 月，在他 21 岁生日那天，这名士兵帮助从无人区（敌对战壕之间的危险地带）营救受伤的士兵。

paras.en: Later that year, Nuttall was wounded in northern France. He was sent to a hospital in Stourbridge, where he met Palfreyman. The couple tied the knot in March 1918. “All excited,” the corporal wrote in his journal. “Married 12:30 p.m. All went well.” Five weeks later, he shipped out again. His service records show that he died on August 13, 1918, just three days after his final diary entry.
paras.zh: 同年晚些时候，纳托尔在法国北部受伤。他被送往斯托布里奇的一家医院，在那里他遇到了帕尔弗里曼。这对夫妇于 1918 年 3 月喜结良缘。这位下士在日记中写道：“非常兴奋。” “中午 12 点 30 分结婚。一切都很顺利。”五周后，他再次出境。他的服役记录显示，他于 1918 年 8 月 13 日去世，距他写下最后一篇日记仅三天。

paras.en: Thanks to Palfreyman’s relatives, Reid tracked down photos from the couple’s wedding. He also traveled to Cheltenham, the Australian suburb where the soldier grew up, to meet Nuttall’s family, as well as the French battlefields where Nuttall had fought and died.
paras.zh: 感谢帕尔弗里曼的亲戚，里德找到了这对夫妇婚礼的照片。他还前往这名士兵长大的澳大利亚郊区切尔滕纳姆，会见了纳托尔的家人，以及纳托尔曾战斗并牺牲的法国战场。

paras.en: In 2018, Reid and Southall met up with Arthur Thomas, the corporal’s nephew, to visit Nuttall’s grave in Harbonnieres, France. Together, they commemorated the 100th anniversary of his death. A few months later, the diary was returned to Nuttall’s family at a ceremony in Cheltenham.
paras.zh: 2018 年，里德和索撒尔与下士的侄子阿瑟·托马斯会面，参观了位于法国哈博尼埃的纳托尔墓。他们一起纪念他逝世100周年。几个月后，这本日记在切尔滕纳姆举行的仪式上被归还给纳托尔的家人。

paras.en: “I keep saying that the saddest part is that my mother, her two sisters and even Claude’s own mother know nothing of this. I can’t tell them what’s happened,” Thomas told the Dudley News’ Kelly Harris in 2018. “I have seen pictures of Claude’s wedding and Violet’s family that they would never have seen.”
paras.zh: “我一直说，最悲伤的是我的母亲、她的两个姐妹，甚至克劳德自己的母亲对此一无所知。我无法告诉他们发生了什么事，”托马斯在 2018 年告诉《达德利新闻》的凯莉·哈里斯。“我看到了克劳德的婚礼和维奥莱特一家的照片，他们永远不会看到。”

paras.en: But what about the bloodstains? Was the bullet that struck the diary fatal? “I’m afraid that I can’t reveal that to you,” Reid tells Smithsonian. “It’s a huge spoiler, and the emotional climax of the book—definitely embargoed.”
paras.zh: 但那些血迹呢？击中日记的子弹致命吗？ “恐怕我无法向您透露这一点，”里德告诉史密森尼。 “这是一个巨大的剧透，而这本书的情感高潮是绝对被禁止的。”

paras.en: He can, however, reveal Palfreyman’s fate, which was equally tragic. After Nuttall’s death, she married the owner of a carpet shop. The couple had a son named Eric and a baby girl who died soon after she was born. Palfreyman herself died from childbirth complications a few months later. “She and the child are buried together at Holy Trinity Church in Stourbridge,” Reid says, “barely 100 yards from the altar where she and Claude were married.”
paras.zh: 然而，他可以揭示帕尔弗里曼的命运，这同样是悲惨的。纳托尔去世后，她嫁给了一家地毯店的老板。这对夫妇有一个名叫埃里克的儿子和一个女儿，但女儿出生后不久就去世了。几个月后，帕尔弗里曼本人也因分娩并发症去世。 “她和孩子被埋葬在斯托布里奇的圣三一教堂，”里德说，“距离她和克劳德结婚的祭坛只有 100 码。”

paras.en: The Digger’s Diary, as the author writes in the preface, is a “tribute to the man I discovered: a forgotten hero, a soldier of quiet fortitude and extraordinary courage.” But it’s also a tribute to the woman Nuttall fell in love with—and to Reid’s own wife, who shares her name. The book begins with a dedication page, which reads simply “For Violet.”
paras.zh: 正如作者在序言中所写，《挖掘者日记》是“向我发现的那个人致敬：一位被遗忘的英雄，一位拥有平静坚韧和非凡勇气的士兵。”但这也是对纳托尔爱上的女人以及里德自己的妻子（与她同名）的致敬。这本书的开头是一个奉献页，上面简单地写着“献给紫罗兰”。

articles.title: On an Island Outside Paris, a Sprawling Contemporary Arts Center Aptly Called 'Large' Prepares to Open Its Doors

paras.en: Just outside of Paris, perched on an island in the Seine River, a massive, much-anticipated institution is preparing to open its doors. Spanning some 54,000 square feet, the capital region’s newest contemporary art center, which officially debuts this weekend, appears poised to live up to its name: Large.
paras.zh: 就在巴黎郊外塞纳河上的一座小岛上，一座备受期待的大型机构正准备开业。首都地区最新的当代艺术中心占地约 54,000 平方英尺，将于本周末正式开业，似乎名副其实：大型。

paras.en: The scale of the new development on Île Seguin is, in fact, large. Shining with a copper and aluminum exterior, Large is the centerpiece of a roughly 570,000-square-foot, $500-million development called Pointe des Arts, which includes a performing arts center, movie theater, sculpture garden, hotel, shopping district and more.
paras.zh: 事实上，塞甘岛新开发项目的规模非常大。 Large 拥有闪亮的铜铝外观，是占地约 570,000 平方英尺、耗资 5 亿美元的 Pointe des Arts 开发项目的核心，该开发项目包括表演艺术中心、电影院、雕塑花园、酒店、购物区等。

paras.en: Though Large’s name is also meant to evoke the French phrase “prendre le large,” which means “to set sail,” the island it sits on is better known among Parisians for its rich automotive history.
paras.zh: 尽管Large的名字也让人想起法语短语“prendre le large”，意思是“扬帆起航”，但它所在的岛屿因其丰富的汽车历史而在巴黎人中更为人所知。

paras.en: Throughout much of the 20th century, the island belonging to the inner suburb of Boulogne-Billancourt was home to the original Renault car factory, an industrial and economic powerhouse for France. In the 1930s, more than 30,000 workers made their living at the plant. But after its closure in 1992, the island began to stall. The abandoned plant was not torn down until 2005, and the effort to turn the post-industrial site into a public space moved slowly.
paras.zh: 在 20 世纪的大部分时间里，属于布洛涅-比扬古内郊的岛屿是雷诺汽车工厂的所在地，该工厂是法国的工业和经济强国。 20 世纪 30 年代，有超过 30,000 名工人在工厂谋生。但1992年关闭后，该岛开始陷入停滞。直到2005年，废弃的工厂才被拆除，将后工业场地转变为公共空间的努力进展缓慢。

paras.en: - Renault company founder Louis Renault continued to produce vehicles under the German occupation of France in World War II, leading to his postwar arrest for collaboration.
paras.zh: - 雷诺公司创始人路易斯·雷诺在第二次世界大战期间德国占领法国期间继续生产汽车，导致他在战后因合作而被捕。

paras.en: - The Renault company was subsequently nationalized in 1945.
paras.zh: - 雷诺公司随后于 1945 年被国有化。

paras.en: “In the face of trials and tribulations, the project called for a great deal of perseverance,” Pierre-Christophe Baguet, the mayor of Boulogne-Billancourt, says in a statement. “Over the course of almost 20 years, many succumbed to fatalism and discouragement and gave up on the site. Others sought to derail the project rather than to see it succeed. … It is a great victory over ignorance and prevailing selfishness.”
paras.zh: 布洛涅-比扬古市市长皮埃尔-克里斯托夫·巴盖在一份声明中表示：“面对考验和磨难，该项目需要极大的毅力。” “在近 20 年的时间里，许多人屈服于宿命论和灰心丧气，放弃了这个工地。其他人则试图破坏该项目，而不是看到它成功。……这是对无知和普遍自私的伟大胜利。”

paras.en: As an homage to the location’s history, Large’s inaugural exhibition, titled “Imaginary Engine,” will focus on the relationship between humans and machines, with a particular emphasis on cars. The show features more than 100 artworks created by 55 artists from 23 countries. The oldest pieces on display were made in the 1930s, while 17 pieces were commissioned for the museum’s opening.
paras.zh: 为了向该地点的历史致敬，Large 的首场展览题为“想象中的引擎”，将重点关注人类与机器之间的关系，特别是汽车。展览展出了来自 23 个国家的 55 名艺术家创作的 100 多件艺术作品。展出的最古老的作品是 20 世纪 30 年代制作的，另有 17 件作品是为博物馆开幕而委托制作的。

paras.en: “Opening a new institution is always rare, and doing it on an island so charged with memory is a real privilege,” Cecilia Alemani, who curated “Imaginary Engine,” tells ARTnews’ Sarah Belmont. “The Renault factory was dismantled long ago, and today a brand-new building rises in its place, open to everyone.”
paras.zh: “开设一个新机构总是很少见，在一个如此充满记忆的岛屿上开设一家新机构是一种真正的荣幸，”策展人塞西莉亚·阿莱玛尼（Cecilia Alemani）告诉艺术新闻的莎拉·贝尔蒙特（Sarah Belmont）。 “雷诺工厂很久以前就被拆除了，今天一座全新的建筑拔地而起，向所有人开放。”

paras.en: The exhibition is separated into five thematic chapters, each exploring industrial constraints and mechanical language with a variety of media. Accompanying the exhibition, which runs through March 7, is a series of film screenings that center iconic cars and car chases, including The Blues Brothers, Thelma and Louise and Taxi Tehran.
paras.zh: 展览分为五个主题章节，每个章节都通过各种媒体探索工业约束和机械语言。展览将持续至 3 月 7 日，伴随该展览的还有一系列以标志性汽车和汽车追逐为中心的电影放映，包括《布鲁斯兄弟》、《塞尔玛与路易丝》和《德黑兰出租车》。

paras.en: Starting with “Imaginary Engines,” Large is meant to serve a similar function to the Museum of Modern Art in New York City. “Paris needed a place where it could showcase art by artists who live and work here, whether they are established or emerging,” Paula Aisemberg, Large’s director, tells the New York Times’ Tina Isaac-Goizé.
paras.zh: 从“想象引擎”开始，大型博物馆旨在提供与纽约市现代艺术博物馆类似的功能。 “巴黎需要一个可以展示在这里生活和工作的艺术家的艺术作品的地方，无论他们是已成名的艺术家还是新兴艺术家，”Large 总监保拉·艾森伯格 (Paula Aisemberg) 告诉《纽约时报》的蒂娜·艾萨克-戈伊泽 (Tina Isaac-Goizé)。

paras.en: Large plans to operate by rotating temporary exhibitions throughout its vast public-facing space, 40 percent of which will cost nothing to visit. Visitors who are 26 or younger will be admitted free.
paras.zh: 大型计划的运作方式是在其面向公众的广阔空间内轮流举办临时展览，其中 40% 的参观无需付费。 26 岁或以下的游客可免费入场。

paras.en: “‘Large’ is its name. It is an invitation to set sail, to shift our perspectives, and to broaden our horizons,” Laurent Dumas, president of Large, says in the statement. “Because art transforms our ways of seeing and understanding the world, it is essential that we share and transmit it.”
paras.zh: Large 总裁 Laurent Dumas 在声明中表示：“‘Large’就是它的名字。这是一次扬帆起航、改变我们观点、拓宽我们视野的邀请。” “因为艺术改变了我们看待和理解世界的方式，所以我们分享和传播它至关重要。”

paras.en: “Imaginary Engine” will be on view at Large in Boulogne-Billancourt, France, from October 17, 2026, to March 7, 2027.
paras.zh: “想象中的引擎”将于2026年10月17日至2027年3月7日在法国布洛涅-比扬古大规模展出。

articles.title: It's Official: Timekeepers Have Gotten Rid of the Leap Second—and Introduced the Leap Hour Instead

paras.en: Every four years, February gets an extra day. You’ve heard of these “leap” years, especially if an acquaintance was born on the unusual date of February 29. What you might not have heard of, however, is the leap year’s sporadic sibling: the leap second.
paras.zh: 每四年，二月就会多一天。您听说过这些“闰年”，特别是如果您有一个熟人出生在 2 月 29 日这个不寻常的日子。然而，您可能没有听说过闰年的零星兄弟：闰秒。

paras.en: This lesser-known timekeeping fix was center stage at this week’s General Conference on Weights and Measures in France, where timekeepers decided today to return it to obscurity by getting rid of it altogether.
paras.zh: 这种鲜为人知的计时修复成为了本周在法国举行的度量衡大会的中心舞台，计时员们今天决定通过完全摆脱它来使其重新默默无闻。

paras.en: Traditionally, one Earth orbit around the sun determines the length of a year, and one Earth rotation on its axis determines the length of a day. Because it takes Earth around 365.25 days to go around the sun, timekeepers add that extra leap day once every four years to make sure our seasonal calendar stays aligned with the orbit.
paras.zh: 传统上，地球绕太阳公转一周决定一年的长度，地球绕太阳自转一周决定一天的长度。由于地球绕太阳一周大约需要 365.25 天，计时员每四年添加一次额外的闰日，以确保我们的季节日历与轨道保持一致。

paras.en: Earth’s daily rotation, however, isn’t as regular, because the speed of the planet’s spin can change. In general, Earth’s rotational speed has been slowing down throughout history. But starting around 2020, it has increased. A number of factors can play a role in Earth’s spin, including the atmosphere, ocean currents, wind, volcanoes and melting polar ice.
paras.zh: 然而，地球的日常自转并不那么规律，因为地球自转的速度会发生变化。一般来说，地球的自转速度在整个历史上一直在减慢。但从 2020 年左右开始，这一数字有所增加。许多因素都会影响地球的自转，包括大气、洋流、风、火山和融化的极地冰。

paras.en: This makes Earth’s rotation a “lousy” clock, Jeff Sherman, a physicist at the United States’ National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), tells CNN’s Katie Hunt.
paras.zh: 美国国家标准与技术研究所 (NIST) 的物理学家杰夫·谢尔曼 (Jeff Sherman) 告诉美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的凯蒂·亨特 (Katie Hunt)，这使得地球自转成为一个“糟糕”的时钟。

paras.en: Earth’s rotation does not exactly match the length of a day on our clocks. Right now, the average day on Earth is slightly longer than 24 hours. October 14, 2026, was 24 hours and 0.0006471 seconds.
paras.zh: 地球的自转与我们时钟上一天的长度并不完全一致。目前，地球上的平均一天略长于 24 小时。 2026 年 10 月 14 日是 24 小时 0.0006471 秒。

paras.en: Even as Earth’s spin wavers, our atomic clocks—crucial to keeping ultra-precise time in this age of computers, phones, GPS and satellites—tick at a stable rate. That’s because in 1967, the General Conference on Weights and Measures chose a reliable way to define a second with the help of the isotope cesium-133. When a cesium-133 atom undergoes a change between specific energy states, it emits radiation that oscillates in an exceptionally regular manner, Vahe Peroomian, a physicist at the University of Southern California, writes for the Conversation. As such, scientists reclassified a second as equivalent to 9,192,631,770 cesium-133 atom oscillations.
paras.zh: 即使地球自转发生波动，我们的原子钟（在这个计算机、电话、GPS 和卫星时代保持超精确时间至关重要）仍会以稳定的速度运行。这是因为1967年，度量衡大会在同位素铯133的帮助下选择了一种可靠的方法来定义秒。南加州大学的物理学家瓦赫·佩鲁米安 (Vahe Peroomian) 在《对话》中写道，当铯 133 原子在特定能态之间发生变化时，它会发出以异常规律的方式振荡的辐射。因此，科学家将一秒重新分类为相当于 9,192,631,770 次铯 133 原子振荡。

paras.en: Today, Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) follows this principal. But astronomical time, or Universal Time 1 (UT1), follows Earth’s fickle rotation, sometimes leading to discrepancies between the two time scales. To keep these systems as aligned as possible, timekeepers have added 27 leap seconds to UTC since 1972. “We effectively stop our clocks for that second to give Earth the opportunity to catch up,” as Konstantin Bikos and Anne Buckle write for Time and Date.
paras.zh: 如今，协调世界时 (UTC) 遵循这一原则。但天文时间或世界时 1 (UT1) 遵循地球变化无常的自转，有时会导致两个时间尺度之间的差异。为了使这些系统尽可能保持一致，自 1972 年以来，计时员在 UTC 基础上增加了 27 个闰秒。康斯坦丁·比科斯 (Konstantin Bikos) 和安妮·巴克尔 (Anne Buckle) 在《时间与日期》杂志上撰文称，“我们实际上在那一秒停止了时钟，让地球有机会赶上”。

paras.en: The goal has been for UTC and UT1 to differ by less than 0.9 seconds, and a leap second has been added when the misalignment approaches that limit. Today, however, experts at the General Conference on Weights and Measures voted to increase this margin to one hour. This negates the need for a leap second and creates the much rarer leap hour, which will be added when UTC deviates from UT1 by 3,600 seconds. Such a change likely won’t be needed for hundreds or thousands of years.
paras.zh: 我们的目标是 UTC 和 UT1 的误差小于 0.9 秒，并且当偏差接近该限制时会添加闰秒。然而今天，度量衡大会的专家们投票决定将这一时间间隔增加到一小时。这消除了对闰秒的需要，并创建了更罕见的闰时，当 UTC 与 UT1 相差 3,600 秒时，将添加闰时。这样的改变可能数百年或数千年都不需要。

paras.en: “It’s kind of a philosophical discussion, because if a leap hour happens, it won’t be for a very, very long time,” Christian Bizouard, director of the IERS Earth Orientation Center in France, tells the Guardian’s Ian Sample. “What we are doing is pushing back the decision.”
paras.zh: 法国 IERS 地球定向中心主任克里斯蒂安·比祖阿尔 (Christian Bizouard) 告诉《卫报》的伊恩·桑普勒 (Ian Sample)，“这是一场哲学讨论，因为即使发生了闰时，也不会持续很长时间。” “我们正在做的就是推迟这一决定。”

paras.en: The move caps off 30 years of debate, as the leap second has been highly controversial in the world of timekeeping. Leap seconds aren’t nearly as smooth of a fix as leap years are, and they can cause computer and website issues. Reddit famously crashed when a leap second was added on June 30, 2012. It’s “always been a problem,” Judah Levine, a former researcher at the NIST’s Time and Frequency Division, tells Scientific American’s Emma Gometz.
paras.zh: 这一举措为长达 30 年的争​​论画上句号，因为闰秒在计时界一直备受争议。闰秒的修复并不像闰年那样顺利，而且可能会导致计算机和网站出现问题。 Reddit 因 2012 年 6 月 30 日添加闰秒而崩溃。NIST 时间和频率部门前研究员 Judah Levine 告诉《科学美国人》的 Emma Gometz，这“一直是个问题”。

paras.en: Instead of adding the entire second all at once, companies such as Google and Meta add the extra time in smaller segments in a tactic called “smearing,” according to the Conversation. It’s not a simple task, however, and companies that employ smearing have long lobbied to get rid of the leap second.
paras.zh: 据《Conversation》报道，谷歌和 Meta 等公司并没有一次性添加整个秒，而是以一种名为“涂抹”的策略将额外的时间分成较小的部分。然而，这并不是一项简单的任务，采用拖尾技术的公司长期以来一直在游说废除闰秒。

paras.en: What’s more, with Earth’s recent spin acceleration, timekeepers around the world were facing the possibility of the world’s first negative leap second, in which a second would be subtracted from UTC. This sparked fears, akin to those surrounding Y2K, that our modern technologies wouldn’t be able to handle such a change.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，随着地球最近自转加速，世界各地的计时员都面临着世界上第一个负闰秒的可能性，即从 UTC 中减去一秒。这引发了类似于千年虫问题的担忧，即我们的现代技术无法应对这样的变化。

paras.en: “It’s never happened before, and therefore the software for that has never been tested,” Darryl Veitch, a researcher who leads the Timing Lab at the University of Technology Sydney, tells the Australian Broadcasting Corporation’s Ellen Phiddian. But others argued that it wouldn’t be much of a problem.
paras.zh: 悉尼科技大学计时实验室负责人达里尔·维奇 (Darryl Veitch) 告诉澳大利亚广播公司的埃伦·菲迪安 (Ellen Phiddian)，“以前从未发生过这种情况，因此相关软件也从未经过过测试。”但其他人则认为这不是什么大问题。

paras.en: The vote means that in the future, UTC will be allowed to diverge from astronomical time more than ever before.
paras.zh: 此次投票意味着未来UTC将被允许比以往任何时候都更加偏离天文时间。

paras.en: “Astronomers, Earth scientists and other users of Earth-orientation data will need to account for the growing offset when relating their observations and measurements to civil time,” Peroomian writes in the Conversation. As for everyone else, hopefully whatever technology rules everyday life when a leap hour does eventually come around will be better equipped for the time fix.
paras.zh: 佩鲁米安在对话中写道：“天文学家、地球科学家和其他地球定向数据用户在将他们的观测和测量结果与民用时间联系起来时，需要考虑到不断增加的偏移。”对于其他人来说，希望当闰时最终到来时，统治日常生活的任何技术都能够更好地适应时间修复。

articles.title: Microplastics React With Water, a New Study Says. That’s a Problem for Biology
articles.author: Jorge Garay

paras.en: One of the reasons plastic has become so ubiquitous is that, generally, it’s very chemically stable, meaning it does not readily react with the substances around it. That’s why this material is so often used for food packaging and water bottles.
paras.zh: 塑料变得如此普遍的原因之一是，通常它的化学性质非常稳定，这意味着它不容易与周围的物质发生反应。这就是为什么这种材料经常用于食品包装和水瓶。

paras.en: The same was thought to be true of microplastics—those tiny pieces of debris that break off from larger plastic objects and which, according to numerous studies, have spread to virtually every ecosystem on the planet. But scientists at Columbia University and UC Berkeley have just discovered that water can make the surfaces of microplastics chemically active and turn them into a potential hazard.
paras.zh: 人们认为微塑料也是如此，这些微小的碎片是从较大的塑料物体上脱落下来的，根据大量研究，它们几乎已经扩散到地球上的每个生态系统。但哥伦比亚大学和加州大学伯克利分校的科学家刚刚发现，水可以使微塑料表面产生化学活性，并将其变成潜在的危险。

paras.en: According to the findings of the article published in Nature, this activity can trigger the spontaneous formation of chemicals capable of altering other molecules, like those that are essential for living organisms. The phenomenon, the authors note, occurs even under normal environmental conditions, without the need for sunlight or other agents that cause plastic degradation.
paras.zh: 根据发表在《自然》杂志上的文章的研究结果，这种活动可以触发能够改变其他分子的化学物质的自发形成，例如那些对生物体至关重要的分子。作者指出，即使在正常环境条件下，这种现象也会发生，不需要阳光或其他导致塑料降解的物质。

paras.en: So how can microplastics be so reactive when bigger plastics generally aren’t? The scientists suggest this has to do with the greater available surface area for these reactions to occur.
paras.zh: 那么，当较大的塑料通常不会发生反应时，微塑料怎么会如此活跃呢？科学家们认为，这与发生这些反应的可用表面积更大有关。

paras.en: “As plastic fragments into smaller and smaller particles, its surface area increases enormously,” Wei Min, a professor of chemistry and biomedical engineering at Columbia University, said in a press release. “Then microplastics change the water that surrounds them, generating high-energy, reactive radicals that very likely contribute to biological damage that we see in animals and potentially in humans as a result of microplastic exposure.”
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚大学化学与生物医学工程教授魏敏在一份新闻稿中表示：“随着塑料碎片分解成越来越小的颗粒，其表面积大大增加。” “然后，微塑料会改变周围的水，产生高能反应性自由基，这些自由基很可能会导致我们在动物身上看到的生物损害，也可能会在人类身上看到因接触微塑料而造成的生物损害。”

paras.en: Among these potentially dangerous chemical products—called reactive oxygen species—a variety known as hydroxyl radicals stands out. They are particularly dangerous because they can snatch electrons from the proteins and fats that make up cell membranes, disrupting their structure and function. These “are textbook examples of the kinds of molecules that can damage animal and human tissue,” added Naixin Qian, a postdoctoral researcher in Min’s lab who helped lead the research.
paras.zh: 在这些具有潜在危险的化学产品（称为活性氧）中，一种被称为羟基自由基的化学产品脱颖而出。它们特别危险，因为它们可以从构成细胞膜的蛋白质和脂肪中夺取电子，破坏其结构和功能。这些“是可以损害动物和人体组织的分子类型的教科书例子，”帮助领导这项研究的Min实验室的博士后研究员钱乃新补充道。

paras.en: Our body has some defenses against this kind of damage. This is the biological function of the buzzy molecules known as antioxidants. These neutralize the reactive chemicals, but if the reactive compounds greatly outnumber antioxidants, this line of defense can be overwhelmed.
paras.zh: 我们的身体对这种损伤有一定的防御能力。这就是被称为抗氧化剂的活跃分子的生物功能。它们可以中和反应性化学物质，但如果反应性化合物的数量大大超过抗氧化剂，则这条防线可能会被淹没。

paras.en: This can develop into a scenario called oxidative stress, leading to the damage of cells. Previous research had already identified oxidative stress among the cellular responses associated with exposure to microplastics, although the mechanisms responsible for this damage are not yet fully understood.
paras.zh: 这可能会发展成一种称为氧化应激的情况，导致细胞损伤。先前的研究已经确定了与接触微塑料相关的细胞反应中的氧化应激，尽管造成这种损害的机制尚未完全清楚。

paras.en: The extent to which microplastics have pervaded our bodies remains an open debate, with some of the more sensational findings having been called into question. But if even a small amount of microplastics are present in our tissues, they could be reacting with the water in our bodies.
paras.zh: 微塑料在我们身体中的渗透程度仍然是一个公开争论，一些更耸人听闻的发现受到了质疑。但即使我们的组织中存在少量微塑料，它们也可能与我们体内的水发生反应。

paras.en: The researchers were particularly concerned with the potential effects on blood, which is largely composed of water. If contact with this fluid can chemically activate the surfaces of microplastics, their presence inside the body could pose an additional danger beyond that of the pollutants they carry or release.
paras.zh: 研究人员特别关注对血液的潜在影响，因为血液主要由水组成。如果与这种液体接触可以化学激活微塑料的表面，那么它们在体内的存在可能会带来除了它们携带或释放的污染物之外的额外危险。

paras.en: When the researchers exposed red blood cells extracted from mice to different types of microplastics, the cells became deformed and ruptured—a phenomenon known as hemolysis. The effects were greater with plastics that were more reactive with water, indicating that this activity was the cause of cellular damage.
paras.zh: 当研究人员将从小鼠身上提取的红细胞暴露于不同类型的微塑料时，细胞变形并破裂，这种现象称为溶血。对于与水反应性更强的塑料，这种影响更大，表明这种活性是细胞损伤的原因。

paras.en: Research into the effects of microplastics has long focused on other chemicals leaching from the particles or on their physical effects, often considering the plastic itself chemically inert. The larger pieces generally are, but these findings challenge the assumption that what is true of plastic on a grand scale is also true of the microscopic pieces it breaks down into.
paras.zh: 长期以来，对微塑料影响的研究一直集中在从颗粒中浸出的其他化学物质或其物理效应上，通常考虑到塑料本身具有化学惰性。较大的碎片通常是这样，但这些发现挑战了这样一种假设，即大范围塑料的真实性也适用于其分解成的微观碎片。

paras.en: This story originally appeared on WIRED en Español and has been translated from Spanish.
paras.zh: 这个故事最初出现在《连线》西班牙语版上，并由西班牙语翻译而来。

articles.title: Don’t Let a Crypto Inheritance Get Stuck on the Blockchain
articles.author: Jill Duffy

paras.en: If someone you know has cryptocurrency that you might inherit, let me just say ahoy matey! I hope your pirate spirit is alive and your treasure-hunting skills sharp, because that's what it might take to get those assets. And if you're the one holding crypto, know that if you do nothing, it's very possible those funds will die with you.
paras.zh: 如果您认识的人拥有您可能继承的加密货币，请让我说一声嘿伙计！我希望你的海盗精神依然存在，你的寻宝技巧也很敏锐，因为这就是获得这些资产所需要的。如果你是持有加密货币的人，请知道，如果你什么都不做，这些资金很可能会和你一起消失。

paras.en: In the US, cryptocurrency is considered a digital asset rather than money in terms of probate and estate law. With money and physical assets, you can sign a beneficiary form and create an estate plan or write a last will and testament naming who should get what when you die. With digital assets, however, the law says we should not assume that a deceased person wanted their private materials—everything from emails to photos—given to another person unless they explicitly said so. This puts cryptocurrency, as a digital asset, in an awkward position.
paras.zh: 在美国，根据遗嘱认证和遗产法，加密货币被视为数字资产而不是货币。有了金钱和实物资产，您可以签署受益人表格并制定遗产计划或撰写遗嘱和遗嘱，指定您去世时谁应该得到什么。然而，对于数字资产，法律规定我们不应假设死者希望将其私人材料（从电子邮件到照片的所有内容）交给另一个人，除非他们明确表示如此。这使得加密货币作为一种数字资产处于尴尬的境地。

paras.en: The options for arranging a transfer of cryptocurrency upon one's death or incapacitation breaks down by one big division: whether the crypto is held by a custodian or in a noncustodial crypto wallet.
paras.zh: 在一个人死亡或丧失行为能力时安排加密货币转移的选择分为一大类：加密货币是由托管人持有还是在非托管加密钱包中。

paras.en: A custodian or custodial wallet means a third party, such as a bank or a cryptocurrency marketplace, holds and manages the assets for you. Typically, transferring assets after death is much easier with a custodian, especially if it's a bank.
paras.zh: 托管人或托管钱包是指第三方（例如银行或加密货币市场）为您持有和管理资产。通常情况下，在死后通过托管人转移资产会容易得多，尤其是银行。

paras.en: Noncustodial wallets eliminate the middleman and let a person hold their assets directly. For crypto enthusiasts whose interest in digital currency is driven by a distaste for the traditional banking system, then using a noncustodial wallet is kind of the whole point.
paras.zh: 非托管钱包消除了中间人，让人们直接持有自己的资产。对于因对传统银行系统的厌恶而对数字货币产生兴趣的加密货币爱好者来说，使用非托管钱包就是重点。

paras.en: Noncustodial wallets can be software or hardware-based. It can even be a piece of paper with the instructions and passwords for accessing the cryptocurrency on it. (I use "password" here and throughout to refer to any string of letters, numbers, and characters needed to gain access to someone’s cryptocurrency.) Whatever kind of noncustodial wallet you choose, passing on your assets will require a DIY solution.
paras.zh: 非托管钱包可以是基于软件或硬件的。它甚至可以是一张纸，上面有用于访问加密货币的说明和密码。 （我在这里和全文中使用“密码”来指代访问某人的加密货币所需的任何字母、数字和字符。）无论您选择哪种非托管钱包，传递您的资产都需要一个 DIY 解决方案。

paras.en: When you use a third-party custodian to hold your cryptocurrency, you can choose one that has a beneficiary process in place.
paras.zh: 当您使用第三方托管人来持有您的加密货币时，您可以选择具有受益人流程的第三方托管人。

paras.en: Charles Schwab and Chase are just two examples of large, well-known financial institutions that offer crypto services and have experience transferring assets after death. Schwab, for example, houses its cryptocurrency services within brokerage accounts. Signing a beneficiary form for a brokerage account applies to the crypto account as well. One and done.
paras.zh: 嘉信理财和大通银行只是提供加密服务并拥有死后资产转移经验的大型知名金融机构的两个例子。例如，嘉信理财将其加密货币服务存放在经纪账户中。签署经纪账户受益人表格也适用于加密货币账户。一就完成了。

paras.en: Another benefit of using a bank is that at least three entities know you have an account: the bank, the government, and the credit reporting bureaus. Avenues exist for finding the banked money of deceased people. With a noncustodial wallet, this is not at all the case.
paras.zh: 使用银行的另一个好处是至少三个实体知道您有一个账户：银行、政府和信用报告局。寻找死者银行存款的途径是存在的。对于非托管钱包，情况完全不是这样。

paras.en: Similarly, if you get locked out of your online bank account, you can go to a bank branch with ID (I've had to do it) and get back in. More important to your heirs, it doesn't matter if you were locked out of the online portal when you died—that has no bearing on the account or a beneficiary's ability to receive the funds. This is not the case with noncustodial wallets.
paras.zh: 同样，如果您的网上银行帐户被锁定，您可以携带身份证件前往银行分行（我不得不这样做）并重新进入。对您的继承人来说更重要的是，您去世时是否被锁定在在线门户之外并不重要，这对帐户或受益人接收资金的能力没有影响。非托管钱包的情况并非如此。

paras.en: Note that cryptocurrency accounts, even when held through a bank, are not FDIC-insured.
paras.zh: 请注意，即使是通过银行持有的加密货币账户也不受 FDIC 保险。

paras.en: Other custodians include crypto marketplaces, such as Coinbase, and peer-to-peer payment services, like PayPal. Neither Coinbase nor PayPal have beneficiary forms as of this writing, though they do have a clear process for proving a person is entitled to a decedent's account. In both cases, you must have legal documents saying you are the executor of the estate (for PayPal) or are entitled to inherit the account (Coinbase), as well as a death certificate and other documentation. So the process is clunky and takes some advance planning, but it's still straightforward.
paras.zh: 其他托管机构包括 Coinbase 等加密货币市场和 PayPal 等点对点支付服务。截至撰写本文时，Coinbase 和 PayPal 都没有受益人表格，尽管他们确实有明确的流程来证明一个人有权使用死者的账户。在这两种情况下，您都必须有法律文件表明您是遗产执行人（对于 PayPal）或有权继承该帐户（Coinbase），以及死亡证明和其他文件。因此，这个过程很笨重，需要一些提前计划，但它仍然很简单。

paras.en: How many disadvantages there are to using a custodian depends on your outlook. As mentioned, crypto enthusiasts who eschew traditional banking may not see any value in using a custodian. Banks require ID, so you cannot hold the crypto anonymously. Banks and many other custodians report your transactions to the federal government, holding you accountable to an honest tax filing. Custodial wallets also cost money. They typically charge transaction fees, usually a small percentage of each trade.
paras.zh: 使用托管人有多少缺点取决于您的看法。如前所述，避开传统银行业务的加密货币爱好者可能看不到使用托管人的任何价值。银行需要身份证明，因此您无法匿名持有加密货币。银行和许多其他托管机构向联邦政府报告您的交易，要求您对诚实的纳税申报负责。托管钱包也需要花钱。他们通常收取交易费，通常占每笔交易的一小部分。

paras.en: The primary benefit of a noncustodial wallet is that everything is in your control. You hold the assets directly. You're responsible for knowing and keeping safe the information you need to access your assets. You also have to come up with a plan for informing your beneficiaries that a crypto account exists and making sure they can access it.
paras.zh: 非托管钱包的主要好处是一切都在您的控制之下。您直接持有资产。您有责任了解访问资产所需的信息并确保其安全。您还必须制定一项计划，通知您的受益人存在加密货币帐户，并确保他们可以访问该帐户。

paras.en: The first and biggest problem is that if you get locked out while you're alive, it's game over. "If you lose your cryptographic key, there's no company that you can appeal to," says Benjamin Orzeske, chief counsel for Uniform Law Commission and a staff attorney for the Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act, the law that guides how digital inheritance is handled in most states.
paras.zh: 第一个也是最大的问题是，如果你活着时被锁在外面，游戏就结束了。统一法律委员会首席法律顾问兼《修订后的统一信托数字资产访问法》专职律师本杰明·奥尔泽斯克 (Benjamin Orzeske) 表示：“如果你丢失了加密密钥，就没有任何公司可以向你求助。”该法指导了大多数州如何处理数字继承。

paras.en: In the case of a hardware key, a corrupted device or one lost to fire or theft may also cut off a person and their heirs from their crypto, permanently and irreversibly.
paras.zh: 就硬件密钥而言，损坏的设备或因火灾或盗窃而丢失的设备也可能永久且不可逆转地切断一个人及其继承人与加密货币的联系。

paras.en: The other major hurdle is that your fiduciary needs to know the crypto exists. No government or credit reporting bureau has a record of you holding the account. The only people who know are the ones you tell.
paras.zh: 另一个主要障碍是您的受托人需要知道加密货币的存在。政府或信用报告机构没有您持有该账户的记录。唯一知道的人就是你告诉的人。

paras.en: Now let's get procedural. Because of how the blockchain works, you must figure out a secure way to give your heirs instructions for obtaining the assets. Your system has to be safe. It doesn't come with any backups or failsafes unless you create them. And whether you can test your system to make sure it works before you die will require a huge amount of trust.
paras.zh: 现在让我们按程序进行。由于区块链的工作原理，您必须找到一种安全的方式来向您的继承人发出获取资产的指示。您的系统必须是安全的。它不附带任何备份或故障保护，除非您创建它们。在你死之前是否可以测试你的系统以确保它正常工作将需要巨大的信任。

paras.en: Ideas from Reddit users for how to build a system for passing on cryptocurrency include email dead-man switches, printed instructions given to a trusted person, and splitting instructions across two people who will need to come together to obtain access. All these solutions could work but have obvious flaws: the failure of an email system, a trusted person dying alongside you, someone forgetting you gave them instructions, and so forth.
paras.zh: Reddit 用户关于如何构建传递加密货币的系统的想法包括电子邮件紧急开关、向受信任的人提供打印说明以及将说明分给需要聚集在一起才能获得访问权限的两个人。所有这些解决方案都可以工作，但都有明显的缺陷：电子邮件系统故障、值得信赖的人与你一起死去、有人忘记你给了他们指示，等等。

paras.en: The best option may be to put the bulk of the instructions into your estate plan, including your named fiduciary, but crucially omitting any passwords. As Catherine Hodder, a senior attorney editor at FindLaw, explained to me, “The will is a public document,” and you should never put any usernames or passwords in your will.
paras.zh: 最好的选择可能是将大部分说明放入您的遗产计划中，包括您指定的受托人，但最重要的是省略任何密码。正如 FindLaw 的高级律师编辑凯瑟琳·霍德 (Catherine Hodder) 向我解释的那样，“遗嘱是一份公开文件”，您永远不应该在遗嘱中添加任何用户名或密码。

paras.en: An excellent place to put your password is inside a safe-deposit box at a bank. The existence of the deposit box should also be listed in your will. Some crypto owners have suggested stamping the password into a metal plate, which I suppose is a fine idea if you don't trust ink and paper to last longer than you.
paras.zh: 存放密码的最佳地点是银行的保险箱内。保管箱的存在也应在您的遗嘱中列出。一些加密货币所有者建议将密码印在金属板上，如果您不相信墨水和纸张的使用寿命比您更长，我认为这是一个好主意。

paras.en: One potential flaw is still that you can't do a dry run to make sure your system works unless you trust your fiduciary completely. Something as simple as needing your fingerprint to unlock a device could spell the end of your plan.
paras.zh: 一个潜在的缺陷仍然是，除非您完全信任您的受托人，否则您无法进行试运行以确保您的系统正常运行。像需要指纹解锁设备这样简单的事情可能会导致您的计划结束。

paras.en: An objection that some staunchly anti-capitalistic investors may have is that by including your cryptocurrency in your estate plan, you've returned it to the realm of traditional law and governance.
paras.zh: 一些坚定的反资本主义投资者可能会反对的是，通过将加密货币纳入您的遗产计划，您已将其返回到传统法律和治理领域。

articles.title: HTC Made Smart Glasses That Are Way More Private
articles.author: Boone Ashworth

paras.en: You can’t really talk about smart glasses without bringing up Meta. HTC, the company behind 2010-era virtual reality headsets and a failed smartphone business, seems quite eager to tackle that comparison directly.
paras.zh: 谈论智能眼镜就不能不提到 Meta。 HTC 是 2010 年虚拟现实耳机背后的公司，但智能手机业务却失败了，它似乎非常渴望直接解决这一问题。

paras.en: In September, HTC started selling its $499 Vive Eagle smart glasses in the US. The Eagles have lots of the same features as other glasses on the market—cameras for capturing photos and video, speakers in the frames for music playback and calls, an embedded AI agent you can ask questions of and even get recipes from by taking pictures of stuff in your fridge.
paras.zh: 9 月，HTC 开始在美国销售售价 499 美元的 Vive Eagle 智能眼镜。 Eagles 具有许多与市场上其他眼镜相同的功能——用于拍摄照片和视频的摄像头、用于音乐播放和通话的扬声器、一个嵌入式人工智能代理，您可以通过拍摄冰箱里的东西的照片来询问问题，甚至从中获取食谱。

paras.en: But HTC also wants to steer clear of the ongoing debate about privacy in camera-equipped smart glasses. Meta has been dogged by controversy for its smart glasses, with people worried about the company’s interest in enabling face-recognition features, and calling the people who wear them creepy. HTC is aware of that discourse and thinks it is completely possible to make smart glasses that aren’t a privacy nightmare.
paras.zh: 但 HTC 也希望避开有关配备摄像头的智能眼镜的隐私问题的持续争论。 Meta 的智能眼镜一直饱受争议，人们担心该公司对启用面部识别功能的兴趣，并称佩戴这些眼镜的人令人毛骨悚然。 HTC 意识到了这种说法，并认为完全有可能制造出不会成为隐私噩梦的智能眼镜。

paras.en: “It's not just about protecting the consumer, but it's also about protecting people around the consumer,” Dan McDowell, HTC Vive’s head of enterprise sales, tells WIRED. “People can usher in, I think, what are really tremendous experiences with a new layer of confidence and protection.”
paras.zh: HTC Vive 企业销售主管 Dan McDowell 告诉《连线》杂志：“这不仅是为了保护消费者，也是为了保护消费者周围的人。” “我认为，人们可以通过新的信心和保护层迎来真正巨大的体验。”

paras.en: I’ve been wandering around with the glasses for a couple of weeks, and so far they meet my expectations for what smart glasses have become. They protect my eyes from the sun. They snap good photos and videos. You can record and transcribe voice notes. The music playback has decent sound quality. (I’ll always prefer a solid pair of headphones if I’m actually trying to listen to music, but the speakers work just fine.) They come in two styles—one with square Wayfarer-esque lenses and the other more rounded.
paras.zh: 我戴着这款眼镜闲逛了几个星期，到目前为止，它们满足了我对智能眼镜的期望。它们保护我的眼睛免受阳光照射。他们拍摄精彩的照片和视频。您可以录制和转录语音笔记。音乐播放音质不错。 （如果我真的想听音乐，我总是更喜欢一副坚固的耳机，但扬声器工作得很好。）它们有两种款式——一种带有方形的 Wayfarer 式镜片，另一种则更圆。

paras.en: The Vive Eagle glasses can get 4.5 hours of battery life on continuous music playback. They can last 36 hours on standby. HTC also sells a companion clip-on battery pack called Power Boost that costs $49. It clips right onto the frame and is noticeable but not as obnoxious as you might think.
paras.zh: Vive Eagle 眼镜在连续播放音乐时可以获得 4.5 小时的电池续航时间。它们可以持续 36 小时待机。 HTC 还销售一款名为 Power Boost 的配套夹式电池组，售价 49 美元。它直接夹在框架上，很引人注目，但并不像您想象的那么令人讨厌。

paras.en: Don’t forget the AI assistant, Vive AI, which can utilize OpenAI’s ChatGPT or Google’s Gemini. It doesn’t require a login, so users are “de-identified” in a way that keeps the services from retaining personal information. (That also means, by default, you won’t be able to enjoy many of the personalization features these chatbots offer by gleaning information from your emails and messages.) The glasses come with Vive’s AI Plus, free for the first two years. After that, users must pay a monthly $2.50 subscription fee.
paras.zh: 不要忘记人工智能助手 Vive AI，它可以利用 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 或 Google 的 Gemini。它不需要登录，因此用户被“去识别化”，从而防止服务保留个人信息。 （这也意味着，默认情况下，你将无法享受这些聊天机器人通过从你的电子邮件和消息中收集信息而提供的许多个性化功能。）这款眼镜配备了 Vive 的 AI Plus，前两年免费。此后，用户必须每月支付 2.50 美元的订阅费。

paras.en: Right by the cameras is a bright indicator light. If you cover the light, it won’t record. If someone around you says stop recording, that will stop the recording. Video footage you capture is encrypted and stored on the glasses—it’s not automatically sent to the phone or cloud. If you want to import photos or videos, you have to do it manually in the app.
paras.zh: 摄像头旁边有一个明亮的指示灯。如果遮住光线，就不会录制。如果你周围有人说停止录音，录音就会停止。您拍摄的视频片段会被加密并存储在眼镜上，不会自动发送到手机或云端。如果您想导入照片或视频，则必须在应用程序中手动执行。

paras.en: Meta has faced scrutiny over the indicator light before, as some users have blocked the LED with stickers or broken into the hardware to turn it off. Meta has responded with software updates that disable the camera if someone tampers with the indicator light, along with other privacy-focused measures.
paras.zh: Meta 之前就曾面临过指示灯问题的审查，因为一些用户用贴纸挡住了 LED 灯，或者侵入硬件将其关闭。 Meta 已经做出了回应，推出了软件更新，如果有人篡改指示灯，摄像头就会被禁用，此外还有其他注重隐私的措施。

paras.en: I ask McDowell how HTC, and really any smart glasses maker, can get past the “trust me, bro”–style privacy promises companies tend to make.
paras.zh: 我问 McDowell，HTC 以及任何智能眼镜制造商如何才能摆脱公司往往做出的“相信我，兄弟”式的隐私承诺。

paras.en: “We're not a social media company,” McDowell says. “There's no benefit to me to have any of your info. We don't train our AI model or any third-party AI models with any of the information that is used on the glasses.”
paras.zh: “我们不是一家社交媒体公司，”麦克道尔说。 “拥有您的任何信息对我来说没有任何好处。我们不会使用眼镜上使用的任何信息来训练我们的人工智能模型或任何第三方人工智能模型。”

paras.en: The real problem may be that with cameras on the frames, smart glasses are hard to distinguish between brands. The Vive Eagles look a lot like Meta glasses, and people worried about those privacy issues may not know that the Eagles are different and not tied to Mark Zuckerberg’s company. I’ve had friends see me wearing them and ask if they’re smart glasses. Yeah, I replied, but not the ones they’re thinking of. That didn’t seem to dispel any of their suspicions.
paras.zh: 真正的问题可能是，由于镜框上装有摄像头，智能眼镜很难区分品牌。 Vive Eagles 看起来很像 Meta 眼镜，担心这些隐私问题的人们可能不知道 Eagles 是不同的，并且与马克·扎克伯格的公司没有任何关系。我有朋友看到我戴着它们，就问我这是不是智能眼镜。是的，我回答了，但不是他们想到的。这似乎并没有消除他们的任何怀疑。

paras.en: The hope, at least how HTC frames it, is that more players with better privacy practices will help shift cultural disdain for smart glasses. A bunch of other companies are going cameraless, like Even Realities, Viture, and Halliday. Others are building theirs with privacy shields or focusing on virtual displays instead of capturing the world around you. That said, no one has captured the market quite like Meta.
paras.zh: 希望，至少 HTC 是这样设计的，更多拥有更好隐私保护措施的玩家将有助于改变对智能眼镜的文化蔑视。许多其他公司也正在走向无摄像头，例如 Even Realities、Viture 和 Halliday。其他人则在构建自己的隐私防护罩或专注于虚拟显示，而不是捕捉您周围的世界。也就是说，没有人能像 Meta 一样占领市场。

paras.en: “We'd like to make sure that our technology adapts to society's expectations, not the other way around,” McDowell says. “I hope that everybody that's making products like these takes steps in the right direction.”
paras.zh: “我们希望确保我们的技术适应社会的期望，而不是相反，”麦克道尔说。 “我希望每个生产此类产品的人都朝着正确的方向迈出一步。”

articles.title: 2 killed after truck drives into crowd at Wichita sports complex

paras.en: Oct. 17 (UPI) -- A child and an adult were killed Saturday after a truck drove into a crowd at a south soccer game in Wichita, Kans., according to police.
paras.zh: 10 月 17 日（合众国际社）——据警方称，周六，在堪萨斯州威奇托举行的一场南部足球比赛中，一辆卡车冲进人群，造成一名儿童和一名成人死亡。

paras.en: The Wichita Police Department said multiple people were injured at the Stryker Sports Complex and taken to area hospitals.
paras.zh: 威奇托警察局表示，史赛克体育中心多人受伤，已被送往当地医院。

paras.en: A suspect is in custody, police added. A spokesperson said two juveniles were in the vehicle at the time.
paras.zh: 警方补充说，一名嫌疑人已被拘留。一名发言人称，当时车内有两名青少年。

paras.en: The city of Wichita said on social media all events at the sports complex have been canceled until further notice.
paras.zh: 威奇托市在社交媒体上表示，体育中心的所有活动均已取消，直至另行通知。

paras.en: "We ask that you keep all individuals and families affected in your thoughts and prayers during this difficult time," the city said.
paras.zh: 该市表示：“在这个困难时期，我们请求你们为所有受到影响的个人和家庭祈祷。”

paras.en: Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly said on social media she is monitoring the situation and has been in touch with Wichita Mayor Lily Wu.
paras.zh: 堪萨斯州州长劳拉·凯利在社交媒体上表示，她正在关注事态发展，并已与威奇托市市长吴莉莉保持联系。

paras.en: "My condolences go out to the families of the victims, the survivors, and all those impacted by this event," Kelly said.
paras.zh: 凯利说：“我向受害者家属、幸存者以及所有受这一事件影响的人表示哀悼。”

articles.title: Man killed in New York subway shooting, police say

paras.en: Oct. 17 (UPI) -- A man was shot dead Saturday afternoon after an argument in a crowded New York subway station, police said.
paras.zh: 10 月 17 日（UPI）——警方称，周六下午，一名男子在拥挤的纽约地铁站发生争执后被枪杀。

paras.en: The shooting happened at the 7th Avenue station at 53rd Street station in Midtown Manhattan at around 12:21 p.m. EST, the New York Police Department said.
paras.zh: 枪击事件于中午12点21分左右发生在曼哈顿中城第7大道车站和第53街车站之间。美国东部时间，纽约警察局表示。

paras.en: The unnamed victim in his 30s was shot once in the chest and pronounced dead at a nearby hospital later.
paras.zh: 这名30多岁的未透露姓名的受害者胸部中弹，随后在附近一家医院被宣布死亡。

paras.en: Police told a news conference a dispute between two men began on the platform and moved onto a train and back onto the platform.
paras.zh: 警方在新闻发布会上表示，两名男子之间的争执始于站台上，然后转移到火车上，然后又回到站台上。

paras.en: A weapon has not been recovered and the suspect remains at large and considered dangerous, police said.
paras.zh: 警方表示，武器尚未找到，嫌疑人仍然在逃，被认为是危险的。

paras.en: The suspect was last seen on foot wearing a red track suit and black puffer vest, security footage showed.
paras.zh: 监控录像显示，嫌疑人最后一次出现时是步行穿着红色运动服和黑色羽绒背心。

articles.title: Canadian military base 'incident' has killed people, officials say

paras.en: Oct. 17 (UPI) -- An "incident" at a Canadian military base has resulted in the deaths and injuries of an undisclosed number of people, officials said Saturday evening.
paras.zh: 10 月 17 日（合众社）——官员周六晚表示，加拿大军事基地发生的一起“事件”造成人员伤亡，具体人数不详。

paras.en: Defense Minister David McGuinty, who announced the deaths at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in eastern Alberta, did not disclose what occurred at the installation.
paras.zh: 国防部长戴维·麦坚蒂宣布了阿尔伯塔省东部温赖特加拿大军事基地发生的死亡事件，但他没有透露该设施发生的情况。

paras.en: He said he "cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory."
paras.zh: 他说他“最近不记得发生过这样的事件”。

paras.en: McGuinty added the Canadian Armed Forces, Department of National Defense, and the federal government were working with the provincial and local government "to mobilize all necessary support and working through the details of what actually occurred."
paras.zh: 麦坚蒂补充说，加拿大武装部队、国防部和联邦政府正在与省和地方政府合作，“动员一切必要的支持，并研究实际发生的细节”。

paras.en: Alberta MP Dane Lloyd, who is also a Canadian Army reservist, said in a post on social media that "significant casualties" resulted from the incident.
paras.zh: 阿尔伯塔省议员、加拿大陆军预备役军人戴恩·劳埃德在社交媒体上发帖称，该事件造成“重大人员伤亡”。

paras.en: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police battalion in Wainwright said, "Early reports were that there was a fire at a training area."
paras.zh: 温赖特的加拿大皇家骑警营表示：“早期报告称训练区发生火灾。”

paras.en: The RCMP said it said "numerous resources" were sent to help, but its "initial involvement is winding down."
paras.zh: 加拿大皇家骑警表示，已派出“大量资源”提供帮助，但“最初的参与正在逐渐结束”。

paras.en: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on social media that a "major fire" was caused by the incident.
paras.zh: 加拿大总理马克·卡尼在社交媒体上表示，该事件引发了“重大火灾”。

paras.en: Danielle Smith, Alberta's premier, said her government was in close contact with Carney.
paras.zh: 艾伯塔省省长丹妮尔·史密斯表示，她的政府正在与卡尼保持密切联系。

paras.en: According to the municipality of Wainright, "a large fire originating near the Canadian Forces Base has spread rapidly due to high winds and has crossed into the Municipal District of Wainwright No. 61."
paras.zh: 据温赖特市政府称，“加拿大军事基地附近发生的一场大火由于大风而迅速蔓延，并已蔓延到温赖特第 61 号市政区。”

paras.en: The municipality said emergency responders were assessing the situation and there was currently no order to evacuate.
paras.zh: 市政府表示，紧急救援人员正在评估情况，目前尚未下达疏散命令。

articles.title: Bette Midler Accepts 2026 Woody Guthrie Prize, Sings Protest Classic: ‘My Small Contribution to the Resistance’
articles.author: Paul Grein

paras.en: Bette Midler sang her updated version of Woody Guthrie’s 1940s protest classic “All You Fascists (Bound to Lose)” as she accepted the 2026 Woody Guthrie Prize at Cain’s Ballroom in Tulsa, Oklahoma, on Friday (Oct. 16). Just so no one missed the message, she wore a T-shirt embossed with the blunt song title.
paras.zh: 周五（10 月 16 日），贝蒂·米德勒 (Bette Midler) 在俄克拉荷马州塔尔萨的 Cain’s Ballroom 接受 2026 年伍迪·格思里奖时，演唱了伍迪·格思里 1940 年代抗议经典歌曲《你们法西斯分子（必败）》的更新版本。为了不让任何人错过这条信息，她穿了一件印有直率歌曲标题浮雕的 T 恤。

paras.en: “Justice doesn’t always come from the courthouse,” Midler said in accepting the award. “Sometimes the law is late, overdressed, and on the wrong side. Justice comes from a beat-up guitar instead… So, when I wanted to say something about what I was seeing going on today, I took his [Woody’s] song, and I put new words in its mouth, because the old fights came back in new suits. They always do.”
paras.zh: “正义并不总是来自法院，”米德勒在接受奖项时说道。 “有时候，法律迟到了，穿得太过分，而且站在了错误的一边。正义来自一把破旧的吉他……所以，当我想说点我今天所看到的事情时，我拿起他的[伍迪]歌曲，然后在它嘴里放了新词，因为旧的争斗会穿着新衣服回来。他们总是这样做。”

paras.en: She continued, “Thank you for accepting me, and for letting me rewrite the song, that became my small contribution to the Resistance. We’re having a knife fight in a phone booth. These are hard and terrible times. A war is being waged against us, and we are all being drafted. Whether the letter arrives or not. Thank you for noticing that I showed up for duty.”
paras.zh: 她继续说道，“感谢您接受我，并让我重写这首歌，这成为我对抵抗运动的小小的贡献。我们正在电话亭里进行一场刀战。这是艰难而可怕的时刻。一场针对我们的战争正在发动，我们都被征召入伍。无论信是否到达。感谢您注意到我来值班。”

paras.en: Midler released her spirited version of Guthrie’s song on YouTube in April, accompanied by this message: “You know I’ve been around a long time, but I have never lived through what we are living through now. The great Woody Guthrie wrote this song many years ago. I changed some of the words to fit our times, and I hope you’ll sing it when you are marching. Because sometimes people, sometimes you just gotta SING OUT!”
paras.zh: 米德勒于四月份在 YouTube 上发布了格思里歌曲的充满活力的版本，并附上这样的信息：“你知道我已经存在很长时间了，但我从未经历过我们现在所经历的事情。伟大的伍迪·格思里很多年前写了这首歌。我改变了一些歌词以适应我们的时代，我希望你们在游行时唱这首歌。因为有时人们，有时你就必须唱出来！”

paras.en: Midler had teamed with Eric Kornfeld to write her derivative of Guthrie’s protest classic. She also executive produced the video, which was directed by Toni Basil and Seanne Farmer. The video featured cameos by such celebrities as Barbara Hershey, Midler’s co-star in Beaches, and David Hyde Pierce, her co-star in the Broadway revival of Hello, Dolly!
paras.zh: 米德勒与埃里克·科恩菲尔德 (Eric Kornfeld) 合作，根据格思里的抗议经典作品创作了衍生作品。她还担任该视频的执行制作人，该视频由托尼·巴兹尔和肖恩·法默执导。视频中客串了米勒在《海滩》中的搭档芭芭拉·赫希和在百老汇重演《你好，多莉！》中搭档的大卫·海德·皮尔斯等名人。

paras.en: “She [Midler] woke up our neighborhood this year with her powerful rendition of ‘All You Fascists (Bound To Lose),’” Guthrie’s granddaughter, Anna Canoni, said at the event. “She brought Woody back to the fight, back to the protest, the rallies, the ongoing struggle for democracy, and humanity. We are absolutely honored that she has joined our remarkable community of artists who have also carried Woody’s words and music to the fight.”
paras.zh: 格思里的孙女安娜·卡诺尼 (Anna Canoni) 在活动中说：“今年，她（米德勒）用强有力的《你们法西斯分子（必败）》的演绎唤醒了我们的邻居。” “她让伍迪重新回到战斗中，重新回到抗议、集会、为民主和人性而进行的持续斗争中。我们非常荣幸她加入了我们杰出的艺术家社区，他们也将伍迪的文字和音乐带入了战斗。”

paras.en: Cady Shaw, senior director of the Woody Guthrie Center (which hosts the annual award presentation), added: “Because beneath the glamour, the spectacular voice, and that sharp sense of humor is a woman who understands something Woody knew all along. That we all have a responsibility to leave this world a little better than we found it. And that is precisely what the Woody Guthrie Prize celebrates. It recognizes artists whose contributions extend far beyond their creative achievements, individuals who have demonstrated the courage to speak up, and the determination to turn their convictions into meaningful action. Bette Midler embodies that spirit beautifully.”
paras.zh: 伍迪格思里中心（Woody Guthrie Center）高级总监卡迪·肖（Cady Shaw）补充道：“在魅力、壮观的声音和敏锐的幽默感背后，是一位了解伍迪一直以来都知道的事情的女性。我们都有责任让这个世界比我们发现的更好一点。而这正是伍迪格思里奖所庆祝的。它表彰那些贡献远远超出其创造性成就的艺术家，那些表现出勇气和决心的个人。将他们的信念转化为有意义的行动，贝蒂·米德勒完美地体现了这种精神。”

paras.en: Preceding the presentation, Midler was interviewed onstage by music journalist Rona Elliot.
paras.zh: 在演讲之前，米德勒在台上接受了音乐记者罗娜·埃利奥特的采访。

paras.en: A silent auction featured a signed ukulele from Midler’s personal collection, along with other items from her archive; a signed lithograph by Bob Dylan; rare prints of Dylan and related artists; a premium ticket package from the Oklahoma City Thunder; and tickets to one of Garth Brooks’ upcoming Tulsa shows.
paras.zh: 一场无声拍卖会展出了米德勒个人收藏中的一把签名尤克里里琴，以及她档案中的其他物品；鲍勃·迪伦签名的版画；迪伦和相关艺术家的稀有版画；俄克拉荷马城雷霆队的高级门票套餐；以及加斯·布鲁克斯 (Garth Brooks) 即将在塔尔萨举办的一场演出的门票。

paras.en: Rising country artist Bryan Andrews performed a selection of original songs including “Yeehaw,” as well as leading an audience sing-along of Guthrie’s most famous song, “This Land Is Your Land.”
paras.zh: 新晋乡村艺术家布莱恩·安德鲁斯 (Bryan Andrews) 表演了一系列原创歌曲，包括《Yeehaw》，并带领观众合唱格思里最著名的歌曲《This Land Is Your Land》。

paras.en: The event served as a fundraiser to support the center’s educational programs, public concerts, and exhibitions.
paras.zh: 该活动是为了支持该中心的教育项目、公共音乐会和展览而举办的筹款活动。

paras.en: The Woody Guthrie Prize seeks to recognize artists who reflect Guthrie’s belief that music can be a force for social justice and change. Guthrie died in 1967 at age 55.
paras.zh: 伍迪·格思里奖旨在表彰那些反映格思里信念的艺术家，即音乐可以成为社会正义和变革的力量。格思里于 1967 年去世，享年 55 岁。

paras.en: Midler, 80, has won three Grammys, three Primetime Emmys and a Tony (plus a non-competitive Tony). She has received two Oscar nominations. She would likely have received the Kennedy Center Honors by now, but President Trump has said that he struck potential honorees who were, in his words, “too woke.”
paras.zh: 80 岁的米德勒赢得了三项格莱美奖、三项黄金时段艾美奖和一项托尼奖（外加一项非竞争性托尼奖）。她曾两次获得奥斯卡提名。她现在可能已经获得了肯尼迪中心荣誉奖，但特朗普总统表示，他打击了潜在的获奖者，用他的话说，他们“太清醒了”。

paras.en: Here’s a complete list of recipients of the Woody Guthrie Prize:
paras.zh: 以下是伍迪·格思里奖获得者的完整名单：

articles.title: Iron Maiden Announce 2027 Run for Your Lives North American Tour: See the Dates
articles.author: Mitchell Peters

paras.en: Iron Maiden will return to North America in 2027 for the third and final leg of its Run for Your Lives tour.
paras.zh: Iron Maiden 将于 2027 年返回北美，进行 Run for Your Lives 巡演的第三站，也是最后一站。

paras.en: The heavy metal legends announced the 2027 dates Friday (Oct. 16), extending their 50th-anniversary trek after previously planning to take a break from live performances next year.
paras.zh: 重金属传奇人物周五（10 月 16 日）宣布了 2027 年的演出日期，延续了他们此前计划明年暂停现场表演的 50 周年纪念之旅。

paras.en: “As many of our fans know, Maiden were planning on taking a break from live performances in 2027,” Maiden bassist Steve Harris said in a statement. “But we’ve been enjoying this last leg in the USA and Canada so much that we all had a chat and decided we should take the show to parts we missed, particularly the North West and South East. It just seems fair to our many fans there who have given us tremendous support for so many years.”
paras.zh: “正如我们许多粉丝所知，Maiden 计划在 2027 年暂停现场表演，”Maiden 贝斯手史蒂夫·哈里斯 (Steve Harris) 在一份声明中表示。 “但是我们非常享受在美国和加拿大的最后一站，所以我们都聊了聊，并决定应该把演出带到我们错过的地方，特别是西北和东南部。对于我们多年来给予我们巨大支持的众多粉丝来说，这似乎很公平。”

paras.en: The Live Nation-promoted tour begins April 14, 2027, at the Tacoma Dome in Tacoma, Washington, and concludes May 11, 2027, at UBS Arena in Belmont Park, New York.
paras.zh: Live Nation 宣传的巡演于 2027 年 4 月 14 日在华盛顿州塔科马的塔科马穹顶开始，并于 2027 年 5 月 11 日在纽约贝尔蒙特公园的 UBS Arena 结束。

paras.en: Bullet For My Valentine and The Raven Age will join the trek as special guests, marking the first time since 1983 that Iron Maiden has toured with two other British bands on the bill.
paras.zh: Bullet For My Valentine 和 The Raven Age 将作为特邀嘉宾加入此次巡演，这是 Iron Maiden 自 1983 年以来首次与另外两支英国乐队一起巡演。

paras.en: After the North American run, the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees will perform at two U.S. music festivals: Sonic Temple in Columbus, Ohio, on May 14 and Boardwalk Rock in Ocean City, Maryland, on May 16.
paras.zh: 北美演出结束后，摇滚名人堂入选者将在两个美国音乐节上表演：5 月 14 日在俄亥俄州哥伦布市举行的 Sonic Temple 音乐节和 5 月 16 日在马里兰州大洋城举行的 Boardwalk Rock 音乐节。

paras.en: The 2027 dates “will definitely be the last” of Maiden’s Run for Your Lives tour, according to a press release. The trek will have played 107 shows by the time it concludes.
paras.zh: 据一份新闻稿称，2027 年“肯定将是 Maiden’s Run for Your Lives 巡演的最后一场”。到结束时，旅程已演出 107 场。

paras.en: “We can’t get everywhere but we can try!” Harris continued in his statement. “Also, we have always enjoyed playing the many great festivals that are in Europe and wanted to experience a couple more in the USA which we will do at the end of the tour in Columbus and Maryland. At festivals you are not just playing to your own fans so it’s always a challenge and we all love a challenge!”
paras.zh: “我们无法到达所有地方，但我们可以尝试！”哈里斯继续发表声明。 “此外，我们一直很喜欢参加欧洲的许多精彩音乐节，并希望在美国体验更多音乐节，我们将在哥伦布和马里兰州巡演结束时进行。在音乐节上，你不仅仅是为自己的粉丝演奏，所以这始终是一个挑战，我们都喜欢挑战！”

articles.title: Zach Bryan Gets Candid About Sobriety in Matthew McConaughey Interview: ‘Why Am I Drinking?’
articles.author: Mitchell Peters

paras.en: Zach Bryan is opening up about his sobriety journey in a new interview with Matthew McConaughey.
paras.zh: 扎克·布莱恩在马修·麦康纳的新采访中讲述了他的戒酒之旅。

paras.en: The 30-year-old country star sat down with the Oscar-winning actor for a two-hour conversation, reflecting on his relationship with alcohol and the experience that ultimately led him to quit drinking.
paras.zh: 这位 30 岁的乡村明星与这位奥斯卡获奖演员进行了两个小时的交谈，反思了他与酒精的关系以及最终导致他戒酒的经历。

paras.en: “I always thought sobriety was a joke because it’s people who couldn’t control themselves celebrating not being able to control themselves,” Bryan told McConaughey. “When I was drinking a lot, I thought, ‘Why can’t you control yourself?’ I never realized I had a problem.”
paras.zh: “我一直认为清醒是一个笑话，因为那些无法控制自己的人庆祝无法控制自己，”布莱恩告诉麦康纳。 “当我喝了很多酒时，我想，‘你为什么不能控制自己？’我从来没有意识到我有问题。”

paras.en: The interview arrives following the release of Bryan’s new eight-song EP, Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs, which dropped Friday (Oct. 16) through Warner Records.
paras.zh: 此次采访是在布莱恩的新 8 首歌 EP《Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs》发行后发布的，该 EP 于周五（10 月 16 日）通过华纳唱片公司发售。

paras.en: In the conversation, uploaded to Bryan’s YouTube channel Friday, the singer-songwriter recounted a month-long motorcycle trip he planned to take with friends from New York City to Los Angeles. When his friends couldn’t make it, he decided to hit the road alone.
paras.zh: 在周五上传到布莱恩 YouTube 频道的对话中，这位创作歌手讲述了他计划与朋友从纽约到洛杉矶为期一个月的摩托车之旅。当朋友们无法成行时，他决定独自上路。

paras.en: “One night I was drinking at the Grisly, this bar in the West Village and I was like, ‘I’m leaving tomorrow’ … I wake up, get on my motorcycle and I stayed at all these national parks,” Bryan said.
paras.zh: “有一天晚上，我在西村的 Grisly 酒吧喝酒，我当时想，‘我明天就要离开’……我醒来，骑上摩托车，然后呆在所有这些国家公园里，”布莱恩说。

paras.en: Although the trip included memorable experiences, such as dining with veterans and skydiving from vintage planes, Bryan said he spent much of his time drinking at local bars.
paras.zh: 尽管这次旅行包括了令人难忘的经历，例如与退伍军人一起用餐和从老式飞机上跳伞，但布莱恩说他大部分时间都在当地的酒吧喝酒。

paras.en: “I was stopping at all these bars and drinking myself to sleep,” the musician said. “Waking up every morning, getting on my motorcycle thinking I was on some sort of soul journey.”
paras.zh: “我在所有这些酒吧停下来，喝酒睡觉，”这位音乐家说。 “每天早上醒来，骑上摩托车，我就觉得自己正在进行某种灵魂之旅。”

paras.en: The trip took a turn when Bryan arrived in Seattle. After weeks on the road, he found himself sitting outside a truck stop with a beer, questioning what the experience had actually given him.
paras.zh: 当布莱恩抵达西雅图时，旅程发生了转变。在路上行驶了几周后，他发现自己坐在一个卡车停靠站外，手里拿着啤酒，质疑这段经历到底给他带来了什么。

paras.en: “After all this beautiful scenery, all these nights, all these bars I’ve been to, all this s—t that I’ve done, I was at this Pilot truck stop right outside of Seattle. I’ll never forget this for as long as I live,” he said. “I go into this Pilot and I grab a 40 Budweiser and I’m sitting on the curb with my motorcycle in front of me. I’m drinking [the beer] and I’m thinking ‘What the hell was all that worth? Why did I do any of that? I feel emptier than when I left.’”
paras.zh: “经历了所有这些美丽的风景、所有这些夜晚、我去过的所有这些酒吧、我所做的所有这些事情之后，我来到了西雅图郊外的这个 Pilot 卡车停靠站。只要我活着，我就永远不会忘记这一点，”他说。 “我走进这个 Pilot 车，抓起一杯 40 瓶百威啤酒，坐在路边，摩托车在我面前。我一边喝着啤酒，一边想‘这一切到底值啥？我为什么要这么做？我感觉比离开时更空虚。’”

paras.en: Bryan said he felt he had “wasted 30 days” chasing a defining moment, prompting him to confront his drinking habits.
paras.zh: 布莱恩表示，他觉得自己“浪费了 30 天”去追逐一个决定性的时刻，这促使他正视自己的饮酒习惯。

paras.en: “It was just me in a f—king truck stop parking lot. And that’s when I said, ‘Why am I drinking right now? What am I celebrating?’ That’s when I kind of looked in the mirror,” he said. “I’m not the f—king sober type either.”
paras.zh: “只有我一个人在一个该死的卡车站停车场。就在那时我说，‘我为什么现在喝酒？我在庆祝什么？’就在那时我看着镜子，”他说。 “我也不是那种该死的清醒类型。”

paras.en: Despite once believing sobriety wasn’t for him, Bryan said giving up alcohol has left him happier and more creatively fulfilled.
paras.zh: 尽管布莱恩一度认为戒酒不适合他，但他表示戒酒让他更​​快乐，更有创造力。

paras.en: “Quitting drinking has been really great. I’ve had a lot of fun,” he said. “I enjoy writing again, I haven’t felt [like this] since I was 17. I feel like a kid again. I wake up and I’m ready to go, I want to jump in the pond. I want to play with the dog. I want to do everything.”
paras.zh: “戒酒真的很棒。我玩得很开心，”他说。 “我又喜欢写作了，从 17 岁起我就没再有过这样的感觉了。我感觉自己又像个孩子了。我醒来，准备好出发，我想跳进池塘里。我想和狗一起玩。我想做一切。”

paras.en: Bryan’s Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs features collaborations with Lana Del Rey (“Lies”) and Turnpike Troubadours (“Plainsman”), along with tracks including “Robot Killed the Working Man” and “Backwards.” The EP marks his first new music since his sixth studio album, With Heaven On Top, which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in January.
paras.zh: 布莱恩的《Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs》与 Lana Del Rey（《Lies》）和 Turnpike Troubadours（《Plainsman》）合作，曲目包括《Robot Killed the Work Man》和《Backwards》。这张 EP 是他自第六张录音室专辑《With Heaven On Top》以来的首张新音乐，该专辑于 1 月份首次亮相就登上 Billboard 200 排行榜第一名。

articles.title: ‘The Diplomat’ U.K. Prime Minister on the Operatic Way He Learned of His “Shocking” Season 4 Storyline
articles.author: Hilary Lewis

paras.en: [The following story contains spoilers from the first four episodes of The Diplomat season four, through “Pagliacci.”]
paras.zh: [以下故事包含《外交官》第四季前四集到“丑角”的剧透。]

paras.en: Rory Kinnear couldn’t leave The Diplomat without one more surprise.
paras.zh: 罗里·金尼尔 (Rory Kinnear) 离开《外交官》时必然会带来更多惊喜。

paras.en: The actor, who has spent the past four seasons playing wild-card British prime minister Nicol Trowbridge, resigns midway through the Netflix political thriller’s latest season, announcing the move in a shocking moment at the end of episode four. Trowbridge steps down after an unusually surreal episode for The Diplomat, in which he imagines that former adviser Margaret Roylin (Celia Imrie), who dies early in season three, is still alive and chiming in on his latest actions. He also hallucinates that the U.S. officials with whom he’s meeting are laughing at and mocking him and sings an aria as he thinks of himself as both a king and a clown (donning both costumes).
paras.zh: 这位在过去四季中一直扮演外卡英国首相尼科尔·特罗布里奇的演员在 Netflix 政治惊悚片最新一季的中途辞职，并在第四集结尾的一个令人震惊的时刻宣布了这一举动。特罗布里奇在《外交官》经历了一段异常超现实的情节后辞职，在该情节中，他想象第三季早些时候去世的前顾问玛格丽特·罗伊林（西莉亚·伊姆里饰）仍然活着，并参与了他的最新行动。他还幻想与他会面的美国官员正在嘲笑他，并唱着一首咏叹调，因为他认为自己既是国王又是小丑（穿着两种服装）。

paras.en: Despite the trippy scenes leading up to Kinnear’s final scene, which comes just one episode after viewers learn that U.K. foreign secretary Austin Dennison (David Gyasi) has died in a helicopter crash, Diplomat showrunner Debora Cahn says there were grounded, real-life reasons for this season’s shake-up in the British government.
paras.zh: 金尼尔的最后一幕是在观众得知英国外交大臣奥斯汀·丹尼森（大卫·吉亚西饰）在直升机失事中丧生后的一集，尽管在金尼尔的最后一幕中出现了一些迷幻的场景，但《外交官》剧集制片人黛博拉·卡恩表示，本季英国政府的改组是有其现实原因的。

paras.en: “By the time we got to this season, Rory had been prime minister for a period of time where the actual U.K. had like five different people at 10 Downing Street,” Cahn tells The Hollywood Reporter. “And it felt like there was this essential part of being a diplomat, which is that you’re always learning the cast of characters from scratch. You either outlast the people that you’re working with, or you’re sent to a different country. And I wanted to see our team going through the struggle of just when you think you know where the ground is under your feet, it completely changes. You’ve built all these relationships, and suddenly you have nothing.”
paras.zh: “当我们进入这一季时，罗里已经担任首相一段时间了，而真正的英国在唐宁街 10 号就像五个不同的人，”卡恩告诉《好莱坞报道》。 “感觉作为一名外交官有一个重要的部分，那就是你总是从头开始学习角色。你要么比和你一起工作的人活得更久，要么你被派到另一个国家。我想看到我们的团队经历挣扎，当你认为你知道脚下的地面在哪里时，它就完全改变了。你建立了所有这些关系，突然间你一无所有。”

paras.en: Cahn was also interested in showing what it would mean for Keri Russell‘s American ambassador to the U.K. to no longer have to work with someone like Trowbridge.
paras.zh: 卡恩还想展示克里·拉塞尔 (Keri Russell) 的美国驻英国大使不再需要与特罗布里奇这样的人合作意味着什么。

paras.en: “I also really wanted to play with the dynamic of like, you think you’re working with somebody who’s difficult and they’re the problem, and then they leave, and it turns out you were the problem or both of you were the problem,” she says.
paras.zh: “我也很想玩弄这样的动态，你认为你正在和一个很难相处的人一起工作，他们就是问题所在，然后他们离开了，结果发现你就是问题所在，或者你们俩都是问题，”她说。

paras.en: Cahn gave Kinnear a heads-up that his character would be resigning at some point in season four, but the specifics around his departure didn’t emerge until the actor received an unusual request while he was boarding a flight to Lithuania.
paras.zh: 卡恩向金尼尔发出了警告，称他的角色将在第四季的某个时刻辞职，但直到金尼尔在登上飞往立陶宛的航班时收到一个不寻常的请求后，有关他离开的具体细节才浮出水面。

paras.en: “I got a message from Deb saying, ‘Do you think you’d be able to sing this?’ And she sent me the aria,” Kinnear recalls. “And I thought, ‘Why on earth would I be required to do that?’ And I said, ‘I think I could, but how did you know I could sing?’ And she said, “Do you remember it? I think it was at the beginning of season two, there was a funeral in St Paul’s Cathedral, and the whole congregation was asked to sing a hymn and I could hear your voice.’ I thought, ‘Interesting.’ And she’d obviously held on to that for two and a half seasons and brought it back. So I thought, ‘OK, how does that fit into why he might be resigning?'”
paras.zh: “我收到黛布发来的信息，‘你觉得你能唱这首歌吗？’然后她把咏叹调发给了我，”金尼尔回忆道。 “我想，‘到底为什么我会被要求这样做？’我说，‘我想我可以，但你怎么知道我会唱歌？’她说，“你还记得吗？我想那是在第二季开始的时候，圣保罗大教堂举行了一场葬礼，全体会众被要求唱一首赞美诗，我能听到你的声音。’我想，‘有趣。’显然她已经坚持了两个半季，然后又把它带回来了。所以我想，‘好吧，这与他辞职的原因有何关系？’”

paras.en: Trowbridge’s resignation is immediately preceded by Russell’s Kate blackmailing him by telling the newly appointed British foreign secretary Robyn Palmer (Abigail Marlowe), as Trowbridge looks on, about Roylin’s involvement in the carrier ship attack that kicked off the series and how Trowbridge “tried to kill” Roylin when he learned what she’d done.
paras.zh: 就在特罗布里奇辞职之前，拉塞尔扮演的凯特向新任命的英国外交大臣罗宾·帕尔默（阿比盖尔·马洛饰）勒索了他，特罗布里奇在一旁看着，罗伊林参与了引发该系列的航母袭击事件，以及特罗布里奇在得知罗伊林的所作所为后如何“试图杀死”罗伊林。

paras.en: The risky move is, unsurprisingly, Hal’s (Rufus Sewell) idea and though Kate initially resists his “mafioso”-like approach to foreign policy, she ends up doing what he suggested.
paras.zh: 不出所料，这一冒险举动是哈尔（卢夫斯·休厄尔饰）的主意，尽管凯特一开始抵制他“黑手党”式的外交政策方针，但她最终还是按照他的建议做了。

paras.en: “I just think [Trowbridge] makes her crazy. I think he pushed her buttons,” Russell says of why Kate threatens him after he said, in part, that she and Hal won’t be invited to Dennison’s funeral. “He knew how to get her riled up and make it personal, and it’s too fresh. She’s doing something she doesn’t want to do anyway. She doesn’t believe in it, and then he’s attacking her when she hasn’t processed something.”
paras.zh: “我只是觉得[特罗布里奇]让她发疯了。我认为他触怒了她，”拉塞尔谈到为什么凯特在他部分地说她和哈尔不会被邀请参加丹尼森的葬礼后威胁他。 “他知道如何激怒她，并将其变得针对个人，这太新鲜了。她正在做一些她不想做的事情。她不相信它，然后当她还没有处理某些事情时，他就攻击她。”

paras.en: The shake-up also meant Gyasi and Kinnear would be leaving the Netflix series on which they’d been central castmembers for the past few years, a disappointing development for Cahn and the show’s remaining cast.
paras.zh: 这次人事变动还意味着吉亚西和金尼尔将离开 Netflix 的这部剧，过去几年他们一直是该剧的核心演员，这对卡恩和该剧的其余演员来说是一个令人失望的进展。

paras.en: “We wanted to keep Dave Gyasi and Rory Kinnear forever,” Cahn says. “I wish I could see them every day. It’s a bummer when the company shifts in some way. We’ve had the luxury of bringing a lot of people in, and sometimes the story is ejecting people out on the other end, and it sucks.”
paras.zh: “我们希望永远保留戴夫·吉亚西和罗里·金尼尔，”卡恩说。 “我希望每天都能见到他们。当公司以某种方式发生转变时，这真是令人沮丧。我们有幸引进了很多人，但有时故事的另一端却把人们赶了出去，这很糟糕。”

paras.en: Sewell adds that Dennison’s death and Trowbridge resigning are “tremendously shocking.”
paras.zh: 休厄尔补充说，丹尼森的去世和特罗布里奇的辞职“非常令人震惊”。

paras.en: For Kate, though, Russell says the loss of Dennison, with whom she had a close relationship (the show teased the possibility of a romance early on, culminating in a passionate kiss in season three) is “really hard.”
paras.zh: 不过，对于凯特来说，拉塞尔表示，失去与她有着密切关系的丹尼森（该剧一开始就戏弄了恋爱的可能性，并在第三季中以热烈的吻达到了高潮）“真的很难受”。

paras.en: “I think what that does to Kate is really hard, especially at this moment when her morals are being put to the test because he was such a moral character, so I think that fuels all of those doubts,” she says. “And then you have Hal on the other line going, ‘This is what you got to do. You got to do this.’ It’s an enormous loss for the show, for a lot of people who loved him, too. But it’s good storytelling ultimately.”
paras.zh: “我认为这对凯特来说真的很难，尤其是在她的道德受到考验的时刻，因为他的道德品质很高，所以我认为这加剧了所有这些怀疑，”她说。 “然后哈尔在另一条线上说，‘这就是你必须做的。你必须这样做。’这对这部剧来说是一个巨大的损失，对很多爱他的人来说也是如此。但最终这是一个很好的故事讲述。”

paras.en: Kinnear, while sad that he won’t get to keep working with his Diplomat colleagues, is confident the bonds he’s forged with them will continue after he’s left the show. And he’d be happy to return in a guest capacity.
paras.zh: 金尼尔虽然对无法继续与《外交官》同事们一起工作感到难过，但他相信，在他离开节目后，他与他们建立的联系将继续下去。他很乐意以嘉宾身份回归。

paras.en: “I’d be fascinated to see where Trowbridge does end up,” he says. “There are so many different roles that a retired politician finds themselves in, and I’m sure he wouldn’t spend the rest of his life lying low.”
paras.zh: “我很想知道特罗布里奇最终会走向何方，”他说。 “一位退休的政治家发现自己扮演了很多不同的角色，我相信他不会在余生中低调度过。”

paras.en: Speaking with The Hollywood Reporter, Kinnear opens up about why Trowbridge resigns; how his character feels about Dennison’s death, as the two had a complicated relationship; and the experience of filming his final episode.
paras.zh: 金尼尔在接受《好莱坞报道》采访时谈到了特罗布里奇辞职的原因；他的角色对丹尼森的死有何感想，因为两人的关系很复杂；以及拍摄最后一集的经历。

paras.en: What was your reaction when you found out that this is what would be unfolding for your character?
paras.zh: 当你发现这就是你的角色将要发生的事情时，你的反应是什么？

paras.en: I got a heads up from Deb that at some point during the series, Trowbridge will be resigning, and I’ve already felt pretty lucky to have stayed on for as long as I have, given the nature of British politics over the last six or seven years. To finally receive the script, to see, as is typical of Debora’s writing, the psychological acuity she was going to bring to it, and how much she wanted to explore his inner life at the point of his greatest crisis. I sort of knew then that it was going to be a real gift for me as as an actor to be able to to bring that to life.
paras.zh: 我从黛布那里得到提醒，在这个系列赛的某个时刻，特罗布里奇将辞职，考虑到过去六七年英国政治的性质，我已经感到非常幸运，能坚持这么久。最终收到剧本，就像黛博拉写作的典型一样，看到她将给剧本带来的心理敏锐度，以及她在他最严重的危机时刻有多么想探索他的内心生活。那时我就​​知道，作为一名演员，能够将这一点变为现实，这对我来说将是一份真正的礼物。

paras.en: How do you feel about about having to leave the show and the people that you were working with for a number of seasons?
paras.zh: 对于不得不离开这部剧以及与你共事了好几季的人，你有何感受？

paras.en: Well, luckily, when you do a job for as long as this has been — a lot of the time we were hosting our American friends in London, and then luckily they got to return the favor when we were filming in New York — we’re in and out of each other’s lives to such an extent that we knew that we had formed these lifelong friendships. So while it’s obviously sad that I won’t be able to get to go to work with them. I know that I’ll still be able to hang out with them whenever they’re in town or I’m in their town. To have been able to be part of a series that is so smart, so funny, so dramatic, so psychologically aware and so incredibly well-written and -cast is one thing. But to have left with a load of lifelong friends is far too great.
paras.zh: 好吧，幸运的是，当你从事一份工作这么长时间时——很多时候我们在伦敦招待我们的美国朋友，然后幸运的是，当我们在纽约拍摄时他们得到了回报——我们在彼此的生活中进进出出，以至于我们知道我们已经形成了这些终生的友谊。因此，虽然我无法和他们一起工作，这显然令人难过。我知道只要他们在城里或者我在他们的城里，我仍然可以和他们一起出去玩。能够成为如此聪明、如此有趣、如此戏剧性、如此具有心理意识、如此出色的编剧和演员阵容的系列剧的一部分是一回事。但带着一大堆终生的朋友离开，实在是太伟大了。

paras.en: What was it like filming that very surreal episode in which Trowbridge resigns, with the Margaret Roylin hallucinations? That’s such a different approach for this show.
paras.zh: 拍摄特罗布里奇辞职、玛格丽特·罗伊林幻觉的超现实情节是什么感觉？对于这个节目来说，这是一个非常不同的方法。

paras.en: What was exciting about it was that you knew that it was a new flavor. Shows like this, they constantly have to reinvent themselves or show new aspects of themselves, and a character that has loomed as large as Trowbridge has over the four seasons, to be able to get into what really sort of drives him, what makes him tick and to see what what it meant to him to be prime minister, to see what losing that meant to him, what destruction it wreaked him, and how he thought he might be seen both as a king and as a clown and that he’d sort of straddled both roles in his prime ministership, and that we get to see them played out for for real, as it were, within this kind of wild dream life.
paras.zh: 令人兴奋的是你知道这是一种新口味。像这样的节目，他们不断地重塑自己或展示自己的新方面，以及一个像特罗布里奇一样在四个赛季中脱颖而出的角色，能够深入了解他真正的动力是什么，是什么让他兴奋，并了解担任首相对他意味着什么，了解失败对他意味着什么，它给他造成了什么样的破坏，以及他如何认为自己可能会被视为国王和小丑，并且他有点横跨两者在他的首相任期内，我们可以看到这些角色在这种狂野的梦想生活中真实地发挥出来。

paras.en: We never really get a concrete explanation from Trowbridge about why he resigned. How much do you think Kate’s blackmail threat prompted his resignation? What do you think it was really due to?
paras.zh: 我们从未真正从特罗布里奇那里得到关于他辞职原因的具体解释。您认为凯特的勒索威胁在多大程度上促使他辞职？你认为这到底是因为什么？

paras.en: Well, I mean, I do think that most politicians have a sort of self-awareness about how they how they can present themselves or how they can operate and what constitutes a line in the sand for something they wouldn’t be able to to go on with. And I think knowing how compromised he would be, particularly in his relationship with America, and how complicated he had been with that, with this new information in their hands, I think he knew: There’s nothing I can do without feeling I’ll be limping on. I won’t be able to do it with the gusto that I feel like I’ve been able to operate for as long as he has been prime minister. I also think events catch up with people, and it caught up with him what happened with Roylin and at the very beginning of season one, and sometimes people’s appetite goes for the the hurly burly of politics, and I think everyone knows that you’re a long time retired and resigned once you leave it so you keep on going, keep on going because there’s nothing quite like it in terms of the status that you’re afforded, in terms of the decisions you get to make, in terms of just the day-to-day excitement of it, but when it’s time to to step away, it must be sort of crashingly obvious, and I think that’s why he leaps to resignation.
paras.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我确实认为大多数政客都有一种自我意识，知道他们如何展示自己或如何运作，以及什么构成了他们无法继续做的事情的底线。我认为，知道他会做出多么妥协，特别是在他与美国的关系方面，以及他对此感到多么复杂，有了他们手中的这些新信息，我想他知道：我无能为力，除非我感觉自己会一瘸一拐地前进。我将无法像他担任首相期间那样充满热情地开展工作。我还认为事件会吸引人们，他会被罗伊林和第一季一开始发生的事情吸引住，有时人们的胃口是为了喧嚣的政治，我想每个人都知道你已经退休很长时间了，一旦离开就辞职了，所以你继续前进，继续前进，因为就你所获得的地位而言，就你要做的决定而言，就就而言，没有什么比这更好的了。日复一日的兴奋，但当需要离开时，它一定是非常明显的，我认为这就是他突然辞职的原因。

paras.en: We also find out at the end of the previous episode that Austin Dennison (David Gyasi) has died. How does Trowbridge feel about that? He and Dennison had a complicated relationship.
paras.zh: 我们还在上一集的结尾发现奥斯汀·丹尼森（大卫·吉亚西饰）已经去世。特罗布里奇对此有何感想？他和丹尼森的关系很复杂。

paras.en: That’s, I think, definitely another reason that pushes him towards the resignation. They had come up together. They had been adversaries together, but they had found a use for each other as well in the highest echelons of politics. So, to have lost Roylin, to then lose Dennison. Those were the good cop and bad cop on his shoulder, or the devil and the angel on his shoulder, throughout his time. So, I think he felt completely settled as to where he would turn. Lydia obviously provides some support, ballast and encouragement, determination for him. But without Dennison and without Roylin, there was there was an instability to how he saw himself.
paras.zh: 我认为，这绝对是促使他辞职的另一个原因。他们是一起上来的。他们曾是对手，但他们也在政治最高层找到了彼此的用处。所以，失去了罗伊林，然后失去了丹尼森。在他的一生中，这些都是他肩上的好警察和坏警察，或者是他肩上的魔鬼和天使。所以，我认为他对于自己的方向已经完全确定了。莉迪亚显然为他提供了一些支持、镇定和鼓励、决心。但如果没有丹尼森和罗伊林，他对自己的看法就会变得不稳定。

paras.en: Do you have a favorite memory or scene from playing Nicol Trowbridge in The Diplomat?
paras.zh: 您在《外交官》中扮演尼科尔·特罗布里奇时有最喜欢的记忆或场景吗？

paras.en: Driving up in that Jag outside the big country house, in the first [season], you thought, oh yeah, this is going to be fun. This show’s got something about it. Getting to film in St Paul’s Cathedral, getting to film in all those amazing locations. We’re up in the foreign office, and there were times where you felt — I see why people in the top echelons of power try and cling on because traveling in big motorcades or helicopters, all the ceremony of it, you can see how it can go to people’s heads and become quite addicted. I’ve made sure that I kept my feet on the ground, but you could see, particularly with a Netflix-style budget affording you. I’m sure it’s not all as quite as grand and as glamorous, being prime minister, but it certainly felt it at times. And I always remember turning the corner dressed in full crown and coronation robes and singing an aria straight down the camera, and I don’t think the crew had any idea what was going on or why I was doing that or dressed like that.
paras.zh: 在第一季中，你开着那辆捷豹车来到乡间别墅外，你会想，哦，是的，这会很有趣。这个节目有一些关于它的东西。在圣保罗大教堂拍摄，在所有那些令人惊叹的地点拍摄。我们在外交部，有时候你会感觉到——我明白为什么权力高层的人会试图坚持下去，因为乘坐大型车队或直升机旅行，所有这些仪式，你可以看到它如何进入人们的头脑并变得相当上瘾。我确保我脚踏实地，但你可以看到，特别是在你有 Netflix 式的预算的情况下。我确信担任首相并不那么宏伟和迷人，但有时确实有这种感觉。我总是记得穿着皇冠和加冕长袍转过拐角，直接对着镜头唱着咏叹调，我不认为工作人员知道发生了什么，也不知道我为什么要这么做或穿成那样。
