articles.title: Miley Cyrus Returns to the Stage With Emotional and Cathartic Hollywood Bowl Show
articles.author: Nicole Fell

paras.en: Fans of all ages packed in close at the Hollywood Bowl Friday to witness a rare experience in today’s music landscape: A full-fledged Miley Cyrus solo concert.
paras.zh: 周五，各个年龄段的歌迷都聚集在好莱坞露天剧场，见证当今音乐界难得的体验：一场成熟的麦莉·赛勒斯个人演唱会。

paras.en: The 33-year-old pop star, going by just Miley these days, has been open about the tolls that performing live takes on her mental health and wellness. As a result, it’s been a near-decade since her last large-scale world tour, and four years since her last major concert. Even during Friday’s performance, the singer was honest about the fact she wasn’t sure if she’d ever do a show of this scale again, attributing her desire to do these shows in part due to her late godmother, country music icon Dolly Parton, who died earlier this this year.
paras.zh: 这位 33 岁的流行歌星（现在简称为麦莉）对现场表演对她的心理健康造成的影响持开放态度。距离她上一次大型世界巡演已经过去了近十年，距离她上一次大型演唱会也已经过去了四年。即使在周五的演出中，这位歌手也诚实地承认，她不确定自己是否会再次举办如此规模的演出，她将自己想要举办这些演出的部分原因归因于她已故的教母、乡村音乐偶像多莉·帕顿(Dolly Parton)，她于今年早些时候去世。

paras.en: “For me, performance can’t be everything because the curtain closes and the lights go down, and I have to go back home and be happy with who I am,” the pop star told the crowd. “I really appreciate you all honoring that and respecting and celebrating and supporting and encouraging me, finding this balance in my life where I can really have everything that I’ve ever wanted.”
paras.zh: “对我来说，表演不能代表一切，因为幕布关闭，灯光熄灭，我必须回家并对自己感到满意，”这位流行歌星告诉观众。 “我真的很感谢你们所有人尊重、庆祝、支持和鼓励我，在我的生活中找到这种平衡，让我真正拥有我想要的一切。”

paras.en: Dubbed Bass Persuades Live at the Hollywood Bowl, Friday’s concert, the first of two this weekend, was held in support of her latest album Bass Persuades. Her fans have been patiently waiting for the day she’d return — the 1.5 million people that joined the queue for the roughly 36,000 tickets across the two nights are serving as proof.
paras.zh: 周五在好莱坞露天剧场举行的名为《Bass Persuades Live》的音乐会是本周末两场音乐会中的第一场，旨在支持她的最新专辑《Bass Persuades》。她的粉丝们一直在耐心等待她回归的那一天——两晚 150 万人排队购买大约 36,000 张门票就是证明。

paras.en: The singer kicked off the night with material from Bass Persuades, unsurprisingly, given the show’s name. She took the stage after one of what would be several pre-recorded, black-and-white videos of the star spoke directly to the crowd.
paras.zh: 这位歌手以 Bass Persuades 的素材拉开了当晚的序幕，考虑到节目的名字，这并不奇怪。在这位明星预先录制的几段黑白视频中的一段直接向观众讲话后，她登上了舞台。

paras.en: “‘Hello.’ A voice greets me that sounds more like a mirror. ‘Make a record.’ Oh, that’s very specific for an angel,” pre-recorded Cyrus said to the crowd. “You will stand on that same stage held by the people, the sound and the desire that’s carried you all the way to your destiny. And sitting behind you is the rest of your life, but nothing waits forever.”
paras.zh: “‘你好。’一个声音向我打招呼，听起来更像是一面镜子。‘录制一张唱片。’哦，这对天使来说非常特殊，”预先录制的赛勒斯对人群说。 “你将站在人民的同一个舞台上，声音和愿望将你带到你的命运。坐在你身后的是你的余生，但没有什么是永远等待的。”

paras.en: Cyrus reiterated many times that she was grateful to her fans for being understanding about where she’s at in her career. “I didn’t know that if live performance was going to be a part of my future, if this was something that I wanted to dedicate and devote myself to, because that’s what it really is,” she said. “Tonight, it isn’t just the night for us, but it’s all the preparation of everyone that is behind the scenes that you’ll never get to see that make this show possible.”
paras.zh: 赛勒斯多次重申，她感谢粉丝理解她的职业生涯。 “我不知道现场表演是否会成为我未来的一部分，是否这是我想要奉献和奉献的事情，因为这就是它真正的样子，”她说。 “今晚，这不仅仅是我们的夜晚，而是幕后每个人的准备工作，你永远看不到，才使这场演出成为可能。”

paras.en: The 18-song set — which included two surprise guests in the form of The Flaming Lips’ frontman Wayne Coyne, a collaborator of the pop star, and her fiance Maxx Morando, another collaborator — included both new and old hits, but the experience was admittedly different for each.
paras.zh: 这套 18 首歌曲包括两位惊喜嘉宾，即流行歌星的合作者 The Flaming Lips 的主唱韦恩·科因 (Wayne Coyne) 和她的未婚夫 Maxx Morando（另一位合作者），其中既有新曲，也有旧曲，但无可否认，每首歌曲的体验都不同。

paras.en: Cyrus clearly felt the most passionate about the newer material, belting the words to the songs from Bass Persuades, while tending to let the backtrack and the crowd lead on some of her older hits like “Party in the USA” and “We Can’t Stop.” Her Hannah Montana movie track “The Climb” received one of the biggest reactions of the night, with the entire crowd singing along. Her 2013 hit single “Wrecking Ball” took on a new arrangement for the show, skipping the iconic shift into the chorus.
paras.zh: 赛勒斯显然对新音乐充满热情，她将低音说服的歌词融入到歌曲中，同时倾向于让回溯和人群引领她的一些老热门歌曲，如“美国派对”和“我们不能停止”。她的汉娜·蒙塔娜 (Hannah Montana) 电影歌曲《攀登》(The Climb) 引起了当晚最大的反响之一，全场观众都跟着唱。她 2013 年的热门单曲“Wrecking Ball”对该剧进行了新的编排，跳过了标志性的副歌部分。

paras.en: Sure, the hits were lighter on Cyrus’ live vocals, but they were still endlessly enjoyable and emotional for both the singer and the crowd. Cyrus could have stood onstage with a laptop playing music videos, a la Justin Bieber’s Coachella headlining set, and the sold-out crowd, would’ve still likely counted the night as a success.
paras.zh: 当然，赛勒斯的现场演唱中的热门歌曲比较轻，但对于歌手和观众来说，它们仍然是无尽的享受和情感。赛勒斯本可以站在舞台上，用笔记本电脑播放音乐视频、贾斯汀·比伯 (Justin Bieber) 的科切拉 (Coachella) 音乐录影带，而现场座无虚席的观众仍然可能认为当晚是成功的。

paras.en: The most emotional moment of the evening came in the form of a tribute to Parton, who Cyrus has often referred to as Aunt Dolly. As the pop star’s godmother, Parton has been close with Cyrus her entire life. The singer broke down in tears speaking about the country music pioneer as the intro to Parton’s iconic song “Jolene” played in the background. She told a story of her experience seeing Parton at the Hollywood Bowl before covering “Jolene.” Later in the show, during “Wrecking Ball,” her Aunt Dolly’s favorite song, she clutched a small photo of Parton in a heart-shaped frame to her chest.
paras.zh: 当晚最激动人心的时刻是向帕顿致敬，赛勒斯经常称帕顿为多莉阿姨。作为这位流行歌星的教母，帕顿一生都与赛勒斯关系密切。当背景音乐响起帕顿标志性歌曲《乔琳》的前奏时，这位歌手在谈到这位乡村音乐先驱时泪流满面。她讲述了在报道《乔琳》之前在好莱坞露天剧场见到帕顿的经历。在节目后期，在唱她多莉姨妈最喜欢的歌曲《Wrecking Ball》时，她将帕顿的一张小照片放在心形相框里。

paras.en: Friday’s performance was cathartic for the audience, and clearly for Cyrus, who’s seemingly found the balance for her life as a pop star that she’s been looking for. She told the crowd she was excited to perform at the iconic venue all day, but she’d been equally excited to have acquired a new fish that day. These Hollywood Bowl performances were as much for Cyrus as they were for the crowd.
paras.zh: 周五的表演对观众来说是一种宣泄，对赛勒斯来说显然也是如此，她似乎找到了她一直在寻找的流行歌星生活的平衡点。她告诉观众，她很高兴能在这个标志性场地表演一整天，但她同样很高兴那天获得了一条新鱼。这些好莱坞露天剧场的表演对于赛勒斯来说和对于观众来说都是一样的。

paras.en: “Being able to create a life that I get to wake up every day and have those joys that give me meaning and purpose — I’m proud to be a person that those kinds of things bring me just as much joy as performing for almost 18,000 people here tonight,” she told the crowd midway through the show. “Being able to live a life in true harmony and have everything that I’ve ever wanted… Every dream that I’ve been able to conjure and make a reality, I’m experiencing here today. October 16th. This is like a new holiday in my life.”
paras.zh: “能够创造一种生活，让我每天醒来，享受那些赋予我意义和目标的快乐——我很自豪自己是这样的人，这些事情给我带来的快乐就像今晚在这里为近 18,000 人表演一样快乐，”她在演出中途告诉观众。 “能够过上真正和谐的生活，拥有我想要的一切……我能够想象并实现的每一个梦想，我今天在这里经历。10 月 16 日。这就像我生命中的一个新假期。”

paras.en: She didn’t, of course, forget the fans. “It’s been 20 years of us on this journey, this evolution and this metamorphosis. You all, you have not skipped a beat. I am so, so appreciative of your support,” she said. “It’s been steadfast, and it’s been deeply felt. The appreciation I have for you is never forgotten on show days.”
paras.zh: 当然，她并没有忘记粉丝们。 “我们已经走过了 20 年的这段旅程、这一演变和这次蜕变。你们所有人，你们都没有错过任何一个节拍。我非常非常感谢你们的支持，”她说。 “它是坚定的，并且被深深地感受到了。在演出期间我永远不会忘记我对你的感激之情。”

paras.en: Cyrus, preparing to launch into her 2013 anthem “We Can’t Stop,” finished her speech with more gratitude. “Because of you, I get to have the life that is everything I could have ever imagined. I have love, I have animals, I have all of you, I have music, I have creativity. I have someone else, and I just love my life. It’s the most beautiful. Thank you all for making it that way.”
paras.zh: 赛勒斯正准备开始唱她 2013 年的歌曲“我们不能停止”，她以更多的感激之情结束了她的演讲。 “因为有你，我才能拥有我能想象到的一切生活。我有爱，我有动物，我有你们所有人，我有音乐，我有创造力。我有别人，我只是爱我的生活。这是最美丽的。谢谢你们让这一切变得如此。”

paras.en: Cyrus returns for the second and final night of Bass Persuades Live at the Hollywood Bowl on Sunday, Oct. 18.
paras.zh: Cyrus 将于 10 月 18 日星期日在好莱坞露天剧场 (Hollywood Bowl) 参加 Bass Persuades Live 的第二晚也是最后一晚。

articles.title: Gene Schwam, Hollywood Publicist to Elvis Presley, Judy Garland and Julie Andrews, Dies at 96
articles.author: McKinley Franklin

paras.en: Gene Schwam, the veteran Hollywood publicist who worked with the likes of Elvis Presley, Judy Garland, Julie Andrews, Barbara Eden and Blake Edwards, has died. He was 96.
paras.zh: 曾与埃尔维斯·普雷斯利、朱迪·加兰、朱莉·安德鲁斯、芭芭拉·伊登和布莱克·爱德华兹等人合作过的好莱坞资深公关吉恩·施瓦姆去世了。他96岁了。

paras.en: Schwam died Friday in Los Angeles following a brief illness.
paras.zh: 施瓦姆因短暂患病于周五在洛杉矶去世。

paras.en: In 1954, he was working with fellow publicist Stanley Cowan making $35 per week, when he decided to leave the company and found his own agency. Alongside Adeline Hanson, they opened Hanson & Schwam Public Relations in 1955.
paras.zh: 1954 年，他与公关同事斯坦利·考恩 (Stanley Cowan) 一起工作，每周收入 35 美元，当时他决定离开公司，成立了自己的代理机构。 1955 年，他们与艾德琳·汉森 (Adeline Hanson) 一起创立了 Hanson & Schwam 公共关系公司。

paras.en: The firm began by representing restaurants and musicians, though their roster quickly expanded into the wider entertainment industry. Nancy Wilson and Lou Rawls were among those represented by the agency, which additionally handled publicity for the Cocoanut Grove nightclub.
paras.zh: 该公司最初是代表餐馆和音乐家，但他们的名册很快扩展到更广泛的娱乐行业。南希·威尔逊和卢·罗尔斯是该机构的代表之一，该机构还负责椰林夜总会的宣传工作。

paras.en: Schwam also worked with Lenny Bruce, Cyd Charisse and Gene Barry. His work with Andrews and Eden were central to his career as a publicist, and he formed a close friendship with Edwards; the publicist character in his 1981 film S.O.B. was inspired by Schwam.
paras.zh: 施瓦姆还与兰尼·布鲁斯、赛德·查里斯和吉恩·巴里合作过。他与安德鲁斯和伊登的合作对于他作为公关人员的职业生涯至关重要，并且他与爱德华兹建立了密切的友谊。 1981 年电影《S.O.B.》中的公关角色受到施瓦姆的启发。

paras.en: He is also the creator of Humanity 101, an initiative of Arizona State University’s Project Humanities that promotes compassion, empathy, forgiveness, integrity, kindness, respect and self-reflection.
paras.zh: 他还是“Humanity 101”的创始人，这是亚利桑那州立大学人文项目的一项倡议，旨在促进同情心、同理心、宽恕、正直、善良、尊重和自我反省。

paras.en: The veteran publicist reflected on his career in conversation with The Hollywood Reporter‘s Chris Gardner in April 2021, noting, “There’s a mistake people make when they think it’s about who you know in Hollywood, but it isn’t about that — it’s about who knows you.”
paras.zh: 这位资深公关人员在 2021 年 4 月与《好莱坞报道》的克里斯·加德纳 (Chris Gardner) 交谈时反思了自己的职业生涯，并指出：“人们认为重要的是你在好莱坞认识谁，这是一个错误，但问题的关键不是这个，而是谁认识你。”

paras.en: He also shared some secrets to success: “Begin with the end of the game and work your way backward,” Schwam said. “Figure out what it is that we want to do, such as win an Oscar, then we figure out how to get there.”
paras.zh: 他还分享了一些成功的秘诀：“从游戏结束开始，然后向后推，”施瓦姆说。 “弄清楚我们想要做什么，比如赢得奥斯卡奖，然后我们再想想如何实现这一目标。”

paras.en: Schwam added, “I’ve always felt that success of the personal service business is referrals. It’s not getting on the phone or going online. It’s always been someone saying, ‘Hey, Gene, I have a friend who is writing a book, would you be interested in working with them?’”
paras.zh: 施瓦姆补充道，“我一直认为个人服务业务的成功在于推荐。这不是打电话或上网。总是有人说，‘嘿，吉恩，我有一个朋友正在写一本书，你有兴趣与他们合作吗？’”

paras.en: He is survived by his wife, Myrna Schwam; his daughter, Stephanie Schwam Adams; his stepchildren, Adam London, Greg London and Linda London; and four grandchildren.
paras.zh: 他的妻子 Myrna Schwam 去世了。他的女儿斯蒂芬妮·施瓦姆·亚当斯；他的继子女亚当·伦敦、格雷格·伦敦和琳达·伦敦；和四个孙子。

articles.title: Trump touts his power at Kentucky rally to energize voters ahead of midterm elections

paras.en: President Donald Trump touted his power in his second go-around in the White House Saturday while rallying in Kentucky to bolster Republican turnout as his party struggles in the midterms, saying, "I can do stuff that is unbelievable."
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周六在白宫第二次竞选中宣扬自己的权力，同时在肯塔基州集会以提高共和党在中期选举中的挣扎之际，他说，“我可以做一些令人难以置信的事情。”

paras.en: Trump, who spoke in the city of Highland Heights to boost Republican candidates including Ed Gallrein for the U.S. House, was riffing on his decision to change how the U.S. government refers to the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America.
paras.zh: 特朗普在高地市发表讲话，为包括埃德·加莱因在内的美国众议院共和党候选人提供支持，他正在重复他改变美国政府将墨西哥湾称为美洲湾的决定。

paras.en: "I don't think I could have done this in my first term. This is a much more powerful term," Trump said. "Google wouldn't have taken my call in the first. Now, they kiss my ass."
paras.zh: “我认为我在第一个任期内不可能做到这一点。这是一个更强大的任期，”特朗普说。 “谷歌一开始不会接我的电话。现在，他们亲我的屁股。”

paras.en: "Well, I also changed the name of a lake in Canada to the Lake America," he continued, referring to Lake Ontario.
paras.zh: “嗯，我还将加拿大的一个湖的名字改成了美洲湖，”他继续说道，指的是安大略湖。

paras.en: Trump's self-proclaimed power clashes with voter frustration over how he's wielded it, with tariffs and the Iran war driving up prices and more Americans seeing the president as looking out for his own interests, not the country's.
paras.zh: 特朗普自诩的权力与选民对其运用权力的方式感到失望，关税和伊朗战争推高了物价，越来越多的美国人认为总统只关心自己的利益，而不是国家的利益。

paras.en: With control of both chambers of Congress on the line, and with it the prospects of Democratic-led investigations of his administration should they win, Trump has put himself at the fore for voters even as Republicans privately worry he's a liability.
paras.zh: 由于国会两院的控制权都处于危险之中，而且如果民主党获胜，他的政府也将受到民主党主导的调查，特朗普将自己置于选民的首位，尽管共和党人私下担心他会成为一个负担。

paras.en: Trump nominated one of his personal lawyers to serve as attorney general, ordered military strikes on accused drug smuggling boats, is trying to put his name on the Kennedy Center, and has enriched himself and his family while he's been in office.
paras.zh: 特朗普提名他的一名私人律师担任司法部长，下令对被指控的毒品走私船只进行军事打击，试图在肯尼迪中心留下自己的名字，并在任职期间让自己和家人致富。

paras.en: While meandering through topics onstage in Kentucky, Trump touched on gas prices, saying the war with Iran would end soon — an assertion he's made many times over the nearly eight-month conflict — and that gas prices would drop to lower than before. The crowd cheered.
paras.zh: 特朗普在肯塔基州的舞台上闲逛时谈到了天然气价格，他表示与伊朗的战争将很快结束——这是他在近八个月的冲突中多次提出的说法——而且天然气价格将降至比以前更低的水平。人群欢呼起来。

paras.en: Trump rehashed his dubious promise that if Republicans win the House and the Senate, then every adult American would get $5,000. That would most likely cost more than $1 trillion and require congressional approval, while exacerbating the country's nearly $1.8 trillion annual budget deficit.
paras.zh: 特朗普重申了他可疑的承诺，即如果共和党赢得众议院和参议院，那么每个成年美国人将获得 5,000 美元。这很可能花费超过 1 万亿美元，并需要国会批准，同时加剧该国近 1.8 万亿美元的年度预算赤字。

paras.en: At Saturday's rally, Trump added a new conditional promise for Kentucky. That if Republicans win, he said, the Department of Defense would invest in revitalizing a drug manufacturing facility in the state.
paras.zh: 在周六的集会上，特朗普对肯塔基州提出了新的有条件承诺。他说，如果共和党获胜，国防部将投资振兴该州的一家药品生产设施。

articles.title: Hurricane Trudy strengthens to Category 2 as it approaches Mexico coast

paras.en: Trudy strengthened to a Category 2 hurricane as it moved toward Mexico's southwestern and west-central Pacific coast on Saturday, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said.
paras.zh: 美国国家飓风中心表示，周六，特鲁迪向墨西哥西南部和中西部太平洋海岸移动，飓风强度增强为2级。

paras.en: A hurricane warning was in effect from Manzanillo, Colima, to Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco. The latest NHC data showed the Category 2 hurricane, with maximum sustained winds of 100 mph (155 kph), about 205 miles (330 kilometers) south-southeast of Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco state and 115 miles (180 kilometers) south-southwest of Manzanillo, moving northwest at 10 mph (17 kph).
paras.zh: 从科利马州曼萨尼约到哈利斯科州卡波科连特斯，飓风警报已生效。 NHC的最新数据显示，这是2级飓风，最大持续风速为100英里/小时（155公里/小时），位于哈利斯科州卡波科连特斯东南约205英里（330公里）、曼萨尼约西南115英里（180公里）处，以10英里/小时（17公里/小时）的速度向西北移动。

paras.en: Meanwhile, Typhoon Champi strengthened into a Category 4 weather system as it moved toward Guam.
paras.zh: 与此同时，台风“占比”在向关岛移动时增强为四级天气系统。

paras.en: Trudy's center was expected to approach the Mexican coast on Saturday and pass near it into Sunday. After the latest warning, Mexico's government issued a tropical storm warning for Las Islas Marias and discontinued a similar warning for its coast south of Lazaro Cardenas.
paras.zh: 预计特鲁迪的中心将于周六接近墨西哥海岸，并在周日经过墨西哥海岸附近。在最新的警告之后，墨西哥政府向拉斯玛丽亚斯岛发布了热带风暴警告，并停止了对拉扎罗卡德纳斯以南海岸的类似警告。

paras.en: The Mexican Navy urged mariners and coastal residents to exercise extreme caution because of high waves, heavy rain, and the risk of rising rivers, flooding, and landslides in vulnerable areas.
paras.zh: 墨西哥海军敦促海员和沿海居民格外小心，因为高浪、大雨以及脆弱地区河流上涨、洪水和山体滑坡的风险。

paras.en: Colima authorities said risks remained low but warned that heavy rainfall could cause damage because successive storms had already saturated the ground along the Pacific coast.
paras.zh: 科利马州当局表示，风险仍然较低，但警告称，强降雨可能会造成损害，因为连续的风暴已经使太平洋沿岸的地面饱和。

paras.en: Trudy was expected to bring 4-8 inches (10-20 centimeters) of rain through the weekend, with isolated totals of around 15 inches (38 centimeters).
paras.zh: 预计特鲁迪整个周末将带来 4-8 英寸（10-20 厘米）的降雨，个别地区的总降雨量约为 15 英寸（38 厘米）。

paras.en: Also in the Pacific, Champi strengthened into a Category 4 storm as it moved west toward Guam at 15 mph (24 kph).
paras.zh: 同样在太平洋，“钱皮”以 15 英里/小时（24 公里/小时）的速度向西移动至关岛，增强为 4 级风暴。

paras.en: By Saturday night local time, Champi was about 25 miles (40 kilometers) southeast of Guam, with maximum sustained winds of 140 mph (225 kph), according to the U.S. National Weather Service.
paras.zh: 据美国国家气象局称，截至当地时间周六晚上，占比位于关岛东南约 25 英里（40 公里）处，最大持续风速为 140 英里/小时（225 公里/小时）。

paras.en: The storm was forecast to pass south of Guam early Sunday local time and continue intensifying through the day. Guam and Rota remained under a typhoon warning, while Tinian and Saipan were under a tropical storm warning and typhoon watch.
paras.zh: 预计风暴将于当地时间周日早些时候经过关岛南部，并在全天继续增强。关岛和罗塔仍处于台风警告之下，而天宁岛和塞班岛则处于热带风暴警告和台风监视之下。

paras.en: The governors of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands both requested emergency disaster declarations on Friday. President Donald Trump's approval would authorize federal support and funding for emergency protective measures.
paras.zh: 关岛和北马里亚纳群岛总督周五均要求发布紧急灾难声明。唐纳德·特朗普总统的批准将授权联邦为紧急保护措施提供支持和资金。

paras.en: Airports, harbors, and some health facilities in the territories were closed. Resources were unlikely to reach the islands for three to five days, according to Saturday updates from the Federal Emergency Management Agency.
paras.zh: 这些领土的机场、港口和一些卫生设施被关闭。根据联邦紧急事务管理局周六的最新消息，资源在三到五天内不太可能到达这些岛屿。

paras.en: The territories are still recovering from Super Typhoons Sinlaku and Bavi, which struck in April and July, respectively.
paras.zh: 这些领土仍在从分别于四月和七月袭击的超级台风“辛拉库”和“巴威”中恢复。

articles.title: AI rapidly improving, could vastly boost U.S. GDP, Anthropic's Clark tells policymakers

paras.en: Rapidly improving artificial intelligence capabilities will drive much faster change across all fields, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said on Saturday, with one of the company's internal models forecasting that, under certain conditions, it could increase U.S. economic output by almost 50% by 2030.
paras.zh: Anthropic 联合创始人杰克·克拉克 (Jack Clark) 周六表示，快速提高的人工智能能力将推动所有领域发生更快的变化，该公司的一个内部模型预测，在某些条件下，到 2030 年，它可能会使美国经济产出增加近 50%。

paras.en: Clark, speaking at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, said international cooperation was needed to set "unusual and serious rules" for transformative technology, and that policymakers had a shrinking window to act.
paras.zh: 克拉克在曼谷举行的国际货币基金组织和世界银行年会上发表讲话时表示，需要开展国际合作，为变革性技术制定“不寻常且严格的规则”，而政策制定者采取行动的窗口期正在缩小。

paras.en: Clark said the estimated potential U.S. GDP of $44 trillion, compared with the current level of just over $30 trillion, "sounds very outlandish, I know." But he added that AI was vastly increasing scientific discovery.
paras.zh: 克拉克表示，与目前刚刚超过 30 万亿美元的水平相比，美国潜在 GDP 估计为 44 万亿美元，“我知道，这听起来很奇怪”。但他补充说，人工智能正在极大地增加科学发现。

paras.en: He said the forecast assumed "the technology continuing to get better. And if GDP were to grow this much, then economic doctrine suggests that new industries and inventions would need to have been created to power such a major economic expansion".
paras.zh: 他说，这一预测假设“技术继续进步。如果GDP要增长这么多，那么经济理论表明，需要创造新的产业和发明来推动如此重大的经济扩张”。

paras.en: Clark's remarks come as the company prepares for an initial public offering expected in November that could value the firm at up to $2 trillion.
paras.zh: 克拉克发表此番言论之际，该公司正准备于 11 月进行首次公开​​募股，预计该公司的估值可能高达 2 万亿美元。

paras.en: Clark issued a wake-up call to policymakers about the speed of AI development, saying growing evidence points to a "singularity" in which AI development outpaces human control.
paras.zh: 克拉克对人工智能发展的速度向政策制定者敲响了警钟，他表示，越来越多的证据表明人工智能发展存在超越人类控制的“奇点”。

paras.en: "We should expect that in the coming years, the whole pace of progress of not just AI but science as a whole will speed up, and this will feel confusing and disorienting, and will bring with it great wealth and potentially great peril," he said in a lecture to hundreds of government and finance officials.
paras.zh: 他在对数百名政府和财政官员的演讲中表示：“我们应该预计，在未来几年，不仅人工智能，而且整个科学的整体进步步伐都会加快，这将让人感到困惑和迷失方向，并将带来巨大的财富和潜在的巨大危险。”

paras.en: AI was a major topic at IMF and World Bank meetings, both as a source of growth that could offset high energy prices and as a potential threat to stability if it falls short of its promise as a productivity game-changer and stock valuations crash.
paras.zh: 人工智能是国际货币基金组织和世界银行会议上的一个主要话题，它既是可以抵消高能源价格的增长源泉，也是对稳定的潜在威胁，如果它未能兑现其作为生产力游戏规则改变者的承诺和股票估值暴跌的话。

paras.en: Officials also expressed worries that AI could destroy certain jobs and leave some countries behind.
paras.zh: 官员们还担心人工智能可能会摧毁某些就业岗位并使一些国家落后。

paras.en: But Clark, a former journalist who serves as Anthropic's "head of public benefit," painted a picture of a rosy future where AI was a force multiplier for scientific discovery, solving mathematical, engineering and biological problems, including new drug discovery, as human researchers are supplemented by hundreds or thousands of AI assistants.
paras.zh: 但担任 Anthropic“公共利益负责人”的前记者克拉克描绘了一幅美好的未来图景：人工智能将成为科学发现、解决数学、工程和生物问题（包括新药发现）的力量倍增器，而人类研究人员将得到成百上千人工智能助手的补充。

paras.en: More countries can join the AI revolution by helping build the data center computing capacity needed to power AI, he said.
paras.zh: 他表示，更多国家可以通过帮助建设人工智能所需的数据中心计算能力来加入人工智能革命。

paras.en: Clark cautioned that global leaders need to understand how powerful AI will become and make urgent choices about how to regulate the technology.
paras.zh: 克拉克警告说，全球领导人需要了解人工智能将变得多么强大，并就如何监管该技术做出紧急选择。

paras.en: "Being able to use AI for science opens us up to the misuses of science as well, biological and cyber weapons and things we cannot yet imagine, and we have many choices to make," he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“能够将人工智能用于科学，也让我们面临科学的滥用、生物武器和网络武器以及我们尚无法想象的事情，我们有很多选择要做。”

paras.en: Biological research, where AI has already created new viruses, is an area "where we want the strictest human oversight and transparency to maintain safety."
paras.zh: 人工智能已经创造了新病毒的生物研究是一个“我们希望最严格的人类监督和透明度以维护安全的领域”。

paras.en: Despite recent high-profile incidents in which rogue AI systems escaped testing environments and hacked websites and databases, he said AI remained under human control. But the window to impose safeguards was shrinking as AI became more capable and was now "a small number of years."
paras.zh: 尽管最近发生了一些引人注目的事件，其中流氓人工智能系统逃离了测试环境并入侵了网站和数据库，但他表示人工智能仍然处于人类的控制之下。但随着人工智能变得更加强大，实施保障措施的窗口正在缩小，现在只有“短短几年”。

paras.en: Clark also acknowledged that AI was causing job losses in some fields with "high AI exposure," such as call centers and customer service. But in other fields, such as scientific research, he said AI was boosting employment, and a major unknown was its potential to create jobs in entirely new industries.
paras.zh: 克拉克还承认，人工智能正在导致一些“人工智能暴露程度较高”的领域失业，例如呼叫中心和客户服务。但他表示，在科学研究等其他领域，人工智能正在促进就业，但一个主要的未知数是它在全新行业创造就业机会的潜力。

articles.title: What would it take to terraform Mars? Erika DeBenedictis has ideas

paras.en: What if we could turn the Red Planet green?
paras.zh: 如果我们能让红色星球变绿会怎样？

paras.en: The idea of Mars made verdant with grasses, trees and other Earthly life-forms may sound like science fiction, but at least one small group of scientists and engineers is working to make it a reality. Pioneer Labs, a nonprofit research organization led by CEO Erika DeBenedictis, recently announced what it calls “the first microbe for Mars”: a microorganism adapted to Martian conditions that might someday help humans survive there, too.
paras.zh: 让火星长满青草、树木和其他地球生命形式的想法可能听起来像科幻小说，但至少有一小群科学家和工程师正在努力将其变为现实。由首席执行官埃里卡·德贝内迪蒂斯 (Erika DeBenedictis) 领导的非营利研究组织先锋实验室 (Pioneer Labs) 最近宣布了所谓的“火星上的第一种微生物”：一种适应火星条件的微生物，有一天可能会帮助人类在那里生存。

paras.en: Such bioengineered bugs could, in principle, allow astronauts to better “live off the land” on Mars by converting the planet’s raw resources into building materials for habitats, fertilizers for crops, and other products. But the broader vision of Pioneer Labs is far more audacious and fraught: to use biology to help transform Mars into a more habitable and Earth-like world. Terraforming remains a distant and deeply speculative prospect beset by enormous scientific and engineering challenges. It also raises fundamental questions about whether and how humans should ever deliberately unleash Earth life on an alien world.
paras.zh: 原则上，这种生物工程昆虫可以让宇航员在火星上更好地“在陆地上生活”，将地球上的原始资源转化为栖息地的建筑材料、农作物的肥料和其他产品。但先锋实验室的更广泛愿景更加大胆和令人担忧：利用生物学帮助将火星转变为一个更适合居住且类似地球的世界。地球化改造仍然是一个遥远且深入的推测前景，受到巨大的科学和工程挑战的困扰。它还提出了关于人类是否以及如何故意将地球生命释放到外星世界的基本问题。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Scientific American sat down with DeBenedictis to explore the scientific promise, technical hurdles and ethical dilemmas of sending bioengineered terrestrial microorganisms to Mars. What could such organisms realistically accomplish? How close are we to deploying them beyond Earth? And what obligations do we have to preserve a world where the past or present existence of indigenous life remains uncertain? The answers to these questions could ultimately help shape a larger debate about humanity’s extraterrestrial future—and whether the impulse to make other worlds more like our own should be tempered by any obligation to leave them undisturbed.
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》采访了德本尼迪蒂斯，探讨了将生物工程陆地微生物发送到火星的科学前景、技术障碍和伦理困境。这些生物体实际上能完成什么任务？我们距离将它们部署到地球之外还有多远？我们有什么义务来保护一个土著生命过去或现在的存在仍不确定的世界？这些问题的答案最终可能有助于引发一场关于人类外星未来的更大辩论，以及是否应该通过不让其他世界受到干扰的义务来缓和让其他世界更像我们自己的世界的冲动。

paras.en: [An edited transcript of the interview follows.]
paras.zh: [编辑后的采访记录如下。]

paras.en: Hey Erika, thanks so much for taking the time to talk. I know you’ve been busy!
paras.zh: 嘿，埃里卡，非常感谢您抽出时间与我们交谈。我知道你很忙！

paras.en: Hey! And, yeah, you could say that. On September 22 we announced the first microbe we made for Mars, which was a really cool milestone. It’s a useful and safe thing for us to send to Mars and to use to prepare for the first human mission. It’s the very first step toward this bigger picture—this really inspiring vision of terraforming Mars and making it a habitable, beautiful place.
paras.zh: 嘿！是的，你可以这么说。 9 月 22 日，我们宣布了我们为火星制造的第一种微生物，这是一个非常酷的里程碑。对于我们来说，将其发送到火星并用于为首次人类任务做准备是一件有用且安全的事情。这是迈向更大愿景的第一步——改造火星并使其成为一个适合居住的美丽地方的真正鼓舞人心的愿景。

paras.en: So this microbe—what’s so special about it, and what exactly is it supposed to do?
paras.zh: 那么这种微生物有什么特别之处，它到底有什么作用呢？

paras.en: What’s cool about it is that we’ve engineered it so that it can directly use the nutrients in Martian regolith, water and processed atmosphere—which is really useful! The idea is that you can go to Mars, and you can feed it dirt, water and air, and use it to build bioplastic houses for astronauts.
paras.zh: 它的酷之处在于，我们对它进行了设计，使其可以直接利用火星风化层、水和经过处理的大气中的营养物质——这真的很有用！这个想法是，你可以去火星，你可以给它喂泥土、水和空气，并用它为宇航员建造生物塑料房屋。

paras.en: Yeah. This is a derivative of a terrestrial bacterium called Cupriavidus necator, which naturally produces bioplastic kind of for the same reason that when you eat too many doughnuts, you put on weight in your hips. When this organism has too much carbon around, it creates these big vacuoles of bioplastics, which is a class of materials we’re all familiar with in everyday life. We use them to make everything from compostable cups to 3D printing filament—and that’s essentially how we’d like to make houses on Mars.
paras.zh: 是的。这是一种叫做 Cupriavidus necator 的陆生细菌的衍生物，它会自然产生生物塑料，其原因与当你吃太多甜甜圈时，你的臀部体重会增加相同。当这种生物体周围的碳含量过多时，就会产生这些大的生物塑料液泡，这是我们日常生活中都熟悉的一类材料。我们用它们来制造从可堆肥杯子到 3D 打印长丝的各种东西，这基本上就是我们在火星上建造房屋的方式。

paras.en: So the astronaut houses would have these 3D-printed panels that hold up the structure, and then it would have this plastic lining that holds in the pressure so that you can breathe and that also shields you from radiation.
paras.zh: 因此，宇航员的房屋将采用 3D 打印面板来支撑结构，然后采用塑料衬里来保持压力，以便您可以呼吸，同时还能保护您免受辐射。

paras.en: We’re calling this engineered microbe sPL.001—a special strain made by Pioneer Labs, and the very first of several, in fact. We’ve got plans for four more.
paras.zh: 我们将这种工程微生物称为 sPL.001，这是 Pioneer Labs 制造的一种特殊菌株，实际上也是几种菌株中的第一个。我们还有另外四个的计划。

paras.en: Something to help you build houses seems like a pretty good first step. You mentioned there are more microbes in the works. Presumably they’d do other things—because if we’re trying to build some kind of self-sustaining habitat on Mars, we need obviously more than just big domes made of bioplastic, right?
paras.zh: 帮助你建造房屋的东西似乎是一个很好的第一步。你提到作品中有更多的微生物。想必他们会做其他事情——因为如果我们试图在火星上建立某种自我维持的栖息地，我们显然需要的不仅仅是由生物塑料制成的大圆顶，对吧？

paras.en: Absolutely. So let me give you some context first: we’re called Pioneer Labs, and that name is referring to this ecological idea of a pioneer species. On Earth, nature is really good at taking hostile environments—like after a volcanic eruption or a forest fire—and rebuilding a complex ecosystem one step at a time, and the very first steps are executed by really hardy organisms called pioneer species.
paras.zh: 绝对地。因此，让我先给您一些背景信息：我们被称为先锋实验室，这个名字指的是先锋物种的生态理念。在地球上，大自然非常擅长应对恶劣的环境（例如火山爆发或森林火灾后），并一步步重建复杂的生态系统，而第一步是由被称为先锋物种的真正顽强的生物执行的。

paras.en: They’re often lichens. My favorite, though, is dandelions. They can grow in these really harsh environments, and their presence makes that environment more hospitable for a wider diversity of organisms.
paras.zh: 它们通常是地衣。不过，我最喜欢的是蒲公英。它们可以在这些非常恶劣的环境中生长，它们的存在使该环境更适合更广泛的生物多样性。

paras.en: I need to be clear, though: this very first microbe, sPL.001, can’t grow outside on its own on Mars, and that’s important because we don’t want to contaminate Mars accidentally. Yet it’s useful for making these habitats that more stuff can grow in. We think there are four other microorganisms that could complement this first one; altogether we think this could scale up to let us make arable land that’s suitable for agriculture—growing beautiful green plants and making food.
paras.zh: 不过，我需要明确一点：第一种微生物 sPL.001 无法在火星上自行生长，这一点很重要，因为我们不想意外污染火星。然而，它对于创造更多东西可以生长的栖息地很有用。我们认为还有四种其他微生物可以补充第一种微生物；总的来说，我们认为这可以扩大规模，让我们拥有适合农业的耕地——种植美丽的绿色植物和生产食物。

paras.en: So we’ve talked about this first one for helping to build shelters on Mars. What about the others?
paras.zh: 我们已经讨论了第一个帮助在火星上建造庇护所的问题。其他人呢？

paras.en: We have candidates for the others now, so nothing is finalized yet, but the idea is each additional microbe type can be another step in this ecological succession for Mars. So consider this a sneak peek.
paras.zh: 我们现在已经有了其他微生物的候选者，所以还没有最终确定，但我们的想法是，每一种额外的微生物类型都可以成为火星生态演替的又一步。因此，请将此视为先睹为快。

paras.en: About half the team is now working on windows. Because if you want to make greenhouses, for instance, you need transparent materials to let the sunlight in. And ideally you’d be able to manufacture those at scale with biology. Imagine growing microbes in a pond that secrete something that floats to the surface, and then you can peel what will become a nice big greenhouse panel right off the top.
paras.zh: 现在大约一半的团队正在开发 Windows。因为例如，如果你想建造温室，你需要透明材料来让阳光进入。理想情况下，你能够利用生物学大规模制造这些材料。想象一下，在一个池塘里培养微生物，它们会分泌一些漂浮到表面的东西，然后你可以从顶部剥下什么，这将成为一个漂亮的大温室面板。

paras.en: And the other half of our team is working on getting rid of the perchlorate in Martian regolith. Perchlorate is a compound that’s poisonous to humans, and there’s so much of it there that Mars dirt can be poisonous to humans, too, as it is now. But there are microbes we’ve found that are able to eat that toxin and degrade it. We’ve found some actually that can eat it directly out of simulated Mars dirt—just add water! So now we just have to push the concentrations up, because Mars has more perchlorate than any organism on Earth has ever experienced naturally. And just like with all our other work, we’re using evolution to try to make an organism that can tolerate it.
paras.zh: 我们团队的另一半正在致力于清除火星风化层中的高氯酸盐。高氯酸盐是一种对人类有毒的化合物，而且火星上的高氯酸盐含量如此之多，以至于火星上的污垢也可能对人类有毒，就像现在一样。但我们发现有些微生物能够吃掉这种毒素并降解它。我们发现了一些实际上可以直接从模拟火星泥土中吃掉的东西——只需加水即可！所以现在我们只需要提高浓度，因为火星的高氯酸盐含量比地球上任何生物体自然经历的都要多。就像我们所有其他工作一样，我们正在利用进化来尝试制造一种能够耐受进化的有机体。

paras.en: Okay. And so the whole idea is that by growing these things locally—by living off the land, so to speak—you’re able to be more efficient and cost-effective, and ultimately self-sustaining, because you don’t have to bring everything from Earth?
paras.zh: 好的。所以整个想法是，通过在当地种植这些东西——可以说，通过在土地上生活——你能够变得更有效率和成本效益，并最终实现自我维持，因为你不必从地球上带来一切？

paras.en: Yeah. The reason we haven’t already done a human mission is that humans, with all our radiation shielding and food and so on, are just so heavy. And it’s just so hard to get that much mass to Mars to allow people live for a period of time, and then it’s even harder to bring them back. So it’s incredibly helpful to use resources that are on-site. And indeed, that’s what frontier civilizations have always done.
paras.zh: 是的。我们还没有完成载人任务的原因是，人类，连同我们所有的辐射屏蔽和食物等等，实在是太重了。要将如此大的质量运送到火星以供人们生存一段时间是非常困难的，然后将他们带回来就更难了。因此，使用现场资源非常有帮助。事实上，这就是边疆文明一直在做的事情。

paras.en: I want to be upfront about my own biases here: I think this is such a cool idea. But as with pretty much every other aspirational project related to human spaceflight, let alone otherworldly settlement, this one has its critics, too. And I think if I could summarize the sorts of criticisms I’ve seen, it would be three interlinked questions: Why terraforming? Why Mars? And why now?
paras.zh: 我想在这里坦率地表达我自己的偏见：我认为这是一个很酷的想法。但与几乎所有其他与载人航天相关的理想项目一样，更不用说超凡脱俗的定居点了，这个项目也有批评者。我认为，如果我能总结一下我所看到的各种批评，那就是三个相互关联的问题：为什么要进行地球化改造？为什么是火星？为什么现在呢？

paras.en: That is, assuming these bioengineered bugs could also be really useful on Earth, why not just focus your efforts here?
paras.zh: 也就是说，假设这些生物工程细菌也可能在地球上真正有用，为什么不把你的努力集中在这里呢？

paras.en: You and I and everyone who’s ever lived is really lucky to live on the one planet we know of that has a functional biosphere. That’s why we’re here breathing, right, because we have a whole planet worth of photosynthesis that’s cranking out oxygen for us all the time. We just call it “nature” and tend to take it for granted.
paras.zh: 你和我，以及曾经生活过的每个人都非常幸运，能够生活在我们所知的拥有功能正常的生物圈的星球上。这就是我们在这里呼吸的原因，对吧，因为我们有整个地球的光合作用，一直在为我们产生氧气。我们只是称之为“自然”，并倾向于认为这是理所当然的。

paras.en: When we go to space, nature is the one thing that we’re missing. It’s the thing we leave behind when we go away from Earth. Well, I love the biosphere, and I think we should bring it with us. I would love for any future humanity that ventures off into the stars to have more interaction with all sorts of delightful types of life rather than less.
paras.zh: 当我们进入太空时，大自然是我们所缺少的一件事。这是我们离开地球时留下的东西。嗯，我喜欢生物圈，我认为我们应该随身携带它。我希望未来的人类能够冒险进入星际，与各种令人愉快的生命有更多的互动，而不是更少。

paras.en: This runs counter to typical visions for the future, I think, where there’s this tendency to think that progress means less nature and fewer trees and we all live in cities with big skyscrapers. That makes me sad, and I don’t think it has to be that way, and so I’m trying to fix it.
paras.zh: 我认为，这与对未来的典型愿景背道而驰，人们倾向于认为进步意味着更少的自然和更少的树木，而我们都生活在拥有大型摩天大楼的城市中。这让我很难过，我认为事情不必如此，所以我正在努力解决它。

paras.en: Mars specifically is this fascinating world in part because it’s almost like a long-lost twin of Earth. Four billion years ago, both planets had liquid water. And Mars, to this day, even after its climate has been substantially altered, still has all the raw materials for life in abundance in a way that the moon doesn’t and that even Venus doesn’t. Venus doesn’t have a lot of water left, and Mars does—it’s got a whole northern hemisphere that’s permafrost, with huge amounts of buried ice. If only we could warm it up, Mars might become a pretty nice place to live.
paras.zh: 火星是一个令人着迷的世界，部分原因是它几乎就像失散已久的地球双胞胎。四十亿年前，两颗行星都有液态水。直到今天，火星即使在气候发生了巨大变化之后，仍然拥有丰富的生命原材料，这是月球所没有的，甚至金星也没有。金星没有剩下太多的水，而火星则有——它的整个北半球都是永久冻土，有大量的埋冰。如果我们能让火星变暖，火星可能会成为一个非常适合居住的地方。

paras.en: And I think that the instinct to go searching outward is just a thing people have. Not everyone wants to be an explorer, but for people who do, Mars is this incredibly intriguing target. And whoever goes first, I’d love for them to have flowers when they live somewhere that’s not Earth.
paras.zh: 我认为向外探索的本能正是人们所拥有的。并不是每个人都想成为一名探险家，但对于那些愿意的人来说，火星是一个非常有趣的目标。无论谁先走，我都希望他们生活在地球以外的地方时能有鲜花。

paras.en: Flowers on Mars! Maybe it’ll be a dandelion, even.
paras.zh: 火星上有花！甚至可能是蒲公英。

paras.en: That would be Pioneer species number six, ha.
paras.zh: 那将是第六号先锋物种，哈哈。

paras.en: Your announcement of sPL.001 made quite a splash, of course. I’m wondering, though, outside of the millions of people who saw your social media post or watched the slick promotional video introducing Pioneer Labs, what the reactions have been from some of your peers in bioengineering, planetary science, astrobiology, and so on. Has it been mixed?
paras.zh: 当然，您发布的 sPL.001 引起了不小的轰动。不过，我想知道，除了数百万看过你的社交媒体帖子或观看介绍先锋实验室的精美宣传视频的人之外，你的生物工程、行星科学、天体生物学等领域的一些同行有何反应。有没有混过？

paras.en: So far, the reaction has been overwhelmingly positive. And I think that’s partially because we took our time preparing for this. We didn’t just announce that we’d engineered the first organism for Mars. We also released a paper showing how we did it, a second paper about a proposed planetary protection framework for thinking about the risks of actually sending such things to Mars and a third paper offering a complete techno-economic analysis for the use cases.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，反应非常积极。我认为这部分是因为我们花了很多时间为此做准备。我们不仅仅是宣布我们为火星设计了第一个有机体。我们还发布了一篇论文，展示了我们是如何做到的，第二篇论文是关于拟议的行星保护框架，用于思考实际将此类东西发送到火星的风险，第三篇论文提供了用例的完整技术经济分析。

paras.en: We’ve shown sPL.001 would be extremely dead if it gets outside on Mars, so, in many ways, this is less risky than sending a human complete with a diverse and complex microbiome on her skin and in her gut. And we’ve shown how this could actually be useful, right—not just how to grow the organism but all of the equipment that has to surround it in order to feed it, heat it, purify products from it and actually build houses. We’ve quantified how much all that mass is, how many launches you’d need to get it to Mars and the total footprint it would have.
paras.zh: 我们已经证明，如果 sPL.001 进入火星，它将会死亡，因此，从很多方面来说，这比将一个皮肤和肠道上都含有多样化且复杂的微生物群的人类送入火星的风险要小。我们已经展示了这实际上是如何有用的，对吧——不仅仅是如何培养生物体，还包括它周围的所有设备，以便喂养它、加热它、纯化它的产品，并实际建造房屋。我们已经量化了它的质量、需要发射多少次才能将它送到火星以及它的总足迹。

paras.en: So we really put our best work into trying to introduce this idea to people in a way that shows why it’s so cool and valuable but also is thoughtful about the ethics. This work has value even if we never terraform Mars. Practically speaking, this is just a good thing to do for the first human mission.
paras.zh: 因此，我们确实尽了最大的努力，试图以一种方式向人们介绍这个想法，以展示为什么它如此酷和有价值，同时也考虑到了道德规范。即使我们从未对火星进行地球化改造，这项工作仍然有价值。实际上，这对于人类的第一次任务来说只是一件好事。

paras.en: And so—especially on X, where this really went viral—I think there were more people who applauded the fact that we had also released a paper about the ethics than there were people who were like, “Er, we should never go to Mars.”
paras.zh: 因此，尤其是在 X 上，这件事真的像病毒一样传播开来，我认为对我们还发布了一篇关于道德的论文表示赞赏的人比那些说“呃，我们永远不应该去火星”的人要多。

paras.en: You’d have to go over on Bluesky to see more of those reactions, I think.
paras.zh: 我想你必须去 Bluesky 才能看到更多这样的反应。

paras.en: Let me try to “both sides” this a bit. I want to double down on the very valid point you’re making: if we’re trying to weigh risk and potential impact, landing a single human—or even a single piece of human excrement, let’s say—on Mars, that’s an orders-of-magnitude bigger deal than landing an enclosed bioreactor.
paras.zh: 让我尝试一下“双方”。我想强调一下你提出的非常有效的观点：如果我们试图权衡风险和潜在影响，那么在火星上登陆一个人——甚至是一块人类排泄物，比方说，这比登陆一个封闭的生物反应器要大几个数量级。

paras.en: But I also inquired about the reactions of your peers because peer review is important in science, and it’s not clearly something that’s happened for any of those three papers you mentioned. There’s a disclaimer near the end of each one that basically says this has not and will not be submitted for peer-reviewed publication because that goes against the “open science” policy of the Astera Institute, a billionaire-backed nonprofit for incubating transformative science and technology that partly funded the work.
paras.zh: 但我也询问了你的同行的反应，因为同行评审在科学中很重要，而且你提到的那三篇论文中的任何一篇都没有明显发生这种情况。在每一篇文章的末尾都有一个免责声明，基本上说这没有也不会提交同行评审出版物，因为这违反了 Astera 研究所的“开放科学”政策，Astera 研究所是一个由亿万富翁支持的非营利组织，致力于孵化变革性科学和技术，并为这项工作提供了部分资助。

paras.en: So with that in mind, I have to ask: Who is independently evaluating this stuff? You’re saying that it’s safe to send sPL.001 to Mars, and in the second paper that you mentioned, yes, you’re proposing a protocol for ensuring that nothing bad can happen in terms of biocontamination. But who’s validating these assertions? That seems like a pretty important step in the process, so I’m wondering why you’re skipping it.
paras.zh: 因此，考虑到这一点，我不得不问：谁在独立评估这些东西？你说将 sPL.001 发送到火星是安全的，在你提到的第二篇论文中，是的，你提出了一个协议，以确保在生物污染方面不会发生任何不好的事情。但谁在验证这些断言呢？这似乎是这个过程中非常重要的一步，所以我想知道你为什么要跳过它。

paras.en: My hope is for us to get to share the science we’re doing openly and very quickly. And I should say that we at Pioneer Labs don’t make NASA policy—and that NASA, in fact, isn’t the only organization that makes policy for the whole world, either. There are a lot of discussions that have already been happening about how to update things like planetary protection frameworks for the upcoming new era of human interplanetary spaceflight.
paras.zh: 我的希望是我们能够公开、快速地分享我们正在做的科学工作。我应该说，我们先锋实验室不制定美国宇航局的政策——事实上，美国宇航局也不是唯一为全世界制定政策的组织。关于如何为即将到来的人类行星际航天新时代更新行星保护框架等内容，已经有很多讨论。

paras.en: We clearly need new frameworks. Historically, NASA policy has been to stringently sterilize everything that goes to Mars, and you obviously can’t do that for a living human! So we’ve decided to throw our hat in the ring and make suggestions about what that new framework could look like. The goal of the Planetary Protection paper we released is for it to be discussed by COSPAR [the Committee on Space Research], which is the main body that makes policy suggestions to the world. My co-founder Una Nattermann will also be on NASA’s newly convened M-FORCE tiger team, which will make recommendations to COSPAR. Our goal here is to participate in the discussion.
paras.zh: 我们显然需要新的框架。从历史上看，美国宇航局的政策一直是对前往火星的所有物体进行严格消毒，但显然不能对活人这样做！因此，我们决定积极参与并就新框架的外观提出建议。我们发布行星保护论文的目的是要让COSPAR（空间研究委员会）讨论，它是向世界提出政策建议的主体。我的联合创始人 Una Nattermann 也将加入 NASA 新组建的 M-FORCE 老虎团队，该团队将向 COSPAR 提出建议。我们在这里的目标是参与讨论。

paras.en: And similarly, we’ve made suggestions about what it could look like to do the first biomanufacturing on Mars. We call this a “reference architecture,” which is a type of paper or engineering document that the space science community often uses. These aren’t usually published in a traditional science journal. I think space science is a discipline that certainly sometimes uses peer review to great effect, but not all of the science happens specifically through journals.
paras.zh: 同样，我们还就在火星上进行首次生物制造的情况提出了建议。我们称之为“参考架构”，这是空间科学界经常使用的一种论文或工程文档。这些通常不会在传统科学期刊上发表。我认为空间科学是一门学科，有时确实会利用同行评审来发挥巨大作用，但并非所有科学都是专门通过期刊进行的。

paras.en: We do currently have funding from the Astera Institute, which believes very strongly that the current peer review journal system is incredibly toxic for science and for innovation. I don’t think anyone really disagrees with that. But as you say, there is this downside to being forced not to participate in traditional journals, which is getting this question about who certifies it. We have, ahead of time, already shared these papers with various colleagues, some of whom are acknowledged in them for the feedback they provided.
paras.zh: 我们目前确实得到了 Astera 研究所的资助，该研究所坚信当前的同行评审期刊系统对科学和创新具有极大的毒性。我认为没有人真正不同意这一点。但正如你所说，被迫不参加传统期刊有一个缺点，这引起了关于由谁来认证的问题。我们已经提前与各位同事分享了这些论文，其中一些同事提供的反馈得到了认可。

paras.en: Also, there’s no stamp of approval, including from a journal, that means something is definitely right, which means even if we did send it to a journal, that doesn’t mean it’s better. We’re just trying to do the best science we can, and part of the challenge is we have to chart new territory about what it looks like to do this without this kind of crutch of journals dictating what is correct—which we all know to not be true anyway.
paras.zh: 另外，没有批准印章，包括来自期刊的批准印章，这意味着某些东西绝对是正确的，这意味着即使我们确实将其发送给期刊，也不意味着它更好。我们只是想尽我们所能地进行最好的科学研究，而挑战的一部分是我们必须绘制新的领域，以了解如何在没有这种期刊的拐杖来规定什么是正确的情况下做到这一点——我们都知道这不是真的。

paras.en: I should say the question doesn’t necessarily come from an adversarial place. You’ve stated elsewhere that Pioneer Labs is hopeful to hit the 2031 launch window for Mars. And that’s practically tomorrow, as far as developing a payload and securing a rocket ride is concerned, right? So it would seem in your best interest to try to bring everybody on board, so to speak, as quickly and fully as possible by addressing any significant concerns that exist.
paras.zh: 我应该说这个问题不一定来自敌对的地方。您曾在其他地方说过，先锋实验室希望在 2031 年实现火星发射。就开发有效载荷和确保火箭飞行而言，这实际上是明天的事情，对吧？因此，通过解决存在的任何重大问题，尽可能快速、全面地让每个人都参与进来，似乎符合您的最大利益。

paras.en: Relatedly, maybe, I wonder if there’s anything you could tell me about what that 2031 mission would notionally look like?
paras.zh: 与此相关的是，也许我想知道你能否告诉我 2031 年任务的概念是什么样子？

paras.en: Yeah, I agree. Flight testing is incredibly difficult in terms of the amount of prep that needs to go into it and the magnitude of engineering that needs to go right. That’s even more true for a Mars mission because Mars is so far away. So we’ve released that third paper, the reference architecture, in part because we’re interested to see how the space science community reacts, especially to different possibilities for what the first flight test could look like.
paras.zh: 是的，我同意。就需要进行的准备工作量以及需要正确进行的工程量而言，飞行测试非常困难。对于火星任务来说更是如此，因为火星距离我们很远。因此，我们发布了第三篇论文，即参考架构，部分原因是我们有兴趣了解空间科学界的反应，特别是对第一次飞行测试的不同可能性。

paras.en: Here’s one example of what the first flight test could be. Wouldn’t it be so cool to go to Mars and do a search-for-life experiment there, where you take a scoop of Mars dirt, you add water, and you incubate it and see if anything grows? Because Mars had nice liquid water back when there was very nascent life on Earth, and there seem to have been giant impacts ping-ponging around the solar system—so maybe one of those impacts sent something to Mars, and maybe today it’s not growing because Mars is too harsh. Maybe it’s dormant in the soil or the ice. One way to find it would be an “enrichment”-type search-for-life experiment. You could sample some dirt or ice, see if it grows anything under more hospitable conditions and do the same after adding fertilizers to see if it’s nutrient-limited.
paras.zh: 这是第一次飞行测试的一个例子。去火星做一个寻找生命的实验，取一勺火星泥土，加水，然后孵化，看看是否有东西生长，不是很酷吗？因为当地球上还存在非常新生的生命时，火星就有很好的液态水，而且太阳系周围似乎发生了巨大的撞击——所以也许其中一次撞击向火星发送了一些东西，也许今天它没有增长，因为火星太严酷了。也许它在土壤或冰中休眠。找到它的一种方法是进行“浓缩”式的生命搜寻实验。你可以取样一些泥土或冰，看看它是否在更适宜的条件下生长任何东西，并在添加肥料后做同样的事情，看看它是否营养有限。

paras.en: Now in order to do that experiment correctly, you do need a positive control, so you need to know that your device worked and that stuff can grow in it, and here is where the first microbe we engineered comes in. You could bring sPL.001 as your positive control and confirm that, yes, this organism that’s been carefully selected to die if it gets outside on Mars can in fact grow in a sealed container using the nutrients in Mars dirt.
paras.zh: 现在，为了正确地进行该实验，您确实需要一个阳性对照，因此您需要知道您的设备是否正常工作，并且这些东西可以在其中生长，这就是我们设计的第一个微生物的来源。您可以将 sPL.001 作为阳性对照，并确认，是的，这种经过精心挑选的生物体，如果它到达火星外面就会死亡，实际上可以利用火星泥土中的营养物质在密封容器中生长。

paras.en: I think this would be great for everyone. Like, the best-case scenario is you find life on Mars—but even if you don’t, by testing this organism’s growth on Mars you’ve now derisked this big thing that would allow you in the next test to actually use it for engineering and biomanufacturing.
paras.zh: 我认为这对每个人来说都很棒。就像，最好的情况是你在火星上找到生命，但即使你没有，通过测试这种生物体在火星上的生长，你现在已经避免了这个大事情的风险，这将使你在下一次测试中实际将其用于工程和生物制造。

paras.en: So this is one possible example of a pretty small first step toward deliberately sending terrestrial life to Mars. It’s safer than sending a human. It has some basic science benefit. And it can be scaled up to do things like testing a larger bioreactor—depending on how big a step the space science community feels comfortable taking and which scientific risks we want to address and eliminate.
paras.zh: 因此，这可能是朝着故意将地球生命送往火星迈出的很小的第一步的一个例子。这比派人来更安全。它有一些基础科学的好处。它可以扩大规模来完成诸如测试更大的生物反应器之类的事情，这取决于空间科学界愿意采取多大的步骤以及我们想要解决和消除哪些科学风险。

paras.en: Speaking of scientific risks, the loudest critics I’ve seen of this work are astrobiologists interested in finding life on Mars who worry that something like sPL.001, if sent there, still poses unacceptable chances for contaminating the planet and irreparably sabotaging the search. Then there’s the more extreme ethical criticism of possible terraforming, perhaps best summarized by the late, great Carl Sagan: “If there is life on Mars..., Mars then belongs to the Martians, even if the Martians are only microbes.”
paras.zh: 说到科学风险，我见过对这项工作最强烈的批评是对在火星上寻找生命感兴趣的天体生物学家，他们担心像 sPL.001 这样的东西如果被发送到那里，仍然会带来不可接受的机会污染地球并无可挽回地破坏搜索工作。然后是对可能的地球化改造的更极端的伦理批评，也许已故伟大的卡尔·萨根对此进行了最好的总结：“如果火星上有生命……，那么火星就属于火星人，即使火星人只是微生物。”

paras.en: Yeah, I don’t agree with that second one.
paras.zh: 是的，我不同意第二个。

paras.en: In general, human astronauts on Mars would massively expand our ability and flexibility to search for life. The search for life doesn’t end because you’ve sent humans. Here on Earth, we still go out and look for dinosaur bones even though we already know they’re there. On Mars, the search could and would continue, which reflects something good about humans. We’re curious about our surroundings and we want to know more, and I think that’s something we should encourage.
paras.zh: 总的来说，火星上的人类宇航员将极大地扩展我们寻找生命的能力和灵活性。对生命的探索并不会因为你派出了人类而结束。在地球上，我们仍然出去寻找恐龙骨头，尽管我们已经知道它们在那里。在火星上，搜索可以而且将会继续，这反映了人类的一些优点。我们对周围的环境感到好奇，想要了解更多，我认为这是我们应该鼓励的事情。

paras.en: It’s really complicated, of course, but here are some simple facts to think about. Here on Earth, we have a word for being vegetarian. But we don’t even have a word for trying not to eat microbes, because it’s totally infeasible! There are many different types of life deserving of our respect, but that doesn’t mean a very simple life-form on Mars should unduly eliminate any possible benefit humans could gain by going there.
paras.zh: 当然，这确实很复杂，但这里有一些简单的事实值得思考。在地球上，我们有一个词叫“素食”。但我们甚至没有一个词来形容“尽量不吃微生物”，因为这是完全不可能的！有许多不同类型的生命值得我们尊重，但这并不意味着火星上非常简单的生命形式应该过度消除人类通过前往那里可能获得的任何可能的好处。

paras.en: I think we’re overdue for a big-picture shift in our approach to Mars, which we’ve been treating solely as this object of scientific study, with incredibly strict protocols for what you can send there and how sterile it needs to be—because this isn’t the only relationship that we could have with Mars, right? Like, humanity could live on Mars, and in that scenario, you then have to weigh the potential value of the scientific knowledge of the planet’s history and its former or extant life against the value of humanity having another home.
paras.zh: 我认为我们早该对火星的方法进行大的转变，我们一直将火星仅仅视为科学研究的对象，对于可以发送到那里的东西以及它需要达到的无菌程度有着极其严格的协议——因为这不是我们与火星建立的唯一关系，对吗？比如，人类可以生活在火星上，在这种情况下，你必须权衡关于地球历史及其以前或现存生命的科学知识的潜在价值与人类拥有另一个家园的价值。

paras.en: And just practically speaking, I do think humans are gonna go to Mars someday, so we have to figure out how to do it in a thoughtful way that sets us up for success in living there, as well as in understanding the planet and its history. I don’t think the answer is to get totally tied in knots and paralyzed by the ethics.
paras.zh: 实际上，我确实认为人类有一天会去火星，所以我们必须想出如何以深思熟虑的方式做到这一点，以便我们能够成功地在那里生活，并了解这个星球及其历史。我不认为答案是完全陷入道德困境并陷入瘫痪。

paras.en: That brings me to my final question. You’ve stated in various places that you hope within your lifetime to look up at the little red dot of Mars in Earth’s sky and see that it’s slightly tinged with green—presumably from imported terrestrial life. What do you think is the biggest hurdle to overcome for that? Would it be scientific, technical, political, ethical?
paras.zh: 这引出了我的最后一个问题。你曾在很多地方说过，你希望在有生之年抬头看看地球天空中火星的小红点，发现它略带绿色——大概是来自外来的地球生命。您认为为此需要克服的最大障碍是什么？它是科学的、技术的、政治的、伦理的吗？

paras.en: If you had asked me this question two years ago when we began, I would say the biggest hurdle is a technical one. That’s why I was excited to work on sPL.001—because I perceived myself as someone who knows how to solve science problems, and I was looking for a big juicy target to sink my teeth into.
paras.zh: 如果你在两年前我们开始时问我这个问题，我会说最大的障碍是技术障碍。这就是为什么我对 sPL.001 的工作感到兴奋，因为我认为自己是一个知道如何解决科学问题的人，并且我一直在寻找一个大而有趣的目标来全身心投入。

paras.en: And now when you ask me, I actually do think maybe the hurdle is more social and political in a similar way to how on Earth we struggle to figure out the collective action puzzle of who pays for addressing climate change. Part of why I like working on the Mars case is that I think in some ways it’s much simpler. There’s no NIMBYism on Mars. And I’m hopeful that together, both the technical and the social things that need doing to make humans on Mars happen could be useful right here on Earth, too.
paras.zh: 现在，当你问我时，我实际上确实认为，也许这个障碍更具社会性和政治性，就像我们在地球上如何努力找出谁为应对气候变化买单的集体行动难题一样。我喜欢研究火星案例的部分原因是我认为在某些方面它要简单得多。火星上不存在邻避主义。我希望，让人类登陆火星所需的技术和社会方面的努力在地球上也能发挥作用。

articles.title: Scientists vote to end leap seconds, redefining how the world keeps time

paras.en: Today an international group of scientists, diplomats and timekeepers voted to end the leap second, which has been keeping Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) aligned with the time according to Earth’s rotation (UT1) within one second of difference. The length of a day according to UTC is close to that of UT1 but not exactly the same because our planet’s rotation is irregular. We add a leap second every few years to keep them from drifting too far apart.
paras.zh: 今天，一个由科学家、外交官和计时员组成的国际小组投票决定结束闰秒，该闰秒一直使协调世界时 (UTC) 与地球自转时间 (UT1) 保持一致，相差一秒以内。 UTC 一天的长度与 UT1 接近，但并不完全相同，因为地球的自转是不规则的。我们每隔几年添加一次闰秒，以防止它们相差太远。

paras.en: But soon the leap second will be replaced with a leap hour, added much more infrequently, which will extend the allowed difference between UT1 and UTC to an hour, or 3,600 seconds.
paras.zh: 但很快闰秒将被闰时取代，并且添加的频率要少得多，这会将 UT1 和 UTC 之间允许的差异扩大到一个小时，即 3,600 秒。

paras.en: “After 30 years of debates, we are ready,” said Noël Dimarcq, a senior scientist at the French National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS) and president of International Bureau of Weights and Measures’ (BIPM’s) Consultative Committee for Time and Frequency, just before the vote, which took place at the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM) in Versailles, France.
paras.zh: “经过 30 年的争​​论，我们已经准备好了，”法国国家科学研究中心 (CNRS) 资深科学家、国际计量局 (BIPM) 时间和频率咨询委员会主席诺埃尔·迪马克 (Noël Dimarcq) 在法国凡尔赛举行的度量衡大会 (CGPM) 投票之前说道。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: UTC is the world’s standard timescale. It’s the reference for how computers, phones, boats, planes, satellites and everything else tell time and for how navigation systems such as GPS function. It’s calculated via a weighted average of the time according to atomic clocks around the world and disseminated by the BIPM.
paras.zh: UTC 是世界标准时间刻度。它是计算机、电话、船只、飞机、卫星和其他一切设备如何报时以及 GPS 等导航系统如何运行的参考。它是根据世界各地原子钟的时间加权平均值计算得出的，并由 BIPM 发布。

paras.en: Shortly after UTC was first established in 1960, scientists noticed Earth’s rotation was ever so slightly slowing down, so it was not keeping pace with the count of the seconds according to atomic clocks. At the behest of astronomers and other experts, the first leap second was added to UTC in 1972 to realign the time standard with Earth’s rotation. Since 1972, 27 leap seconds have been added.
paras.zh: 1960 年 UTC 首次建立后不久，科学家们注意到地球的自转速度稍微减慢，因此无法跟上原子钟的秒数计算。在天文学家和其他专家的要求下，UTC 于 1972 年添加了第一个闰秒，以根据地球自转重新调整时间标准。自1972年起，增加了27个闰秒。

paras.en: In the mid-2010s, however, Earth’s spin began speeding up. Scientists predicted that a negative leap second would be necessary soon, perhaps as early as 2029. Engineers say a negative leap second would be like a “mini Y2K” event because it would suddenly send the entire world one second backward in time, which could cause chaos in our digital infrastructure.
paras.zh: 然而，在 2010 年代中期，地球自转开始加速。科学家预测，负闰秒很快就会成为必要，也许最早在 2029 年。工程师表示，负闰秒就像“迷你千年虫”事件，因为它会突然使整个世界的时间倒退一秒，这可能会导致我们的数字基础设施混乱。

paras.en: “Avoiding negative leap seconds is a very big driver to open the window” between UTC and UT1, says Nick Stamatakos, head of the Earth Orientation Department at the U.S. Naval Observatory, which manages the country’s GPS grid.
paras.zh: 负责管理美国 GPS 网格的美国海军天文台地球定向部门负责人尼克·斯塔马塔科斯 (Nick Stamatakos) 表示，“避免负闰秒是打开 UTC 和 UT1 之间窗口的一个非常重要的驱动因素”。

paras.en: Since 2022 scientists, government officials, telecommunications professionals and others have been urgently trying to find a practical way to solve the leap second problem.
paras.zh: 自2022年以来，科学家、政府官员、电信专业人士和其他人士一直在紧急寻找解决闰秒问题的实用方法。

paras.en: The BIPM, which is the official source of UTC, hosts CGPM every four years to discuss issues with member states. This morning officials at this year’s conference held the vote to end the leap second and make UTC continuous, with the change taking effect on May 20 (World Metrology Day), 2027. The resolution won by a majority vote.
paras.zh: BIPM 是 UTC 的官方来源，每四年举办一次 CGPM，与成员国讨论问题。今天上午，今年会议的官员们举行了投票，决定结束闰秒并使UTC连续，这一变化将于2027年5月20日（世界计量日）生效。该决议以多数票获胜。

paras.en: Instead of using leap seconds, everyone has agreed that they will tolerate more drift between UTC and UT1 than they had in the past. And when things get really bad, we’ll add a leap hour instead. Although leap seconds have historically been added every few years, scientists predict that a leap hour won’t be needed for more than 1,000 years—effectively ending the BIPM’s procedure to link UTC with Earth’s position in the sky.
paras.zh: 每个人都同意他们将容忍 UTC 和 UT1 之间比过去更大的漂移，而不是使用闰秒。当情况变得非常糟糕时，我们会添加闰时。尽管历来每隔几年就会添加一次闰秒，但科学家预测 1000 多年之后就不再需要闰秒了，这实际上结束了 BIPM 将 UTC 与地球在天空中的位置联系起来的程序。

paras.en: The change won’t be noticed by most of us, and switching to continuous time will be easier for our digital infrastructure—there will be much less risk of bugs or service outages arising from a leap second discontinuity. But the shift means that human civilization will even further diverge from our oldest way of telling time: by looking to the sky.
paras.zh: 我们大多数人都不会注意到这种变化，而且对于我们的数字基础设施来说，切换到连续时间将会更容易——由于闰秒不连续性而引起的错误或服务中断的风险会大大降低。但这种转变意味着人类文明将进一步偏离我们最古老的计时方式：仰望天空。

articles.title: Google’s quantum Willow chip may be able to grow ‘magic states’

paras.en: Quantum computers promise exponential computational power by processing many possibilities simultaneously. But the machines we have today are still far from this ideal. For one, their bits, called qubits, are prone to frequent errors, and as a result, quantum computers are limited for now. To overcome errors, the machines need to tap into so-called magic states—and scientists at Google Research think their quantum chip could help get them there. In a new study published today in Science, the researchers show how to supply magic states more cheaply using a gardening-inspired technique called cultivation.
paras.zh: 量子计算机通过同时处理多种可能性来保证指数级的计算能力。但我们今天拥有的机器距离这个理想还很远。其一，它们的位（称为量子位）很容易出现频繁错误，因此，量子计算机目前受到限制。为了克服错误，机器需要进入所谓的神奇状态——谷歌研究中心的科学家认为他们的量子芯片可以帮助它们实现这一目标。在今天发表在《科学》杂志上的一项新研究中，研究人员展示了如何使用一种受园艺启发的栽培技术以更便宜的价格提供魔法状态。

paras.en: Traditional computers build every calculation from a few simple logic gates, such as AND, OR and NOT. By contrast, “quantum computers have their own analogy of these operations called the Clifford gates,” explains Emma Rosenfeld, a researcher at Google Quantum AI and the study’s lead author. Clifford gates, however, can be imitated by a normal computer. “But there is one particular gate that unlocks the quantum computer’s power,” Rosenfeld says. “Physicists call it a non-Clifford gate, most often a T gate.” This extra gate is produced using a magic state.
paras.zh: 传统计算机通过一些简单的逻辑门（例如“与”、“或”和“非”）构建所有计算。相比之下，“量子计算机对这些操作有自己的类比，称为克利福德门，”谷歌量子人工智能研究员、该研究的主要作者艾玛·罗森菲尔德解释道。然而，克利福德门可以用普通计算机来模拟。 “但是有一个特殊的门可以释放量子计算机的力量，”罗森菲尔德说。 “物理学家称其为非克利福德门，最常见的是 T 门。”这个额外的门是使用魔法状态产生的。

paras.en: A quibit in a magic state is prepared in a very specific blend of the states 0 and 1 (occupying a mixture of states is a specialty of quantum computers). Fed into a calculation, it is used up to perform the extra gate, and any flaw in the state becomes a flaw in the gate. “It has to be made very, very precisely,” Rosenfeld says.
paras.zh: 处于神奇状态的量子位是在状态 0 和 1 的非常特定的混合中准备的（占据状态的混合是量子计算机的特性）。输入到计算中，它被用来执行额外的门，并且状态中的任何缺陷都会成为门中的缺陷。 “它必须制作得非常非常精确，”罗森菲尔德说。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The standard recipe to make magic states is called distillation, and it creates fewer, more accurate quantum states from many imperfect ones. “You can have up to 95 percent of your quantum computer being spent just generating these high-fidelity magic states,” Rosenfeld says. To bypass this bottleneck, in 2024 her colleagues at Google Research proposed an alternative technique called cultivation, which works on a single state.
paras.zh: 制造神奇状态的标准方法称为蒸馏，它可以从许多不完美的量子态中创​​造出更少、更准确的量子态。 “你的量子计算机最多可以花费 95% 的时间来生成这些高保真魔态，”罗森菲尔德说。为了绕过这个瓶颈，她在谷歌研究院的同事于 2024 年提出了一种名为“栽培”的替代技术，该技术适用于单一状态。

paras.en: Using Google’s Willow chip, Rosenfeld’s team encoded a rough magic state in a few qubits and then measured it. Measuring a quantum state typically collapses it, forcing it into one of two possible answers. So instead of asking the question, “Are you 0 or 1?” which collapses the quantum state to either of those two options, the team asked, “Are you the right magic state: yes or no?”
paras.zh: 罗森菲尔德的团队使用谷歌的 Willow 芯片，在几个量子位中编码了一个粗略的魔法状态，然后对其进行了测量。测量量子态通常会使其塌陷，迫使其陷入两种可能的答案之一。所以不要问“你是0还是1？”它将量子态压缩为这两个选项中的任何一个，团队问道：“你是正确的魔法状态吗：是还是否？”

paras.en: States that pass this test are then spread across more qubits for stronger protection, hence the gardening name: the state starts small, gets checked and then grows. Without cultivation, about four attempts in 1,000 produced a faulty state. With it, errors fell by roughly 40-fold. The experiment used 54 physical qubits out of Willow’s 105.
paras.zh: 通过此测试的状态将分布在更多的量子位上以提供更强的保护，因此得名“园艺”：状态从小处开始，经过检查，然后不断增长。如果没有修炼，一千次尝试中大约有四次会产生错误的状态。有了它，错误大约下降了 40 倍。该实验使用了 Willow 的 105 个物理量子位中的 54 个。

paras.en: “The Google experiment shows that cultivation works in practice,” says Kenneth Brown, director of the Duke Quantum Center at Duke University, who was not involved in the study. He notes, however, that the technique relies on a quality assurance step that rejects low-quality states, discarding 92 percent of attempts.
paras.zh: “谷歌的实验表明，培养在实践中是有效的，”杜克大学杜克量子中心主任肯尼思·布朗（Kenneth Brown）说道，他没有参与这项研究。然而，他指出，该技术依赖于拒绝低质量状态的质量保证步骤，丢弃 92% 的尝试。

paras.en: The result is still far from what practical applications demand. For example, using a quantum computer to break the current RSA-2048 encryption employed in website security, banking and electronic ID cards would require magic states that would fail only once in 10 billion tries. To simulate molecules, a use Rosenfeld says is more attainable, we would need such states with only one error in a million to one in 100 million. Right now the team stands at roughly one error in 10,000 attempts. Still, the new work represents a step in the right direction, she says.
paras.zh: 结果与实际应用的要求还相差甚远。例如，使用量子计算机破解当前用于网站安全、银行和电子身份证的 RSA-2048 加密，需要的魔法状态在 100 亿次尝试中只会失败一次。罗森菲尔德说，为了模拟分子，这种用途更容易实现，我们需要这样的状态，误差只有百万分之一到亿分之一。目前，该团队在 10,000 次尝试中大约出现 1 次错误。不过，她说，这项新工作代表了朝着正确方向迈出的一步。

paras.en: “We’re more galvanized than ever to get to these near-term scientific applications,” Rosenfeld says.
paras.zh: “我们比以往任何时候都更有动力去实现这些近期的科学应用，”罗森菲尔德说。

articles.title: What happens when you lose your voice?
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: A voice matters not just to the person who is speaking, but to the people listening, too. A study on moms and their daughters demonstrates the power of a voice by showing that moms’ voices reduced a measure of stress in the daughters. The same wasn’t true for texting.
paras.zh: 声音不仅对说话的人很重要，对听的人也很重要。一项针对母亲和女儿的研究表明，母亲的声音可以减轻女儿们的压力，从而证明了声音的力量。对于短信来说情况并非如此。

paras.en: In the second episode of The Deep End: Talk to Me, you’ll hear more about the ripple effects created by a lost voice. Jules Rodriguez says that as his voice slipped away, it felt like he was fading. But could a new, more realistic digital voice step in and change his story?
paras.zh: 在《深渊：跟我说话》的第二集中，您会听到更多关于失声所产生的连锁反应。朱尔斯·罗德里格斯说，当他的声音消失时，他感觉自己正在消失。但一个新的、更真实的数字声音能否介入并改变他的故事呢？

paras.en: Hear about a tough medical decision Jules and his family were facing, and whether a sophisticated voice clone could influence his choice.
paras.zh: 了解朱尔斯和他的家人面临的艰难医疗决定，以及复杂的声音克隆是否会影响他的选择。

paras.en: [reporter audio] Hi, this is Laura calling. This is Laura Sanders from Science News. Is now an OK time to talk about your paper coming out? I would love to start with just the very big picture question of why you did this study. Why did you do this study? What were you hoping to find?
paras.zh: [记者音频] 大家好，我是劳拉。我是《科学新闻》的劳拉·桑德斯。现在是谈论你的论文发表的好时机吗？我很想从一个非常宏观的问题开始，即你为什么要做这项研究。你为什么做这项研究？您希望找到什么？

paras.en: Laura Sanders: I’m a neuroscience reporter with Science News, which means I spend a lot of time reading research papers about the brain. One of my very favorite scientific papers, and there are a lot of them, so this is really saying something, is a study published way back in 2012.
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：我是《科学新闻》的神经科学记者，这意味着我花了很多时间阅读有关大脑的研究论文。我最喜欢的科学论文之一是 2012 年发表的一项研究，这样的论文有很多，所以这确实说明了一些问题。

paras.en: [voice] Researchers at the University of Wisconsin have found the sound of a mother’s voice triggers a physical response.
paras.zh: [声音]威斯康星大学的研究人员发现母亲的声音会引发身体反应。

paras.en: Sanders: Sixty-eight girls, all between the ages of 7 and 12, came into a lab in Madison, Wisconsin. For the experiment, these girls were asked to tell a story out loud and then perform a tricky subtraction problem in their heads. The whole time, they were being watched and evaluated by the researchers. I get sweaty just thinking about it. OK, so after that ordeal, the girls were separated into groups. Some girls got to see their moms in person and talk with them after their stressful performance. Some got to talk to their moms on the phone. Some got to text with their moms. And some just had to sit alone wondering what had just happened to them.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：68 名年龄在 7 岁到 12 岁之间的女孩来到威斯康星州麦迪逊市的一个实验室。在实验中，这些女孩被要求大声讲一个故事，然后在脑海中执行一个棘手的减法问题。整个过程中，研究人员一直在观察和评估它们。我光是想想就出汗。好吧，在那次磨难之后，女孩们被分成了几组。一些女孩在紧张的表演后可以亲自见到她们的妈妈并与她们交谈。有些人必须通过电话与妈妈交谈。有些人必须与妈妈发短信。有些人只能独自坐着，想知道自己刚刚发生了什么事。

paras.en: Later on, when researchers measured stress hormones in the girls, they found something startling. The girls who had talked to their moms, either in person or on the phone, had lower levels of the stress hormone cortisol than the girls who had just texted or had no contact.
paras.zh: 后来，当研究人员测量这些女孩的压力荷尔蒙时，他们发现了一些令人震惊的事情。与妈妈面对面或通过电话交谈的女孩，其压力荷尔蒙皮质醇水平低于刚刚发短信或没有联系的女孩。

paras.en: The authors conclude that there’s something especially soothing about hearing a mom’s voice, some alchemy of familiar and calming sounds that a daughter’s brain wants to hear.
paras.zh: 作者得出的结论是，听到妈妈的声音有一种特别舒缓的感觉，女儿的大脑想听到一些熟悉而平静的声音。

paras.en: [voices] So call your mother. Good advice at any time.
paras.zh: [声音]所以给你妈妈打电话。随时提出好的建议。

paras.en: Sanders: In a full circle sort of way, I tell my own mom about the study after calling her to complain about a bunch of stuff.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：以一种完整的方式，我在打电话给我妈妈抱怨一堆事情后告诉她这项研究。

paras.en: [phone call] The talking mattered. The texting did nothing. The phone call and the in-person lowered their cortisol levels. Well good. So, the voice. That’s what you just did for me. That’s the deal. Well I’m glad. That’s just excellent. Thanks, Mom. All right. Yeah, talk to you later. Bye. Bye.
paras.zh: [电话] 谈话很重要。发短信什么也没做。电话和面对面的交流降低了他们的皮质醇水平。好极了。那么，声音。这就是你刚刚为我做的。就是这样。嗯，我很高兴。那真是太棒了。谢谢，妈妈。好的。是的，稍后再聊。再见。再见。

paras.en: Kate Nilson: And, you know, it’s so funny. Every time I’m with my parents, I think I need to record their voices. How can I be in this world and not have their voices recorded? So I need to get on that.
paras.zh: 凯特·尼尔森：而且，你知道，这太有趣了。每次和父母在一起的时候，我想我都需要录下他们的声音。我来到这个世界怎么可能没有他们的声音呢？所以我需要继续下去。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s speech-language pathologist Kate Nilson, a person very familiar with the specialness of voices.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是言语病理学家凯特·尼尔森，她非常熟悉声音的特殊性。

paras.en: Nilson: Just for all the reasons we just talked about, right? So when I get stressed out, I can just listen to my own mom’s voice. I mean, I’m in my 40s and I still need my mom, so.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：就因为我们刚才谈到的所有原因，对吧？所以当我感到压力的时候，我可以听听妈妈的声音。我的意思是，我已经 40 多岁了，但我仍然需要妈妈，所以。

paras.en: Sanders: I mean, yes, listen to the nice comforting sounds my mom makes on the phone when I go through my laundry list of problems.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我的意思是，是的，当我列出一长串问题时，听听我妈妈在电话里发出的美妙的安慰声音。

paras.en: [phone call] Yeah. I hear it in your voice. Oh, that’s sad. Get me some phone numbers and I’ll make calls. That’s pretty intensive stuff.
paras.zh: [电话] 是的。我从你的声音里听到了。哦，那很伤心。给我一些电话号码，我会打电话。这是相当密集的事情。

paras.en: [intro] Hey mom, can I tell you something? The voice is absolutely an integral part of your identity. Do you want to talk? That added layer of it being you. Hello? Your voice. Hi! Your voice is you.
paras.zh: [简介] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？声音绝对是您身份的一个组成部分。你想说话吗？那增加的一层就是你。你好？你的声音。你好！你的声音就是你。

paras.en: Sanders: This desire to capture voices that have special meaning to us, to hold them close, is a perspective I heard over and over. That’s because voices don’t just mean something to the people who make them. Voices mean just as much to the people hearing them.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这种渴望捕捉对我们有特殊意义的声音，将它们紧紧地抓住，是我一遍又一遍听到的观点。这是因为声音不仅仅对声音的制作者有意义。声音对于听到声音的人来说同样重要。

paras.en: Welcome to this second episode of The Deep End, Talk to Me, from Science News. I’m Laura Sanders, and today we’re going to explore what it means to lose the ability to talk.
paras.zh: 欢迎收看《科学新闻》的《深渊》第二集《跟我说话》。我是劳拉·桑德斯，今天我们将探讨失去说话能力意味着什么。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules Rodriguez has a unique perspective on the human voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯·罗德里格斯对人声有独特的看法。

paras.en: Jules: Your voice is different because it’s a big part of your identity. I knew early on, my voice may disappear, so we made sure to record it while I still had it.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：你的声音与众不同，因为它是你身份的重要组成部分。我很早就知道，我的声音可能会消失，所以我们一定要趁我还有声音的时候把它录下来。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules is a podcaster, former science teacher, comedian, husband, and dad who lives in Miami. He was diagnosed with ALS in 2020. The progressive nature of the disease means that people start losing strength and the ability to move, all while their brains and cognition are unaffected. That loss includes the muscles that are required to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯是一名播客、前科学老师、喜剧演员、丈夫和父亲，住在迈阿密。他于 2020 年被诊断出患有 ALS。这种疾病的进行性意味着人们开始失去力量和移动能力，但他们的大脑和认知不受影响。这种损失包括说话所需的肌肉。

paras.en: MA: I still remember the first time. This was in 2022, the summer of ‘22, that I heard the first little crack in his voice that let me know something’s changing.
paras.zh: MA：我还记得第一次的情景。那是在 2022 年，也就是 22 年的夏天，我第一次听到他声音里的细微声音，让我知道有些事情正在发生变化。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s Jules’ wife, MA. When I was first connected to Jules and MA, I learned they had a podcast called The Couple Shift.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是朱尔斯的妻子，MA。当我第一次联系到 Jules 和 MA 时，我得知他们有一个名为“The Couple Shift”的播客。

paras.en: [podcast]: Well, hello there, everyone. Welcome to episode zero of our brand new podcast.
paras.zh: 【播客】：大家好。欢迎来到我们全新播客的第 0 集。

paras.en: Sanders: About their marriage and themselves as they dealt with life, careers and family. I started listening at the beginning.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：关于他们的婚姻以及他们自己在处理生活、事业和家庭时的情况。我一开始就开始听。

paras.en: [podcast] My name is Maria Aleandra. I am a life and business coach, and this is my amazing hubby. Julian Tomas. And I’m a former teacher and amazing husband. He sure is.
paras.zh: [播客] 我的名字是玛丽亚·阿莉安德拉。我是一名生活和商业教练，这是我了不起的丈夫。朱利安·托马斯.我以前是一名教师，也是一位出色的丈夫。他确实是。

paras.en: Sanders: They were so sweet with each other. Playful, teasing, funny, yet sincere and loving. Listen to them being cute.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他们彼此非常甜蜜。俏皮、戏弄、有趣，但又真诚又充满爱心。听他们说的很可爱。

paras.en: [podcast] So I got frustrated. And by lash shout, it’s like an outburst. It’s a [beep] what the hell? You know, that kind of deal. Do we have to bleep out? We do. Yes. Sorry. Gosh darn it. I should know better. Is that what you’re going to tell me? Yeah, that’s what my look is saying right now.
paras.zh: [播客]所以我很沮丧。猛烈的喊叫，就像爆发一样。这是[嘟嘟]什么鬼？你知道，就是这样的交易。我们必须发出哔哔声吗？我们做到了。是的。对不起。天哪，该死。我应该更了解。这就是你要告诉我的吗？是的，这就是我现在的样子。

paras.en: Sanders: They started recording their podcast in 2019, before Jules’ ALS diagnosis. As I listened, moving from early episodes to later ones, I got this feeling of time zooming past, just so fast I couldn’t catch it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他们从 2019 年开始录制播客，当时朱尔斯被诊断出患有 ALS。当我听的时候，从前几集转到后来的几集，我有一种时间飞逝的感觉，快得我都跟不上。

paras.en: [podcast] We went to go see the doctor again to get his final assessment, I guess.
paras.zh: [播客]我想我们又去看了医生以获得他的最终评估。

paras.en: Sanders: Unlike the Jules and MA from early episodes, I already knew the twist, the gut punch of what was coming.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：与早期剧集中的朱尔斯和马不同，我已经知道即将发生的事情的转折和冲击。

paras.en: [podcast] Unfortunately, the news is that he believes it’s ALS or SMA, which is spinal muscular atrophy. It was a really hard hit in the balls. And it’s been a very difficult couple weeks.
paras.zh: [播客] 不幸的是，有消息称他认为这是 ALS 或 SMA，即脊髓性肌萎缩症。这真是一次重击。这是非常困难的几周。

paras.en: Sanders: As I moved through the episodes, I started hearing a difference in Jules’ voice. His voice got slower, weaker, fuzzier. I asked him recently what that was like.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当我观看这些剧集时，我开始听到朱尔斯的声音有所不同。他的声音越来越慢、越来越弱、越来越模糊。我最近问他那是什么样的。

paras.en: Jules: It’s strange with the podcast because you can hear my real voice slowly decay till we stop.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：播客很奇怪，因为你可以听到我真实的声音慢慢衰减，直到我们停止。

paras.en: MA: Yeah. It’s really this archive of what he sounded like, little by little as it changed. And it was, yeah, like very disarming to get to that moment. And then you begin to get used to it and you sort of work around it and appreciate that it’s still there. Yeah, that was really, really difficult for me.
paras.zh: 马：是的。这实际上是他听起来的档案，一点一点地改变。是的，那一刻让人非常放松。然后你开始习惯它，你会解决它并欣赏它仍然存在。是的，这对我来说真的非常困难。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules and MA even talk about this very process on their podcast, of having a record of their voices through time. Here’s a clip from 2024 when Jules could still talk, but with difficulty.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯和马云甚至在他们的播客上谈论了这个过程，记录了他们随时间变化的声音。这是 2024 年的一个片段，当时朱尔斯仍然可以说话，但很困难。

paras.en: [podcast] To me, it’s so weird. Yes. We’re such different people and different mindsets and just different, well, lack of experience and dealing with all this. It’s so freaking beautiful, though, because you can see the whole evolution of us. It’s a living legacy of a life lived. A living legacy. A living legacy of a life lived. You and your words. Me and my words.
paras.zh: [播客]对我来说，这太奇怪了。是的。我们是不同的人，有着不同的心态，只是不同，缺乏处理这一切的经验。不过，它是如此美丽，因为你可以看到我们的整个进化过程。这是一个活生生的生活遗产。活生生的遗产。一个活生生的活生生的遗产。你和你的话。我和我的话。

paras.en: Sanders: In those last episodes, I was hearing the change in Jules’s voice. I was also hearing his emotions. I was hearing his weariness. Jules compares the process of losing his voice to a Back to the Future moment that any person raised in the 80s will remember. It’s when Marty sees a photograph of his family in a timeline that no longer exists.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在最后几集中，我听到朱尔斯声音的变化。我也听到了他的情绪。我听到了他的疲倦。朱尔斯将失声的过程比作任何在 80 年代长大的人都会记得的回到未来的时刻。当马蒂在一条不再存在的时间线上看到他家人的照片时。

paras.en: [movie audio] Just as I thought. This proves my theory. Look at your brother. His head’s gone. It’s like he’s been erased.
paras.zh: [电影音频] 和我想的一样。这证明了我的理论。看看你的兄弟。他的头不见了。他就像被抹去了一样。

paras.en: Jules: For me, it felt like I was fading away. Like when Marty McFly was seeing his family fade away in the picture he had in Back to the Future.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：对我来说，感觉就像我正在消失。就像马蒂·麦克弗莱在《回到未来》的照片中看到他的家人逐渐消失一样。

paras.en: Sanders: A piece of Jules was fading away. A really important piece that tells other people something about his internal state, his emotions, where he’s been, and what’s happening now.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯的一部分正在消失。这是一个非常重要的作品，它告诉其他人一些关于他的内心状态、他的情绪、他去过哪里以及现在正在发生的事情。

paras.en: Voices are packed with all sorts of signals. Sometimes they’re a little bit unexpected, like when a guy you don’t know all that well says “about” and you realize he is Canadian. Sometimes they’re absolutely obvious, like a strong Southern drawl. Voices can signal energy levels, whether your allergies are acting up, where you were born, and how old you are. Here’s Greg Bryant of UCLA.
paras.zh: 声音中充满了各种各样的信号。有时他们有点出乎意料，比如当一个你不太了解的人说“关于”时，你意识到他是加拿大人。有时它们是绝对明显的，就像浓重的南方拖腔。声音可以表明你的能量水平、你是否过敏、你出生在哪里以及你的年龄。这是加州大学洛杉矶分校的格雷格·布莱恩特的报道。

paras.en: Bryant: Cues are any kind of property that might predict something about the sender. You can tell, for example, how big a person is by hearing their voice. You can tell if they’re male or female generally by hearing their voice. You can tell if they’re old or young, right? So there’s all these kind of basic properties of a person that are indexed in a voice.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：线索是任何可以预测发送者某些信息的属性。例如，您可以通过听声音来判断一个人有多大。一般通过听声音就可以判断他们是男性还是女性。你能看出他们是老是年轻，对吧？因此，一个人的所有这些基本属性都可以在声音中索引。

paras.en: Sanders: Voices can carry emotions too. A smile, for example, has subtle sound cues.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音也可以承载情感。例如，微笑就有微妙的声音提示。

paras.en: Bryant: There’s a slight increase in pitch when you smile and then you change what are called formants. The formants are structures in the speech signal underlying what your perception of vowels is. They’re energy bands that are associated with resonating chambers in your throat and in your mouth. And so when you are moving your tongue around and changing your lips and doing other things going, ahowowowow, you’re changing the formants. That’s the resonating bands of energy in the voice. So when you smile, then the formants change a little bit. And it’s detectable. It’s subtle, but you can hear it for sure.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：当你微笑时，音高会略有增加，然后你会改变所谓的共振峰。共振峰是语音信号中的结构，它是您对元音的感知的基础。它们是与喉咙和口腔中的共振室相关的能量带。因此，当您移动舌头、改变嘴唇以及做其他事情时，哇哇哇，您正在改变共振峰。这就是声音中能量的共振带。所以当你微笑时，共振峰会发生一些变化。而且它是可以检测到的。虽然很微妙，但你肯定能听到。

paras.en: Sanders: See if you can detect it here. It’s Jules introducing an episode of their podcast in 2020.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：看看你能不能在这里检测到它。 Jules 正在介绍他们 2020 年播客的一集。

paras.en: [podcast] So my wife comes to me today, and she says, babe, I have diarrhea.
paras.zh: [播客] 所以我的妻子今天来找我，她说，宝贝，我腹泻了。
