articles.title: Venetian Artist Canaletto Merged Fantasy and Architectural Detail in This Previously Unseen Sketch, Heading to Auction This Month

paras.en: A previously unknown drawing by the 18th-century Venetian artist Canaletto is heading to auction in England. The pencil and brown ink sketch—only just authenticated—is one of Canaletto’s famous capricci, imaginative art works that blend detailed studies of real architecture into fantastical scenarios.

“His capriccio pictures form a small portion of Canaletto’s oeuvre, and this drawing includes many elements typical of this genre: monumental architectural structures, ruins, water and groups of figures, known as staffage,” art historian John Rolfe tells Artnet’s Richard Whiddington in an email. “They show brilliant observation, an eye for detail, but also imagination, fantasy and drama.”

Mallams, an auction house in Oxford, England, will sell the capriccio later this month. It was authenticated by Charles Beddington, an art dealer, historian and Canaletto expert. Canaletto likely composed this scene between 1746 and 1755, during his stint in England, as a sketch for a painting that was later auctioned by Christie’s in the 1990s.
Born in Venice in 1697, Giovanni Antonio Canal, more commonly known as Canaletto, was a vedutisto, or “view painter.” He became famous for highly detailed depictions of his hometown.

“Canaletto would often sketch out his scenes in a mathematical way, drawing the lines of the architecture in pencil with rulers before going over it in pen,” according to Katherine Gazzard, a curator at Royal Museums Greenwich. In fact, Canaletto’s cityscapes were so accurate that he was once accused by a biographer of tracing buildings with a camera obscura. (Researchers disproved this rumor with the help of infrared technology in 2017.)

The recently authenticated drawing depicts a ruined Renaissance-era arcade with two crumbling arches spanning a canal. Before them is a rickety wooden footbridge. Embedded in the riverbank silt is old debris, including a stray carriage wheel. Harsh light and shadow add depth to the scene, and everyday characters are scattered throughout.
“Silhouetted against the light sky, a mother and child step cautiously across the bridge,” Rolfe says in a video from Mallams. “Pose, character and costume, captured in a few quick strokes.”

From the Italian word for capricious or whimsical, a capriccio is an architectural fantasy of the landscape genre. These artworks depict fabricated scenes amid real structures, such as columns from the Roman Forum or Venetian archways. Capricci became popular among Italian artists during the Baroque period, with practitioners including Francesco Guardi and Giovanni Paolo Panini.

While Canaletto’s fame is today associated with his more straightforward cityscape views—one such painting of Venice sold for $30.5 million earlier this year—“the painter himself may well have been more proud of his capricci, works of the imagination being held in higher esteem, particularly by his Italian contemporaries,” per Mallams.

An inscription on the back of the capriccio drawing says it is “a Present from Sig Canal d Canaletti,” suggesting the artist gave it away as a gift. It is thought to have then belonged to Charles Burney, an 18th-century British composer, and passed down in his family for generations.

“Original paintings and drawings by Canaletto rarely come to auction,” Rupert Fogden, Mallams’ director of fine art and pictures, tells the BBC’s Ethan Gudge. “We are expecting a significant amount of interest from both private collectors and institutions worldwide when it goes under the hammer this autumn.”

articles.title: Microplastics Have Been Linked With Myriad Human Health Problems. Scientists May Have Finally Figured Out How They Harm the Body

paras.en: Microplastics have been found throughout the human body, including the brain, lungs and blood. Past studies have identified associations between the tiny particles and various health issues, such as cardiovascular disease, dementia and reproductive problems. But the exact way they might contribute to these problems has been unclear.

Now, scientists say they’ve found an answer: Microplastics appear to generate highly reactive molecules when they interact with water. If the same effect were to happen in our bodies, microplastics could lead to oxidative stress, which damages cells, and inflammation. The findings, published in the journal Nature on October 14, challenge the idea that plastics don’t easily react with other substances and point to how they can cause harm to humans.

“We’ve long assumed that plastic itself is inert, and that any harm from microplastics comes from the chemicals added to plastics or the pollutants that stick to them,” Lisa Patel, a physician at Stanford Medicine Children’s Health who wasn’t involved in the study, tells Everyday Health’s Becky Upham. “This study suggests the surface of the plastic particle can be chemically active on its own.”

Bulk plastics are generally thought of as durable and chemically resistant, but that “needs to be reconciled with the toxicity of their fragmented microscale forms,” the authors write in the study. When plastics degrade into microplastics—pieces smaller than a pencil-tip eraser—their surface-to-volume ratio goes up. For example, if a credit card gets broken down into bits just ten microns in diameter, or around one-tenth the thickness of a sheet of paper, that increases its surface area more than 200 times, explains study co-author Wei Min, a chemist at Columbia University, to Payal Dhar at Scientific American. The more exposed area, the more chemical activity.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: To better understand how these tiny fragments might generate chemical activity, Min and colleagues examined particles of widely used bulk plastics, including polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyvinyl chloride and polyethylene terephthalate.

Analyses revealed that when microplastics interact with water, they spontaneously generate unstable molecules known as reactive oxygen species. Because plastic repels water, or is hydrophobic, the surrounding water can’t form its usual hydrogen bonds. So, contact between the two substances results in electric changes that can help create volatile molecules called hydroxyl radicals.

Microplastics are therefore “like a permanent little factory” that generates this reactive oxygen species, Min tells Evan Bush at NBC News. “Our cells are 60 to 70 percent water, and therefore this effect could be ubiquitous.”
Did you know? Contributions to climate change
Researchers reported in May that microplastics swirling in the atmosphere might be heating up the Earth by absorbing sunlight and warming the surrounding air.

These harmful hydroxyl radicals were even produced when the team mixed microplastics with mouse blood, although the effect was smaller than in water. In response, some red blood cells seemed to change shape, and their activity levels shifted. “We do show immediate biological consequences,” Min tells NBC News. “Proteins get damaged. Cells get damaged.”

However, the exact size and mechanism of this effect is still unclear, and it may depend on how our bodies get rid of microplastics, Min tells Jo Marchant at New Scientist. “How much plastic is in a regular human being? We have no idea right now.”

What’s more, adding a chemical called a surfactant that weakens the forces holding water molecules together reduces the generation of hydroxyl radicals, the team found. And some substances in the body, such as certain lipids, have this property.

“Microplastics hit your lung, and they are surrounded by surfactants immediately,” Matthew Campen, a biochemist at the University of New Mexico who wasn’t involved in the study, tells New Scientist. “In most situations that I can imagine in a biological system, they will be surrounded by those lipids. The big concern is [whether] this is getting worse over time, and we really need to get a handle on what the health effects are, or could be, so that we can avoid exposures.”

Still, the findings give scientists a new way to look at plastic pollution’s impacts, says Martin Wagner, a toxicologist and a biologist at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology who wasn’t involved in the work, to Scientific American. “It implies microplastics themselves are a source of oxidative species ... and oxidative stress is not a secondary effect of exposure.”

articles.title: Madrid's Renewed and Expanded Sorolla Museum Lets the Paintings of the Spanish 'Master of Light' Re-emerge Into Public View

paras.en: For the first time in two years, the works of one of Spain’s most celebrated painters, Joaquín Sorolla y Bastida, are back on public display at his namesake museum in Madrid.

The Sorolla Museum partially reopened this week, boasting a nearly 20,000-square-foot expansion. That includes new exhibition spaces, an auditorium and storage for the museum’s 1,394 paintings and roughly 5,000 drawings by Sorolla—the world’s largest collection of his works.

“After the remodeling, the Sorolla Museum will have a new, expansive personality,” Enrique Valera, the museum’s director, tells the Art Newspaper’s Alexandra F. Coego. “We didn’t have a space like this before, and it will allow us to expand our cultural programming for every type of visitor.”

The museum is centered around Sorolla’s home and studio, where the artist, who was born in Valencia in 1863, worked and lived with his family from 1911 until his death in 1923. The museum opened to the public in 1932, after his widow’s death.

The home makes for an enchanting space. “Stepping into the seductive confines of the compound, where Sorolla lived with his wife and three children, is like entering one of the artist’s luminous paintings,” Tony Perrottet wrote for Smithsonian magazine in 2008. “Sorolla’s easels stand ready, as if he had just left for a siesta; his palettes, brushes and half-used paint tubes are close by.”

But because the house was designed for a small family, it struggled to keep up with the demands of being a public museum that, in 2023, the centenary of the artist’s death, saw a record 345,000 visitors. Since the 1930s, the museum has undertaken partial measures to adapt to increased visitation, including redesigning exhibition halls and installing climate control to protect Sorolla’s works. “Nevertheless, all these interventions were only partial in scope,” per the museum’s website.

That changed four years ago, when the museum began an ambitious overhaul and expansion project costing some €13 million (roughly $14.5 million), according to Todo Alicante’s Rocío Mendoza. Work on adjacent properties bought by the Spanish Ministry of Culture began in 2022. The main museum shut its doors in 2024. The expanded galleries are now open, although the house and studio will remain closed for years to come.
“The restoration of the studio home is being carried out with surgical precision and will take years. But the goal is to recover its original essence,” Valera tells Todo Alicante.

The expansion was built with the same architectural spirit as Sorolla’s home studio—an ample use of wood and emphasis on natural light—giving it a cohesive feel with the larger museum. It also lives up to Sorolla’s nickname, “the master of light,” which he earned for his paintings of sparkling beaches and other outdoor scenes.

The expanded museum has an interior courtyard and garden roofs that designers hope will help the space blend in to its residential surroundings. A glass wall in the expanded building, which currently frames a view of the under-construction studio home, will later be converted into a connective threshold that physically and conceptually bridges the museum’s past and present.

The reopened museum’s first temporary exhibition, “Behind the Artist’s House: The Architecture of the Sorolla Museum, 1905–2026,” debuted this month and runs through early January. It tells the story of the house’s design, which Sorolla personally oversaw, and the subsequent evolution of the Sorolla Museum.
“Behind the Artist’s House: The Architecture of the Sorolla Museum, 1905–2026” is on view at the Sorolla Museum in Madrid until January 10, 2027.

articles.title: These 12 Automatic Cat Feeders Were the Best We Tested in 2026
articles.author: Molly Higgins

paras.en: An automatic cat feeder may just change your life. No more begging at 4 am. Plus, it can give you peace of mind while you're away from your fur baby. As seen with the rise of automatic litter boxes and pet tracking, technology has made it so we can closely monitor our pets without doing a lot of the manual labor normally involved.

Gravity-fed automatic dry-food dispensers were invented nearly a century ago, but today most automatic cat feeders use Wi-Fi and connect to a phone app that lets you set a schedule or feed on demand from afar, all while monitoring your pet’s eating habits. Newer models have taken this tech further, like the Petkit YumShare Dual-Hopper 2 Automatic Feeder With Camera ($170), which has a built-in, AI-enabled camera that analyzes the remaining food in the bowl and stops dispensing to prevent overfeeding. Automatic wet-food dispensers—our top pick in this category is the Petlibro Polar Smart Wet Feeder ($170)—are relatively new, often using ice packs or mini-refrigeration cooling systems to keep the food as fresh as possible.

paras.en: Automatic feeders are also helpful for pet parents who want to monitor their pets’ health, maintain specialized schedules, or foster healthier eating habits. (A customizable automatic cat feeder can help with the endless gorging-vomiting cycle many cats struggle with.) Nearly all of the automatic cat feeders on this list are marketed toward cats, but some can be used with smaller dogs, and I’ve noted these below.
Check out our related guides, like the Best Automatic Litter Boxes, Best Cat Water Fountains, Best Smart Cat Collars, and Best Pet Cameras.
Updated October 2026: I've added the Neakasa Riko Automatic Cat Feeder and Petlibro Granary 2 Vision and removed the out-of-stock Cheerble Match G1. I've also updated prices and links throughout.

Oneisall 2-in-1 Automatic Cat Feeder and Water Dispenser for $60: Generally, I'm a fan of all the Oneisall pet products I've tested. While they aren't the most technologically advanced, they are always reliable and affordable. This model is relatively simple. To set up, you'll need to attach the bowl supports and dishwasher-safe stainless-steel bowls, fill the water and kibble compartments, and plug in. This model runs on corded power but also has an optional 4 AA batteries in case of a power outage. There is no connected app. You'll just set the clock and adjust meal settings, and you can schedule one to six meals per day with adjustable portions, from one to 10 portion sizes. I don't love having food and water so close, since cats prefer them separate to prevent cross-contamination in the wild. I always recommend automatic pet fountains instead for a fresh source of water, but if you don't have a lot of space, are on a budget, and need a temporary solution for getting fresh water to your kitty while you're out of town, the gravity-fed water system helps keep water relatively fresh (plus, the translucent tank makes it easier to check water levels). I'd recommend this basic option if you're on a budget and need a temporary solution for when you're out of the house (and don't mind not having a connected app).

paras.en: Closer Pets C200 2-Meal Automatic Pet Feeder for $50: This automatic feeder is super simple, which is both its weakness and its strength. It’s essentially two shallow plastic containers with stainless-steel inserts (both dishwasher-safe) and tamper-resistant lids that lock and automatically open using an old-school egg-style timer that runs on an AA battery rather than electricity. Although the container has an ice pack to keep the wet food cool, after one night it lost virtually all of its coolness. There’s a lid-link clip attachment, a small piece of plastic that links the lids to ensure they open at the same time, which is super helpful for owners of two cats like me. I wish the timer were electric so I could program it to the exact time I want it to open, rather than guesstimating the timing on the little marks. However, this is a simple solution to help make sure both my cats are given wet food without me having to wake up at the crack of dawn.

paras.en: Oneisall Cordless WiFi Automatic Cat Feeder for $53: I had high hopes for this cordless feeder, which boasts a rechargeable battery with a 100-day life and an integrated app, but it's just too unreliable. Through the app, you can program up to 10 daily meals (in 1-12 portions each), monitor pets' eating habits, and customize meal calls. Unlike other apps, you can't choose portion size; instead, you have to multiply the number of servings. The app gave me constant problems and would often disconnect from the feeder and be unable to reconnect to WiFi. Luckily, I was able to program meals via the screen and buttons, but it would've been much nicer if the app had worked reliably.

paras.en: Catit Pixi Smart 6-Meal Feeder for $86: Like others on this list, the Catit Pixi wet and dry feeder uses ice packs to keep wet food fresh and rotates meals among six compartments on a set schedule. The schedule can be programmed via the app or adjusted on the feeder itself. At this price point, the app shouldn’t be this limited and glitchy. The schedule is available in military time only, and the app is extremely limited—you can only set the meal schedule for the same day. When I wanted to do only two to three meals a day spread over two days, I had to reschedule the meals for every new day. The feeder didn't keep it cold enough to spread the meals out, and the wet food was not at a safe eating temperature. At this price point, just get the Petlibro Polar wet feeder.

paras.en: Catit Pixi Smart Cat Feeder for $112: Kibble is stored in the feeder’s body, but it lacks a window to visually check food levels. The meal-planning calendar shows only a week at a time, and although it should repeat daily based on the schedule, I found that some days had no schedule despite setting one up. The Pixi also doesn’t tell you how much food was dispensed; it just refers to it as a “portion”—I manually measured and found the portion was less than a tablespoon of kibble. After using it continuously for more than a month, I found it was extremely glitchy and almost never reliably stuck to the programmed schedule, sometimes skipping meals altogether. This feeder is potentially dangerous, and I'd caution pet parents against relying on it.

paras.en: Closer Pets C500 for $77: This automatic wet and dry feeder can schedule up to four pre-portioned meals (and one meal given manually) and opens them on a timer using three AA batteries (sold separately). The user sets the four times they want the bowls, which have ice packs underneath, to rotate. The bowls are quite deep and narrow, and they aren’t super easy for cats to reach, which could cause whisker fatigue. Although there are two relatively large ice packs, when I checked on the feeder after a night’s sleep, the packs weren’t very cold. This may be OK for kibble, but wet food was kept at unsafe temperatures, and my cats couldn't reach all of the food.

paras.en: Automatic feeders are great for pet owners who want to help manage their pets’ weight and monitor eating patterns. Plus, they allow for a lot more control and precision, so owners can learn exactly how much their cat is eating and when. Because cats are naturally more nocturnal, many have the annoying habit of waking you up in the early hours, demanding food. These feeders allow you to set up a schedule that fits their schedule better without inconveniencing yours.

Of course, it’s never recommended to leave pets alone for long periods, but these automatic feeders give more peace of mind and are much healthier for your pet than leaving a huge amount of food out for free-feeding while you're away for the night. Simply put, it’s an easier way to feed and monitor your cat’s health with less work for you, the human.

I have two rescue cats, ages 4 and 5, and they eat two wet-food meals a day, along with small amounts of dry kibble throughout the day. Vets (and TikTokkers) have successfully persuaded me to move toward a primarily wet-food diet, which has a higher water content. This provides more moisture in their diet, which helps with potentially life-threatening problems like UTIs, which are especially prevalent in male cats. I still like to give smaller dry-food meals throughout the day to satisfy their need for crunch.

paras.en: For dry food, I use Hill’s Science Diet, and for wet food, I use Friskies Shreds. (Yes, only Shreds. Fellow cat owners will understand.)

I set up the feeders, noting ease of setup, potential problems, and app navigation. I also tested various schedules and manual feedings in the app, documenting any issues. I used each feeder for at least a week, if not longer.

Although cats are generally considered less high-maintenance than dogs, it’s still not advisable to leave your cat alone for extended periods. In dire circumstances, you can leave a cat alone for 24 to 48 hours with scheduled feedings and a clean water source, but it’s not ideal—especially for cats with health issues, kittens younger than a year, or very elderly cats. Although these feeders are automatic and meals can be scheduled in advance for multiple days, our pets still need their human pals around for enrichment, care, and, well, love.

articles.title: The Best LED Grow Lights for Houseplants This Winter (2026)
articles.author: Kat Merck

paras.en: Summer is officially over, along with its allotment of free sunlight. You might be sad about this, but your indoor plants might be even sadder. A good LED grow light can replicate sunlight with full-spectrum light and day/night cycles, keeping plants lush and thriving even in a dark, windowless corner or basement.

I have no fewer than 40 houseplants in my home at any given time, as well as a fair number of grow lights, and what I've found to be important for a general consumer (i.e., someone not doing that kind of indoor grow) isn't necessarily certain colored light wavelengths but whether a grow light is easy to live with in your house.

Many grow lights are more or less going to serve the same purpose, so what you really need to know is this: Is the light so bright that it's disruptive? Does it require complicated installation? Is it easy for kids or pets to knock over? The grow lights recommended below are ones that WIRED staffers have lived with for months, if not years, and have found them both effective and easy to integrate into our lives.
Also be sure to check out our guides to the Best Indoor Gardening Systems, Best Gifts for Plant Lovers, and Best Kitchen Composters.

Photosynthetic photon flux Ddensity, or PPFD, expressed in micromoles per square meter per second (μmol/m²/s), is a measurement of how much light reaches your plant that's usable for photosynthesis. In general, the higher the plant's energy needs, such as producing a flower or a fruit, the higher the PPFD number you want. Though different lights have different height requirements given the plants they're made for, for standardization purposes, I measured the PPFD of each grow light at 18 inches with the Photone app and a light diffuser. Keep in mind these measurements are general and approximate.

paras.en: Some of these grow lights I bought myself, with my own money, before I even began working at WIRED. Others were owned by staffers and recommended to me. I also have press samples from other guides I worked on, which I liked so much I ended up keeping around.

For the traditional grow lights, I tested them at home under normal-life conditions. I put them where they'd fit, tested their timers, and noted whether or not they were dimmable. I also measured each light's PPFD (see above) and noted whether certain lights could be daisy-chained for more extensive coverage.
Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.
Best Grow Light for Small Plants and Seedlings

There are a lot of options out there for starting seeds and helping houseplants along in the winter, and many of them are bulky, fussy, or require elaborate hanging setups. This simple, 15-inch-long light from Vego sticks to its 3M adhesive mount with a magnet, so it's easy to take on and off and use with existing racks or, as I do, under a kitchen cabinet. Up to four Vego lights can be daisy-chained together, and the five preprogrammed modes (Seeds, Leafy, Fruits, Herbs, Microgreens) have varying intensities and automatic built-in off periods to simulate nighttime. I have not found this light especially disruptive, especially since it's easy to turn on and off with the button on the back.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: WIRED commerce SEO director Stewart Savin used these lights to start her garden earlier this year and had 138 successful germinations across 144 seedling cells. ("The vast majority of those plants went on to have long lives in my garden after I hardened them off," she says.) Note that because this light can only go beneath a rack, shelf, or cabinet, it’s not inherently adjustable, and therefore is best for small plants (like seedlings) that aren’t going to grow especially tall.

This do-anything light, with a broad 2 x 3-foot head, can hang from the ceiling or swivel on its included stand where you need it. (Up to 20 of these lights can be daisy-chained.) Note that while the stand is useful, the 1-inch-diameter pole and offset base aren't the sturdiest, and it's easy to knock over, so I'd recommend hanging it if you have pets and small kids. I learned this the hard way while trying to revive a corn plant in a dark corner at the top of my stairs.

While this light is quite bright and potentially disruptive, it's easily dimmable via the remote, which hangs on a cord. At first I thought this was weird, but I found it extremely useful when the light was behind plants or in another hard-to-reach spot.
Also worth noting: While the stand height is supposed to be adjustable up to 72 inches, mine only goes up to about 64 inches, so it may not be the best option for extremely tall plants.
Best Grow Light for Serious Indoor Growers

Vivosun is a long-respected brand among indoor growers, and its LumaLight panels are sturdy and all business. In fact, you'll be hard-pressed to find a higher-quality grow light for the price. This is not necessarily a light for casual houseplant parents—the 100-watt, 12 x 12-inch model weighs 4.4 pounds and needs to be attached to the ceiling or inside one of Vivosun's grow tents using the included adjustable ropes and carabiners.

If you're growing fruiting or flowering plants, though, this is the grow light you want—none of the other lights I tested even came close to its level of brightness. That said, you probably won't want it in a main living area, though it is dimmable via a dial on top. The LumaLight is IP65-rated for water resistance, and up to seven units can be daisy-chained if you need.

Former WIRED commerce director Martin Cizmar loved and recommended this grow light for his houseplants, which features three bendable heads on a clip you can attach to a table or shelf. It has a timer for three, nine, or twelve hours, plus a 10-foot cord if you need to place it away from an outlet. It also has warm and cool lighting options in addition to full spectrum, if you want to use it for ambiance (despite it looking, in my opinion, sort of like a creepy Freddy Krueger glove), plus 10 dimming modes. Right now, the base price on Amazon is for a two-pack.

articles.title: Encryption Is Getting Squeezed From All Sides
articles.author: Matt Burgess, Lily Hay Newman

paras.en: Oh, Canada. The Great White North is the latest country to contemplate legislation that could essentially mandate backdoors and increase data retention in encrypted services. The proposed changes have prompted the Canadian anti-censorship company Psiphon VPN—which keeps millions of Iranians online during repressive internet shutdowns—to say it will leave the country if the bill passes. And Psiphon is not the only one.

Encrypted messaging app Signal has said it would exit the Canadian market because the legislation would require unacceptable changes to its open source projects. Apple and Meta have criticized the bill, and DuckDuckGo and NordVPN say they would consider pulling their services, too. But as countries around the world contemplate similar legislation, even larger questions begin to emerge about which states or regions could differentiate themselves as being safe havens for privacy services if global hostility to encryption continues to rise.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: It’s been maddening and disturbing to see more and more democratic countries around the world propose changes to their surveillance and data collection laws, with the aim of giving cops and intelligence agencies greater powers to access people’s information. Governments already have broad digital surveillance powers and investigative tactics to solve crimes that involve encrypted data, but legislative proposals almost inevitably include provisions to expand this access even more—mandating additional logging and what amounts to backdoors or intentional flaws in encrypted products, which cryptographers and security engineers have consistently said cannot be built safely. Truly everyone who understands the issue has said it as much for decades. Yet policymakers return again and again to the idea, somehow expecting a different conclusion or a new breakthrough that will make it all possible.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “There have always been some officials within certain agencies that tend to view technology as a crime scene in and of itself, and it becomes a myopic point of fixation where access is desired,” says Kate Robertson, a senior research associate at the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab. “But that type of siloed thinking forgets that technology needs to be the secure operating platform for hospitals, for banks, for national security agencies, for police services themselves to protect victims who report private information to them.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In recent years, the UK and Australia have introduced sweeping surveillance reforms that can compel companies to break their encryption. Other encryption-threatening proposals have also emerged in the EU, France, India, Ireland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and others. While not all measures have passed into law or been enacted, the hostility is clear.

First proposed in 2025, and partially revised due to blistering criticism from tech companies and civil society, Canada’s C-22 bill can broadly place requirements on tech companies, including those outside of Canada, to introduce “technical capabilities” that allow data to be accessed for law enforcement purposes. Like many such bills, C-22 says that companies will not have to introduce a “systemic vulnerability” into their systems. But opponents have pointed out that any capability to access end-to-end encrypted data amounts to a backdoor that could be discovered and abused by anyone. And this risk is only heightened even more by the ease with which anyone can now use AI tools for reverse engineering and system mapping.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Companies could be asked to introduce vulnerabilities, build backdoors, bypass, weaken or otherwise defeat encryption,” members of the US House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs committee said in a May letter to Canadian officials.

In addition to potential impacts on encryption, C-22 also includes provisions that could require companies to retain metadata about user activity, something that many privacy focused services (including VPN services from Psiphon and DuckDuckGo) intentionally avoid. As a result, these companies say, they would be forced to change their business models to collect data they do not need or want to collect about their users. And researchers say that such product changes would diminish user trust while increasing the potential for widespread surveillance.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “If you are asking and requiring for this infrastructural change—that they retain metadata by default—it is creating a surveillance capability within a tool that didn’t have it,” says Afsaneh Rigot, the founder of the De|Center, a research organization that aims to reduce the risk of technological harms. “There are contexts like Iran and other contexts globally, who all of this has a trickle effect on. It's not going to stay in Canada because these types of laws always get copy pasted around the world.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: As more countries contemplate such laws, developers focused on privacy and anti-censorship tools are increasingly casting around for safe jurisdictions to operate in. But this still doesn’t solve the problem of reaching users in all countries around the world and for now, there are no sure bets.

“Changing your headquarters isn’t much of a plan B when the law follows your users, as C-22 would,” says Joseph Lorenzo-Hall, security portfolio lead at the Internet Society. “The strongest protection is holding as little user data as possible, but ‘we don’t have it’ is no defense if governments can force you to start collecting it. A safe haven needs more than favorable winds in strong encryption. It needs laws that let companies keep their privacy promises and defend them against foreign threats to confidentiality and integrity.”

articles.title: Antonio Banderas to co-star with Nicolas Cage in next 'True Detective'

paras.en: Oct. 17 (UPI) -- HBO has announced Antonio Banderas will co-star with Nicolas Cage in the next installment of the anthology series, True Detective.
"Season 5 of #TrueDetective starts production in 2027," the network posted on social media Friday.
Each season of the show has a different cast and setting.
No other details have been announced yet for Season 5.
Previous Detective pairings have included Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, Colin Farrell and Vince Vaughn, Mahershala Ali and Stephen Dorff, and Jodie Foster and Kali Reis.

articles.title: Pope Leo home from hospital after lung cancer surgery

paras.en: Oct. 17 (UPI) -- Pope Leo XIV has been discharged from the hospital Saturday after successful lung cancer surgery and plans to lead the noon prayers Sunday from the window of the Apostolic Palace.

Dr. Luigi Carbone and Prof. Stefano Margaritora said Leo had blood tests and a chest X-ray in the morning, which confirmed that he was healthy enough to leave Rome's Agostino Gemelli Hospital, Vatican News reported.
The pope, 71, was diagnosed with cancer Tuesday and had part of his right lung removed during surgery to remove a nodule, his doctors said.
Carbone and Margaritora said the pontiff had adenocarcinoma "as suspected by the pre-operative tests" he had before the surgery. It's the most common type of lung cancer.
Before leaving the hospital, he celebrated Mass in a room on the 10th floor of the hospital for staff.

As Leo left the hospital, he was greeted by 13-year-old Vavara, a Ukrainian girl who survived cancer. She had met him once before, while she was undergoing treatment for cancer, and he had hugged her.
This time, she wanted to return the well-wishes. Vavara and her family traveled from Castellamonte, in the province of Turin, where they now live.
Varvara told Leo that their hug had given her "the strength to overcome the illness that, fortunately, I have now beaten."
She said she "wanted to come to Rome to pray for him beneath his window and return that important embrace."
"You, too, will overcome this moment and continue your work of spreading the Gospel," she said.

The pope is planning to travel to Latin America Nov. 6-17. He is scheduled to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he lived and worked for years. But the Vatican said it's cautious about his travel plans, CNN reported.

"We need to see how the Pope feels once he is discharged -- what his state of health is -- and based on that, he will decide whether to keep or cancel his trips," Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Holy See Secretary of State, told reporters Friday.

articles.title: Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Liam Payne With Unreleased Song on Anniversary of His Death
articles.author: Jessica Lynch

paras.en: Harry Styles paid tribute to his late One Direction bandmate Liam Payne at Madison Square Garden on Friday (Oct. 16), debuting an unreleased song he wrote for his friend on the second anniversary of Payne’s death.

Performing as part of his 30-night residency at the New York venue, Styles paused to address the crowd before the tribute. “I feel incredibly lucky to get to play these shows here in New York, and this building means a lot to me,” he said, reflecting on the people who had shaped his life. “And two years ago today, I lost one of those friends.”

“I’m sure a lot of you have been through similar things. I hope you haven’t. But really, it’s just about looking after each other,” Styles continued. “So many people who have touched my life in such special ways, I wouldn’t be here without. I’m gonna play you a song I wrote for my friend about two years ago, if that’s all right.” He then introduced the song by name — “This is ‘What Is Enough’” — and performed its live debut.

Payne, who rose to fame alongside Styles, Niall Horan, Louis Tomlinson and Zayn Malik in One Direction, died in October 2024 at age 31. The group, which formed on the U.K.’s The X Factor in 2010 and went on hiatus in 2016, remains one of the best-selling boy bands of all time, with four consecutive No. 1 albums on the Billboard 200. In the two years since Payne’s death, each surviving member has returned to making music.

The tribute came amid a landmark run for Styles. His Together, Together Tour — in support of his fourth studio album, Kiss All the Time, Disco Occasionally — includes a record-breaking 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden, for which Ticketmaster reported 11.5 million people registered for presale access. A two-time Grammy winner, Styles has topped the Billboard Hot 100 with “Watermelon Sugar” and “As It Was” — the latter spending 15 weeks at No. 1 — and scored three consecutive No. 1 albums on the Billboard 200 as a solo artist.

articles.title: ‘I’m Experiencing Everything I’ve Ever Wanted’: Recapping Miley’s Live Return, On Her Own Terms
articles.author: Lyndsey Havens

paras.en: “It’s always been a dream of mine to play such an iconic venue,” Miley wrote on social media just hours ahead of her Hollywood Bowl performance on Friday night (Oct. 16).

It was a funny reminder for longtime fans who have seen the child actor ascend to pop star heights; while Miley has been around and iconic for so many years, it’s really been the last few in which her career has been celebrated more widely.

At the 2024 Grammys, she won her first award (actually, two) for her Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 smash “Flowers,” taking home record of the year and best pop solo performance. In 2025, she joined Spotify’s exclusive Billions Club, delivering a hits-filled set in Paris to perform her biggest songs including “Wrecking Ball” and “The Climb.” And earlier this year, she celebrated the 20th anniversary of Hannah Montana with a Disney+ special and rare media blitz.

Already this year, she dropped Cyrus from her stage name — joining mononymous legends like Madonna, Cher and Beyoncé. And now, in her own words, she is living out a longtime dream of playing Los Angeles’ famed venue the Bowl.

Miley last performed a full set four years ago, in Mexico for over 150,000 fans (the Bowl’s capacity is 17,500). Since, she became a frequent guest at Chateau Marmont for intimate, invite-only sets but has otherwise remained absent from the stage. Needless to say, anticipation and fervor was at an all-time high for her first of two sold-out Bowl shows (the second is Sunday, Oct. 18).

From the live debut of Bass Persuades standouts to the sing-alongs for generational hits like “We Can’t Stop,” “Party in the U.S.A” and “The Climb,” here are the seven most notable moments from Miley’s major live return.

- The Bass Persuades Opening Hat Trick Given that Miley has released three albums since her last full performance, there was a lot of catching up to do. But, given that these two Bowl shows were branded and marketed in promotion of Bass Persuades – her latest album that topped the Billboard 200 for one week — it was only natural to start there. Following a black and white spoken-word video interlude of Miley — the first of a few that were sprinkled throughout the show — she opts to open with Bass standouts “Orbit,” “Different Religion” (for which she plays electric guitar and welcomes collaborator and opener Model/Actriz back on stage) and “Bass Persuades” into its remix. Hearing the new material live helps it snap into place within her catalog, cementing the album overall as a grungier, bassier big sister of Plastic Hearts. Miley followed the trio of Bass selects with “Handstand” off Endless Summer Vacation, saying: “You didn’t expect this one, did you?” But we should have — as the song, which she shares was the very first she ever wrote with her partner Maxx Morando, was basically breadcrumbing the more experimental sound she’s continued to explore.

paras.en: - Honoring Her Aunt Dolly: “Me and Dolly Are Eternal” As a photo of a young Dolly Parton fills the venues’ screens, the crowd softly chants “Miley, Miley” while her back remains to the crowd. Once she finally turns around, compact mirror in hand, she says, “She told me to check my make up,” before sitting on the edge of the stage. “So many reasons that I wanted to perform at the Hollywood Bowl,” she says with a shaky voice and her head down. “Above every single one of them is that I only got to see Dolly Parton live in concert one time in my entire life — and it was here.” Miley continues to share a story of how she wanted to go and enjoy, only to have the experience ruined by Dolly informing the crowd that she was seated among them (Dolly also insisted on entering her own show to the Hannah Montana hit “Best Of Both Worlds”). Despite the funny memory, Miley can’t help but tear up again as she says, “Me and Dolly are eternal,” adding that she feels her presence now more than ever. “I’m going to see her again and I can’t wait,” she continues, “because I fucking miss her.” Miley then performs “Jolene” as she has before. And to begin her next song ,“Walk Of Fame,” she fittingly flashes an image of Dolly’s Hollywood star. The song’s outro says it best: “You’ll live forever.” Just another thing Miley and her Aunt Dolly have in common.

paras.en: - Wayne Coyne’s Surprise Appearance Following another video interlude in which Miley talks about Woodstock as a reminder that “you can be lost and exactly where you need to be,” heads quickly turn toward a B-Stage in the center of the crowd where the one and only Wayne Coyne (of The Flaming Lips) is standing. He begins to sing the band’s hit “Do You Realize??” before being joined by Miley, who welcomes him with a big, long hug and then joins in on the final chorus. After it wraps, she says Coyne is “family” and shouts out Miley Cyrus & Her Dead Petz, which she calls “my favorite album that I’ve ever made.” Coyne sticks around for one more song, as the two dive into “Karen Don’t Be Sad” off that project. “I’m having so much fun,” says Miley as Coyne exits. “I didn’t know if I was gonna… you never know.”

paras.en: - Her Sentimental Moments (And Brief Reunion With Twerking) Dipping into her catalog got Miley feeling reflective again — she had already acknowledged early on how grateful she was to her fans for understanding her need for a balanced life that doesn’t include endless touring. Still speaking from the B-Stage, she shares that she has a new fish that Maxx named: “I have to have those things that give myself balance, she says. “Yeah, I was really excited to perform for you all at the Hollywood Bowl, but to be honest, I’m equally as excited about the new fish. And that’s what I love about my life, is I get both…I’m experiencing everything I’ve ever wanted.” She then says that “it’s been a long ride,” noting her near-20-years-long career “of this metamorphosis – and you have not skipped a beat. It’s been steadfast and deeply felt.” Then, surely and only as a gift to fans, Miley sang the first verse of “We Can’t Stop” before letting it play out — and even attempts to twerk along, saying “let’s see if I can still do it.” She still can, even in pants and blazer.

paras.en: - Her Emotional Walk Through the Crowd: “I Don’t Want My Mom to Worry” Instead of stealthily returning to the main stage, Miley instead takes an emotional walk through the crowd to get back. Once she does, she dives right into her emotional banger “Wrecking Ball,” which she sings while clutching a heart-shaped frame of Dolly. “That was Dolly’s favorite song of mine, so I had to bring her with me,” Miley says. Then, clearly still reeling from the up-close experience she just had with the crowd while walking through it, she offers insight into the emotional toll of such a seemingly simple act. “I’m ok, I don’t want my mom to worry,” she says, glancing side stage. “I do want to say, it is a lot for me… feeling how much passion and love you radiate to me, and I appreciate you so much.”

paras.en: - The Nostalgia-Fueled Backend: “Some Of My Old Ways” By this point, it’s clear we have reached the “Best Of” section of the set. Having heard “We Can’t Stop” and “Wrecking Ball,” Miley fittingly throws in the newer but heavily reflective “Used To Be Young” followed by “The Climb” and then “Party In the U.S.A.” During “Party,” the stage more or less becomes one with confetti and streamers and a final appearance from Coyne, who returns with a giant silver balloon sign that reads: “F–K YEAH HOLLYWOOD BOWL.” As Miley quips: “Some of my old ways.”

paras.en: - Giving the Bowl Its “Flowers” Ad-Lib For her two-song encore, Miley leads with “Let’s Get Married,” walking onstage holding hands with Morando. A portable drum kit has been moved center stage, at which he sits and plays while Miley lovingly sings beside him. After the song, as he returns to his proper kit a bit behind him, Miley declares: “This song is one of my personal favorites,” and delivers her mega hit “Flowers.” (The juxtaposition of the two back-to-back is especially representative of how much of Miley’s life has and continues to play out in public, from a messy divorce to finding love again.) “Flowers” live ad-libs have become a playful and expected bit, with the best to date having been at the 2024 Grammys when she sang through a wide smile: “Started to cry but then remembered… I just won my first Grammy!” Tonight, she updates the lyric to her latest achievement, beaming as she sings: “Started to cry but then remembered… I sold out the Hollywood Bowl!” And not just once, but twice. And not just because she wanted to, but because she crafted a show and its parameters around her own comfort and happiness. Not only can Miley buy her own flowers, but she can make her own rules, too. Just as she always has. And sure enough, the people will come. Just as we always have. articles.title: Becky G Brings World Mental Health Day Festival to a Powerful Close in NYC & More Uplifting Moments
articles.author: Isabela Raygoza

paras.en: From career milestones to new music releases to major announcements and those little important moments, Billboard editors highlight uplifting moments in Latin music. Here’s what happened in the Latin music world this week.
Becky G Opens Up About Identity and Mental Health at Project Healthy Minds Event

Becky G brought Project Healthy Minds’ World Mental Health Day Festival to a powerful close on Saturday (Oct. 10) in New York with an intimate conversation on identity, creativity and mental health. Moderated by NBC News correspondent Morgan Radford, the panel gave the Mexican American star space to reflect on growing up in the public eye, protecting her peace and learning to tell her story on her own terms.

“The whole concept of being a role model is to model this idea of perfection, and I don’t think that is real at all,” Becky G said. “Instead of being a role model, I’ve always felt the responsibility to be a real model, which means I’m not going to have all the answers. I’m not going to get it right every single time.”

She also spoke candidly about therapy, family and her healing journey, saying: “I had to become the person that I needed most, and that’s when Becky G came to be.” The conversation arrives just days before she is scheduled to join Billboard’s Latin Music Week for a Superstar Q&A this Wednesday (Oct. 21).
BMI Creates Space for Women Songwriters in Música Mexicana

“Música mexicana has historically been a male-dominated field, making it more important than ever to champion the women creatives who are shaping its future,” said Lilibeth Patron, BMI’s associate director of creative for Latin, in a statement. “Las Compositoras+ is about fostering community and creating space for connection and collaboration.”

Led by singer-songwriter Erika Vidrio, the camp began at the Fender offices before moving to a Bel Air house, where the participants spent several days developing new music together. Held in Los Angeles earlier this month and announced Sept. 30, the four-day retreat brought together Damaris Bojor, Lorena Cabral, Tania Dominguez, Poe Leos, MXKA, Marián Oviedo, Jacqie Rivera and Adriana Ríos to collaborate and write new songs for potential placements.
Lin-Manuel Miranda to Receive iHeartRadio’s Corazón Latino Award

Lin-Manuel Miranda will receive the 2026 iHeartRadio Corazón Latino Award during iHeartRadio Fiesta Latina on Saturday (Oct. 17) at Miami’s Kaseya Center. Hosted by Enrique Santos and Dayanara Torres, the concert event will feature performances by Anuel AA, Myke Towers, Farruko, Manuel Turizo, Eladio Carrión, FloyyMenor, Greeicy, Alleh and Rey Tony y Helabusador “Los Titi.”

The award recognizes Miranda’s lasting contributions to Latin music and culture, while the event will also bring together artists and presenters from across entertainment. A free kickoff party will take place Oct. 15 at Miami Design District, featuring Tony Succar’s “Unity: The Latin Tribute to Michael Jackson” with special guests including Anthony Ramos, Leslie Grace and Howie D of the Backstreet Boys. The main event will broadcast across iHeartRadio’s Latin stations nationwide.
Latin Recording Academy Announces 2026 Leading Ladies of Entertainment

The Latin Recording Academy announced its 2026 Leading Ladies of Entertainment honorees on Oct. 6, recognizing four women whose work has shaped Latin music and the broader entertainment industry: María Fernández, Sandra Jiménez, Salomé Limón and María Rosa García “Niña Pastori.”

The 10th anniversary class represents executive leadership, digital innovation, music production and artistry. Fernández is chief operating officer of Sony Music Entertainment Latin Iberia; Jiménez is YouTube’s regional director and head of music for Latin America and U.S. Latin; Limón is a five-time Latin Grammy-winning producer, composer and engineer; and Niña Pastori is a six-time Latin Grammy winner and Grammy nominee.

The honorees will be celebrated during Latin Grammy Week in Las Vegas, with Amazon Music returning as presenting sponsor for the third consecutive year. They will also be invited to mentor the next generation of women through the Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation’s Leading Ladies of Entertainment Mentorship Program.

articles.title: Patrick Brammall Is Poised to Join the Ranks of Australia’s Great Exports
articles.author: Mikey O'Connell

paras.en: The year arguably belongs to Anne Hathaway. But it’s been a pretty banner 10 months for a particular co-star from one of the actress’ five theatrical releases.

Patrick Brammall leveled up in 2026. After opening himself to his widest audience ever by playing the love interest to Hathaway’s Andy Sachs in the nearly $700-million grossing Devil sequel, he made a rare turn as a dramatic leading man in Apple TV+ thriller Last Seen. And, in September, he released the third and final season of Colin From Accounts — the romantic comedy he created with and starred alongside his wife, Harriet Dyer.

Colin From Accounts follows strangers Ashley (Dyer) and Gordon (Brammall) as they fall in love after share responsibility for a dog (the titular Colin) Gordon runs over with his car and leaves permanently handicapped. In a funny way. The Australian series was a success in the duo’s home country, a juggernaut in the U.K. and a sleeper hit in the United States. And the fact that its end coincides with an onslaught of other work is not lost on Brammall, whose career, with a few exceptions, has been largely defined by his work in the Southern Hemisphere. “I think we’ve all had a year, the same year, 2026,” he says, when I tally his credits, before surrendering and turning it into a bit. “Yeah, it was mine. You’ve all been having my year. It’s pretty mental, isn’t it?”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Brammall breaks into a few bits over our early October conversation, one where he covers the significance of Colin From Accounts, his daughter’s disinterest in the fact that he voices a character on Bluey and how he still has no idea what was really going on with his character on the bonkers Paramount+ supernatural drama Evil.

You’ve worked a lot in Australia and now a lot in the U.S. as well. I suspect that there are many aspects of television that are done differently. How, in you speaking to like studios and platforms, can you compare the response to pitching a show that starts with a dog getting hit by a car?

Australia and the U.K. didn’t have a problem with it. That’s funny. These two strangers meet at an intersection, she flashes her nipple, he gets distracted, he hits a dog. It’s hilarious. In America… not so hilarious. There’s even a website, doesthedogdie.com. So in when we were pitching it over here, we had to start with, “The dog’s fine and he’s very well cared for.” And you do meet his previous owner at the end of the first season. That guy was an asshole. Colin’s got a much happier life.
The show title obviously worked in the end, but it’s not the easiest sell. Many people assumed it was a workplace comedy. Was there ever any pushback on the name?

There was a bit of pushback. Because Colin from Accounts does not sound like what the show is. Our only alt title was Dog with Wheels, which wasn’t very good either. We liked the name because these two people, in that first episode of season one, what they connect about is naming the dog Colin from Accounts. They have a shared sense of humor. They’re plugged into the same frequency. That serves as their foundation. I think lot of people who found the show either were always going to watch it or just stumbled on it. They watch that first episode and they feel like they’re in on the joke. It does set the tone in many ways. On the other hand, terrible title.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: You and Harriet wrote every episode. Have you ever worked in a traditional writer’s room?

Only once — and even then it wasn’t that traditional. I did a show called No Activity for CBS All Access. We did the show in Australia first, and it was just Trent O’Donnell and myself. We created it, and it was largely improvised. We just had outlines. But for the U.S. version, the studio was like, “Hey, we love it! Write full scripts, please.” That’s not really the show, but they’re paying, so we did it. Trent and I ran a writer’s roombut were not very good at it. (Laughs.) People came in and I found it really inefficient. It was a fun time and you’d order lunch and you’d have your Le Croix, but I found it a very inefficient way to write something. Having said that, there were a lot of great ideas that came out of it. It was just so lumbering.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: So Colin From Accounts wraps up. You have this well-received dramatic turn in Last Seen. And you were in The Devil Wears Prada 2. It’s a real strong year for you. Have you noticed any previously closed doors opening up?

A couple of doors have opened, and it’s probably a result of the combination of the lot. I know Colin opened doors, because I wouldn’t have the offer for Prada because the writer (Aline Brosh McKenna) and director (David Frankel) were huge Colin fans. I don’t have people smashing the door down, but also that’s a little bit intentional. The last eighteen months have been so crazy. Our youngest is 20 months old. We’re just back in L.A., steadying the ship and just being a family for a minute.
I mean, you’re working in all of these different countries with children who are not at, shall we say, a fun age to travel with.

Dude, tell me about it. Just going back for Christmas to Australia is a siege. Recently, our eldest did something like six schools in eighteen months. She didn’t know where the fuck she was. So when we got back to L.A., it was like, let’s just stop for a minute.
Is is it easier for her to transition into a new school with the clout that her father voices a character on Bluey?

It would be if she accepted that I voiced a character on Bluey. She will not. I tried to tell her once, because I’m a sad man. I’m like, “Hey, do you recognize that voice? Is that dad?” And she just looked at me like, “Don’t ruin this for me.” Like, fuck off, mate. (Laughs.) She has a point. What am I doing trying to ruin Bluey for her? I’ll leave her to love Bluey for as long as she can before I ruin it for her.
I heard that when you sent in your audition tape for Last Seen, you had to have your hands tied to your to your body to keep you from gesticulating. Please explain.

My dear friend Kirsty McGregor, who cast last scene and was the casting director on Colin from Accounts, said “Hey, I’m working on this. I’ve put your name in the mix. They want to see a tape. This is the only tape that’s happening. So everyone’s gonna see it, so don’t fuck it up.” I put it down one morning, sent it off and, a couple of days later, she said, “Look, it’s great. I’ve got some notes. This isn’t Colin from Accounts. Stop gesticulating. Like, just be still. This needs to be a leading man. This is a thriller.” This is is some practical screen acting advice, which I haven’t had for 30 years. So, one Sunday morning, we’re out in the back office and Harriet filming. She’s wearing a dressing gown. I’m doing the thing and I’m trying to be good be still. She says, “Stop flapping your hands around!” Then she takes off the cord from her dressing gown and and ties my hands to my side. And that’s the tape that we sent. Everyone is like, “Fantastic! You’ve got the job.” And I thought, fuck, how can I do this job without a dressing gown cord?

paras.en: Semi spoilers for anybody who didn’t watch you in Evil, Michelle and Robert King’s Paramount+ drama, but at a certain point… I had no idea what the hell they were doing with your character.

I love this show, but your character is this absentee husband who pops in and out after climbing expeditions. You were never a series regular. And at some point, you’re just locked in some attic getting a sludge transfusion from your apparently satanist mother in law? Did they explain this to you?

That show is so good. And those last couple of seasons, I would just show show up with the script and go, “Well, what the fuck’s happening to me now?” It was such a fun job, because I was recurring, this husband character who comes in and out. So, periodically I would fly to New York and do two, maybe three episodes a season. And I was the absent partner and father of these five three girls? Four girls? There were a lot of girls. Initially, I was very invested in the character. Like, “What am I doing? What does this mean?” Eventually, I was like, “This show is fucking crazy.” It goes mental. I was kidnapped by Michael Emerson’s character. He and and Christine Lahti, they were putting something into me or taking blood out. I can’t remember! And then in the final season, I’m in a mental institution having an affair with Anna Chlumsky.

I really loved it. That show was underrated.

Just curious, now that Colin from Accounts is over, you employed your canine co-star, Zak, for years. Dogs can be a lot like child actors. Are you going to stay part of his life and make sure he doesn’t spiral?

I’ve done everything I can for that dog. Now I just have to let it go. You can only keep a dog out of rehab so many times before you say, “Go with God. It’s up to you now.” He’s off the rails, and he knows it. He’s on a collision course with something and it’s not good. No, Zak is one of the best boys. He was more professional than many of the humans there — so much so that Harriet sometimes we’d have to get like a bit of turkey on us so that looked like he was doing something. He was very comfortable in the wheelchair, but he’d just sit there.

articles.title: TikTok “Permanently Suspends” the ‘Musk’ Film Account, Raising Suppression Fears (Exclusive)
articles.author: Steven Zeitchik

paras.en: TikTok has banned the entire Musk film account, citing political content that violates its policies. The move, which comes just as the Alex Gibney’s investigation into Elon Musk expands to more than 470 screens across North America, raises concerns about Big Tech suppression that the very film seeks to expose.

Distributor Bleecker Street was informed Friday afternoon a “permanent suspension” was coming. The entire page disappeared from TikTok’s platform shortly after. The film company had been planning to spend ad money to boost certain posts; that will no longer happen.

A spokesperson for the distributor confirmed that TikTok reps had informed them of the suspension and noted “disappointment” in the timing. After grossing $70,000 in four theaters in New York and Los Angeles in its first weekend of release, Musk is now playing in dozens of cities this weekend. The spokesperson said the company is in the process of appealing the move; even a reversal, however, could still prove costly if it doesn’t come during a weekend window when many people are likely to see the film.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: A TikTok representative did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Musk goes deep on a number of its subject’s actions and companies, which Gibney spent more than three years investigating. The film devotes a large portion of its second half focusing on Musk’s political activities with DOGE and beyond. It also centers on his acquisition of Twitter, which Gibney suggests was done to control the digital public square, adding an element of potency and irony to the TikTok move.
An official message from the company to Bleecker Street noted a “level of severity with political-policy violations” and said that “some violations trigger immediate suspension.”

It was unclear, however, what those violations were. Bleecker Street had just posted two new pieces of content before the suspension came. In one, a cheeky ad about what to do during intermission of the nearly four-hour doc, on-screen text suggested deleting your X account, “chat about a fascist hellscape” and “”switch your seats if they are too far to the right.”
A second post suggested seeing the movie “before it gets shut down,” adding a further element of irony to the social ban.
The Musk TikTok account account has garnered more than 10,000 followers since going live, an uncommonly high number for an individual documentary.

TikTok has no official affiliation with Elon Musk, though it is partly owned by Larry Ellison, who gets a rough moment in the doc when a text from him offering to pay billions to the mogul to help finance his Twitter acquisition is shown. TikTok has been more resistant to Musk content than some of its competitors, refusing to reverse its position again accepting an ad for the trailer even after Meta and Google/YouTube did just that. X, of course, been unwilling to accept any advertising for the film.
